NuRD co-occupancy at 628 of the sites (22.6%) was reduced in the absence of HNF-1{beta}. Of the 628 HNF-1{beta}-dependent NuRD-occupied sites, 113 sites (18.2%) showed higher ATAC-seq peaks, indicative of open chromatin, and enrichment of histone H3 lysine-27 (H3K27) acetylation, indicative of active enhancers, in wild-type cells compared to HNF-1{beta}-deficient cells. Correlation with transcriptomic profiles in wild-type and HNF-1{beta}-deficient cells revealed that most of the sites were located near genes that are activated by HNF-1{beta}. Knockdown of CHD4 with shRNA resulted in decreased expression of 67 HNF-1{beta}-regulated genes that contained nearby NuRD and HNF-1{beta} co-occupied sites. Collectively, these results demonstrate that HNF-1{beta} recruits the NuRD complex resulting in H3K27 acetylation and chromatin opening and leading to gene activation. Our findings reveal a new mechanism of HNF-1{beta}-dependent gene expression and expand the role of the NuRD complex in gene activation at distal enhancers.
affiliations: Division of Nephrology and Hypertension, Department of Medicine, Renaissance School of Medicine, Stony Brook University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Excluded Volume Effect-induced Shrinkage for Resolution Enhancement of Hydrogel Bioconstructs
papers.abstract: Biofabrication of hydrogel materials is usually constrained by process-specific resolution limits. Here, we introduce excluded volume effect-induced shrinkage (EVER), a dehydration-enabled resolution enhancement strategy that achieves dimensional refinement via post-processing. In this approach, we treat biofabricated constructs with hydrophilic macromolecular crowding agent bath, with poloxamer as a representative. With EVER treatment, gelatin-based constructs can reach a dimension reduction of up to ~49% with an estimated volumetric reduction of ~87%. Shape fidelity was well retained after shrinkage across different constructs and could be stabilized by introducing secondary crosslinking. In extrusion bioprinted cell-laden constructs, myoblasts retained a considerable cell viability right after the shrinkage treatment and recovered significantly by day 1, with subsequent cell spreading and increasing proliferation over 7 days. Without the need of continued immersion in the shrinkage bath, EVER provides a hardware-independent route for refining hydrogel structures while retaining encapsulated cell compatibility.
affiliations: Tsinghua University (corresponding author)

papers.title: MPFIL: Multi-Level Protein Feature Integration for Predicting Mutation-Induced Protein-Protein Binding Affinity Changes
papers.abstract: Predicting mutation-induced changes in protein protein binding affinity ({triangleup}{triangleup}G) is challenging because mutations can affect both local residue environments and the structural organization of protein complexes. Existing approaches often rely on handcrafted physicochemical, energetic, or evolutionary features, which introduce additional computational costs and require domain-specific knowledge. In this work, we propose MPFIL, a multi-level protein feature integration framework for predicting mutation-induced protein-protein binding affin ity changes. MPFIL integrates structural and sequential infor mation to characterize mutation effects from complementary perspectives. Its structural feature extraction module captures mutation-induced structural changes and differential information between wild-type and mutant complexes, while sequence feature extraction modules model local residue context and long-range dependencies. The resulting features are integrated for {triangleup}{triangleup}G prediction. We evaluate MPFIL on three benchmark datasets. Experimental results demonstrate competitive and consistent performance across different protein complex settings, while ablation studies verify the contribution of the structural and sequential features. These results support the effectiveness of multi-level protein feature integration for modeling mutation induced changes in protein-protein binding affinity.
affiliations: Harbin Institute Of Technology (corresponding author)

papers.title: NMR-measured Per-residue Electrostatic Potentials Reveal the Importance of Arginine-Lysine Balance on the Conformational Ensemble of Disordered Histone H3 Tails in Nucleosome Core Particles
papers.abstract: Biophysical studies of chromatin have provided key insights into how the genome is regulated. Many atomic resolution structures of the fundamental building block of chromatin, the nucleosome core particle (NCP), as well as larger NCP arrays, both in isolation and in complex with effectors, or with post-translational modifications, have been elucidated. These provide in-depth pictures of key functional interactions. Considerably less information is available on the intrinsically disordered nucleosome tails that are critically important for higher order interactions in chromatin, and for transcription, DNA repair, and phase separation, and that serve as hubs for post-translational modifications. Here we focus on the tail of one of the four histones, histone-3 (H3), and measure electrostatic potentials at each of its amide proton positions in isolated NCPs via solution NMR spectroscopy. Using these potentials, in concert with molecular dynamics simulations, an ensemble of structures is calculated for WT H3 tails, as well as variants where all tail arginines are replaced by lysines (R2K) or vice versa (K2R). Our ensembles reveal that K2R tails have a higher propensity to occupy the most negatively charged region of the NCP between the DNA gyres than R2K or WT tails, while lysine enriched tails have an increased relative preference for the less negative regions near the DNA entry and exit points. The structural ensembles provide insight into differences in interactions between neighboring particles that lead to changes in diffusion and phase separation propensities between the NCP variants.
affiliations: University of Toronto (corresponding author)

papers.title: Cancer cells acquire cysteine directly from a reduced tumor microenvironment
papers.abstract: The metabolic environment of a tumor is shaped by the nutrients available in its interstitial fluid, yet the redox composition of that fluid is poorly defined. Measuring sulfur metabolites in the interstitial fluid of tumors, matched healthy organs, and serum across three mouse models of cancer, we find that the tumor microenvironment (TME) is a chemically reduced compartment in which free cysteine predominates over its oxidized form, cystine. This is especially pronounced in the lung TME, where cystine is nearly absent. We further show that lung cancer cells take up cysteine and cystine with comparable efficiency and proliferate on cysteine alone, and that the abundant glutathione in the TME helps keep cysteine reduced through disulfide exchange. In a medium formulated to match the sulfur composition of the lung tumor interstitial fluid, cells become independent of cystine import through xCT. Cells cultured in this medium were resistant to glutaminase inhibitors, oxidants and ferroptosis inducers, and better maintained NADPH levels under oxidative challenge. These findings suggest that standard culture conditions overestimate the dependence of cancer cells on cystine uptake and their vulnerability to oxidative stress-targeting therapies.
affiliations: H. Lee Moffitt Cancer Center (corresponding author)

papers.title: Fine-tuning an intracellular allosteric pocket programs GPCR signaling bias
papers.abstract: Biased signaling of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers a route for precise therapeutics with fewer adverse effects. Intracellular allosteric ligands can impose such bias, yet how subtle chemical changes within these pockets reshape receptor-transducer coupling and downstream signaling remains unclear. Here, we systematically fine-tuned the intracellular allosteric pocket of neurotensin receptor 1 (NTSR1) through chemical modification of the {beta}-arrestin-biased ligand SBI-553. Minor changes to the ligand scaffold altered transducer-coupling preferences, generating distinct profiles of G-protein and {beta}-arrestin signaling. Cryo-electron microscopy structures of NTSR1-{beta}-arrestin2 complexes bound to designed allosteric probes revealed ligand-dependent remodeling of the intracellular cavity that reshapes the receptor-effector interface. Alanine scanning identified transducer-sensitive residues within and beyond the immediate ligand-contact region. In mice, SBI-553 and N065 produced distinct physiological profiles, with N065 improving survival in a lethal endotoxemia model. Finally, phosphoproteomic profiling revealed partially overlapping but distinct downstream signaling profiles among the three modulators. Together, these findings establish the intracellular allosteric pocket as a tunable determinant of transducer coupling and show that closely related modulators can generate distinct signaling and physiological profiles.
affiliations: School of Medicine, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Modulation of planarian seizure-like activity via antiseizure medications
papers.abstract: Acute chemical exposure to organophosphorus compounds (OPs) arising from terrorist attacks or accidental poisonings pose a serious threat to human health. Acetylcholinesterase inhibition due to acute OP exposure causes a cholinergic crisis, manifested as increased secretions, respiratory distress, loss of consciousness, seizures, and ultimately death if left untreated. Benzodiazepines, such as midazolam, are currently used to stop OP-induced seizures, but must be administered within minutes after exposure to be effective. This makes midazolam impractical for large-scale civilian emergencies. Thus, there is a need to identify novel antiseizure medications (ASMs) that are equally effective even when administered later. It has been challenging to identify such compounds with traditional mammalian testing; high throughput screening assays that can quickly and cost-effectively evaluate many candidates for their potential as an ASM are needed. Planarians are aquatic invertebrates that are suitable organismal models for OP neurotoxicity studies due to the conservation of OP targets and their ability to metabolize OPs. Here, we built on our prior work that introduced a computational image analysis pipeline to quantify planarian seizure-like activity (pSLA) in two planarian species (Dugesia japonica and Girardia dorotocephala). We previously used this approach to characterize pSLA following acute exposure (up to 30 minutes) to seizurogenic compounds. In the present study, we asked whether pSLA induced by the OP pesticide parathion, pentylenetetrazole, or NMDA could be rescued by co-exposure to four ASMs: midazolam, topiramate, MK-801, and carbamazepine. All tested ASMs were effective at reducing parathion-induced pSLA in one planarian species. However, ASM responses varied substantially across proconvulsants and planarian species. Defining the molecular mechanisms underlying pSLA will be essential for establishing planarians as a reliable model for ASM discovery.
affiliations: Swarthmore College (corresponding author)

papers.title: Human prion proteins and mutants through the lens of systems biology
papers.abstract: Autocatalytic conformational changes of cellular prion proteins (PrPC) to the {beta}-sheet-enriched scrapie isoform (PrPSC) drive prion diseases, yet the precise molecular mechanisms remain unclear. To address this, we employ a multi-pronged framework integrating network-theoretic analyses, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and experimental validation to characterize critical residues governing human PrP (huPrP) structural integrity. Residue Interaction Networks (RINs) of: (A) wild-type (WT) huPrP, and, (B) five disease-associated point mutants (Met166Val, Glu220Lys, Glu200Lys, Asp178Asn, and Ser170Asn) were evaluated using three rigorous network methods: centrality measures, Shortest Path Alteration Fraction (SPAF), and Differential Networks (DN). Across all the diverse point mutations, five residues (Met206, Val209, Val210, Met213, and Cys214) consistently exhibit high centrality scores. SPAF and DN analyses demonstrate that alterations at these positions disrupt connectivity and increase the propensity for misfolding and protease resistance. To validate these topological findings, key residues within the C-terminal domain (121-230) were substituted via site-directed mutagenesis. Thermal denaturation monitored by circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy reveals that the Met213Ala substitution significantly lowers the melting temperature, Tm, relative to the WT, whereas the Val210Ala variant unfolds with a Tm comparable to the WT. Furthermore, MD simulations of de novo AlphaFold-predicted mutant structures corroborate these findings. Mutants exhibit greater structural flexibility and deviation, with average root Mean Square Deviations rising from 0.18 nm (WT) to 0.32 nm (Cys214Ala), 0.29 nm (Met206Ala), and 0.25 nm (Val210Lys). This integration of theoretical and experimental techniques provides a robust framework for identifying critical determinants of protein stability.
affiliations: Bose Institute, Kolkata (corresponding author)

papers.title: Wasting is essential: cachexia is driven by a wound-healing adaptation
papers.abstract: Background: Several explanations have been given for why cachexia occurs in the presence of severe acute wounds and chronic diseases. None of these explanations address the scope of clinical settings in which cachexia has been observed, nor do they account for the failure of nutritional support to reverse cachexia. We hypothesize that induced muscle wasting (IMW) is an adaptation to support wound healing, and when a wound does not heal, prolonged IMW leads to cachexia. Methods: To evaluate this hypothesis, we developed a mathematical model of IMW. In this model, we compared the time needed for wound healing when IMW was present and when it was inhibited. We also measured the relationship between the pathogen growth rate and final patient muscle mass for chronic diseases such as cancer and tuberculosis, demonstrating the onset of cachexia. Finally, we simulated the effects of nutritional support and contrasted the outcomes of when IMW was present and when it was inhibited. Results: Acute wound healing was ~2-6 times longer without IMW than with IMW. For chronic wounds, steady-state muscle mass strongly depended on the growth rate of the pathogenic agent. Inhibiting IMW was more effective at preventing acute muscle mass loss than nutritional support, and the benefit of nutritional support was enhanced by inhibiting IMW. Nutritional support also increased the speed of healing acute wounds when IMW was inhibited. For cancer with high growth rate, giving nutritional support alone had a negligible effect on steady-state muscle mass. But when IMW was inhibited, muscle mass loss was attenuated. With IMW inhibition, nutritional support with the normal diet was able to abrogate muscle mass loss entirely. Conclusions: Inhibiting IMW slows the healing of acute wounds, supporting our hypothesis that IMW is an adaptation to support rapid wound healing. Our experiments demonstrate that nutritional support is insufficient to prevent severe muscle mass loss while IMW continues. But when IMW is inhibited, nutritional support restores normal levels of muscle mass for both acute and chronic wounds, as well as increasing the rate of wound healing. Discovering and developing methods to inhibit IMW for clinical use will be essential to restore patient muscle mass, ease suffering, and reduce mortality.
affiliations: Moffitt Cancer Center (corresponding author)

papers.title: Disease-associated NK-cell state remodeling reveals transcriptional profiles predictive of clinical phenotypes
papers.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells adapt their cellular states to diverse tissue and inflammatory environments, yet how this plasticity manifests across pathological contexts and relates to patient-level disease phenotypes remains poorly defined. Here we established the Human NK-cell Atlas (HNKA) from over 1 million NK cells, including samples from 1,632 donors spanning 50 diseases. Within a shared NK-cell state architecture, analyses of state abundance and matched-reference exceedance distinguished disease-biased redistribution from transcriptional displacement. Fine-grained analyses localized disease-associated remodeling to specific NK-cell states, including CD56dim NK ISG15 in infection and autoimmunity and CD56bright NK ITM2C in tumors. These patterns were accompanied by recurrent interferon responses and state-specific regulatory activity. Cytokine perturbations recapitulated key transcriptional features of disease-associated NK-cell states. We developed NKceiver, a model based on state-specific NK-cell expression profiles for patient-level prediction. It distinguished 18 diseases and predicted COVID-19 severity and response to immune checkpoint inhibitors, with predictive performance retained in unseen patients and studies. Collectively, our results reveal that disease-associated remodeling within the diverse NK-cell state repertoire resolved by HNKA is biologically interpretable and clinically informative, supporting disease discrimination and prediction of clinical phenotypes.
affiliations: Department of Biomedical Informatics, School of Basic Medical Sciences, Peking University, 38 Xueyuan Road, Beijing 100191, China; State Key Laboratory of Vascu (corresponding author)

papers.title: Ribosome-Associated GTPase Drg1 Links Cytosolic Translation to Mitochondrial Homeostasis
papers.abstract: Coordination of the functionalities among key organelles is essential for maintaining the complexity and adaptability of the eukaryotic cell. Functionally versatile proteins, such as GTPases, often assume important roles in this process. A ribosome-binding GTPase called Developmentally-regulated GTP-binding (Drg) protein is a conserved family of GTPases that promotes protein synthesis and regulates cytoskeletal dynamics, suggesting their importance for cell growth and proliferation. Mitochondrial proteostasis requires coordination between cytosolic translation and the targeting, import, and assembly of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins. However, the ribosome-associated factors that support this coordination remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify the conserved GTPase Drg1, one of the two Drg paralogues in eukaryotic cells, as a translation factor required for mitochondrial homeostasis and cellular fitness. Human Drg1 and its cofactor Dfrp1 are associated with translating ribosomes and co-sedimented with polysomes. Deletion of Drg1 in HEK293T cells caused altered mitochondrial architecture, reduced mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP production, and impaired expression of a mitochondrially targeted reporter. Re-expression of wild-type Drg1 restored ATP production and reporter expression, whereas a GTPase-deficient Drg1 mutant failed to provide comparable rescue in ATP production, demonstrating that Drg1 catalytic activity is required for its cellular function. Mitochondria-directed APEX2 proximity proteomics further connected Drg1-dependent translation to proteins involved in mitochondrial protein import, respiratory-chain function, and mitochondrial protein synthesis. Reporter analyses indicated that Drg1 loss preferentially compromises productive translation toward the 3' region of the coding sequence. Together, these findings establish Drg1 as a ribosome-associated translation factor that supports the synthesis and homeostasis of proteins required for mitochondrial function. At the molecular level, loss of cellular homeostasis that is caused by compromised translation of cytoplasmically synthesized proteins functionally related to mitochondria underpins the observed phenomenon. Our results reveal a previously underappreciated connection between the cytosolic translation machinery and mitochondrial maintenance and provide a framework for understanding how defects in a conserved translational GTPase impair cellular energy metabolism and physiology.
affiliations: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign (corresponding author)

papers.title: A Cell-Autonomous Cold Sensor Promotes Lipolysis Through Phase Separation
papers.abstract: Temperature is a fundamental determinant of mammalian metabolism. The canonical cold-adaptation pathway involves cold sensing by peripheral sensory neurons, which activate sympathetic outflow, {beta}-adrenergic signaling, and lipolysis in adipose tissue. In contrast, we report here a cell-intrinsic mechanism by which physiologically relevant cooling temperatures (27-31 oC) enhance lipolysis in subcutaneous adipose tissue. Mechanistically, cooling drives liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of perilipin 1 (PLIN1), the dominant lipid droplet coat protein, promoting its condensation and the local recruitment of PKA to the droplet surface. This spatial reorganization selectively amplified PKA-mediated perilipin 1 phosphorylation, CGI-58 release, and ATGL-dependent lipolysis. The process depends on the intrinsically disordered region (IDR) of perilipin1, where four aromatic residues, conserved in endotherms but not in ectotherms, are required for cooling-induced LLPS and lipolysis in vivo. Notably, targeted delivery of an LLPS-competent perilipin 1 variant to the inguinal adipose tissue of mice enhanced local lipolysis and reduced depot mass. Together, these findings uncover a cell-intrinsic thermosensitive mechanism that can tune lipolytic responsiveness, offering a possible strategy for targeted depot-selective fat reduction.
affiliations: BIDMC (corresponding author)

papers.title: Rapid early degradation of Cyclin A is important to maintain genomic stability
papers.abstract: The Anaphase Promoting Complex/Cyclosome (APC/C) ubiquitin ligase controls mitosis by targeting the mitotic Cyclins for degradation. At Nuclear Envelope Breakdown the APC/C immediately targets CyclinA but the Spindle Assembly Checkpoint prevents it recognising CyclinB until all chromosomes have attached to the mitotic apparatus. The degradation of CyclinA before CyclinB is conserved in evolution but the physiological role of this is not yet clearly established. Overexpressing CyclinA or a non-degradable mutant interferes with chromosome congression and promotes microtubule instability, but the effect of delaying the degradation of endogenous CyclinA has not been determined. Here, we mutated two APC/C-recognition motifs in human CyclinA2 to slow down its degradation. We find that slower degradation of CyclinA alters microtubule dynamics and induces errors in chromosome congression and chromosome clustering at mitotic exit, leading to aneuploidy and malformed daughter cell nuclei. We identify Ki67 as the candidate to interfere with chromosome clustering since its phosphorylation and behaviour are perturbed when CyclinA is degraded more slowly. We conclude that rapid early CyclinA degradation is important for genomic stability.
affiliations: The Institute of Cancer Research (corresponding author)

papers.title: Chromosome-level Atlantic switchgrass assemblies reveal a supernumerary B-Chromosome with transcriptional and evolutionary impacts
papers.abstract: Supernumerary B-Chromosomes are extra genetic elements that frequently deviate from Mendelian inheritance to ensure their own survival. Their evolutionary origins and biological impacts within natural plant populations remain largely unexplored. Switchgrass (Panicum virgatum) is a model for studies of local adaptation, but reliance on a single reference genome has limited the detection of lineage-specific genomic content. We generated chromosome-level genome assemblies from the diverged Atlantic switchgrass subpopulation and discovered a previously undetected genomic element: a ~34 Mb supernumerary B-Chromosome, validated by Hi-C contact mapping and long-read depth, which indicates two to four B copies per nucleus. The B-Chromosome has a bipartite architecture including a gene-rich, single-copy proximal region (~8 Mb) and a repeat-rich, gene-poor distal region (~27 Mb) dominated by LTR/Ty3 (Gypsy) elements and punctuated by Mutator TIR peaks. High-resolution mapping reveals a highly rearranged chimera of fragments from multiple autosomes, biased toward the N-subgenome. Intact LTR retrotransposons on the B-Chromosome are younger than those on the A-Chromosomes, especially in its distal region, consistent with a B-Chromosome that arose and expanded within the Atlantic lineage. Population screening and phylogenetic analysis indicate that the B-Chromosome is largely restricted to the Atlantic subpopulation and likely has a single origin. In a typical family, 70% of open-pollinated progeny of B-positive maternal plants were B-positive, with substantial variation among families. Finally, B-Chromosome presence is associated with expression differences in A-Chromosome genes that differ between genetic backgrounds. Together, our results show how accessory chromosomes contribute to the evolutionary and genomic diversity of natural plant populations.
affiliations: Department of Integrative Biology, The University of Texas at Austin, Austin, TX 78712, USA (corresponding author)

papers.title: CATFISHR: integration of transcriptome and inferred CNV profiles for comprehensive malignant cell identification
papers.abstract: Malignant cell identification in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) remains challenging because transcriptomic cell typing, somatic variant detection and inferred copy-number approaches each have modality-specific limitations. Rare or ambiguous malignant populations are especially vulnerable to misclassification or exclusion, despite their relevance to treatment resistance, minimal residual disease, and metastasis. We developed CATFISHR, a semi-automated workflow that integrates RNA-expression similarity, inferred copy-number variation (CNV) profiles, and consensus cell typing to classify malignant cells relative to high-confidence references. CATFISHR was evaluated across eight cohorts, including seven scRNA-seq datasets spanning multiple carcinomas and melanoma subtypes, and one 10x Visium spatial transcriptomics sample. Compared with available benchmarks or ground truths, CATFISHR achieved balanced accuracy > 0.85 in six of eight cohorts and F1 score > 0.80 in six of eight cohorts. Cells uniquely identified by CATFISHR as malignant ("Hidden" cells) were present in every dataset and were not consistently explained by standard quality-control metrics. In several cohorts, Hidden cells were transcriptionally closer to benchmark malignant than non-malignant compartments; in Visium data, sampled Hidden spots contained histologist-confirmed morphologically malignant cells. CATFISHR reduces missed malignant calls while preserving rare, transitional and benchmark-discordant populations for downstream investigation.
affiliations: NEXUS Personalized Health Technologies, ETH Zurich (corresponding author)

papers.title: An ITK - SLP-76 Y173 Axis Regulates TCR Signal Persistence and Thymic Development
papers.abstract: The TCR-induced tyrosine kinase cascade results in ITK-mediated phosphorylation of at least two substrates: PLC-{gamma}1 Y783, an essential mediator of TCR signaling, and SLP-76 Y173. We previously provided evidence that SLP-76 Y173 supports proximal TCR and Fc{varepsilon}RI signaling; but its role in thymocyte development was never explored. Here we demonstrate that SLP-76 Y173 was required for TCR/CD28-induced degradation of I{kappa}B; moreover, both ITK and SLP-76 Y173 were required for persistent TCR-induced phosphorylation of PLC-{gamma}1, ERK and p38. To explore whether SLP-76 Y173 may mediate ITK-dependent events in vivo, we replaced SLP 76 Y173 with phenylalanine in a mouse model. Like ITK-deficient thymocytes, SLP-76 Y173F thymocytes exhibited reduced thymic cellularity, reduced CD4/CD8 ratios, and reduced surface expression of CD5. In ex vivo-stimulated thymocytes, mutation of SLP-76 Y173 or inhibition of ITK reduced the persistence of TCR-induced calcium flux; moreover, TCR-induced phosphorylation of ERK and p38 depended on SLP-76 Y173. Like ITK-deficient thymi, SLP-76 Y173F thymocytes exhibited decreased production of CD4- iNKT1 thymocytes, coupled with increased production of innate-like CD4+ and CD8+ SP thymocytes. Our results provide strong evidence that the ITK substrate site, SLP-76 Y173, promotes TCR signal persistence that is required to mediate the thymic developmental effects of ITK.

papers.title: Stimulation strategy matters: A B-cell focused single-cell transcriptomic study on in vitro stimulated immune cells
papers.abstract: Distinct in vitro B-cell stimulation strategies, defined by stimulation condition and incubation duration, have been described in diverse studies. Often, these approaches are considered interchangeable due to comparable flow-cytometric outputs concerning fluorescence intensities and B-cell subset distributions. However, whether these phenotypic similarities also reflect comparable underlying transcriptional states have not been systematically evaluated yet. In this study, we provide an unbiased comparison of B-cell activation strategies on healthy individuals, resulting in a single-cell transcriptomic atlas (4 donors; ~2,029 cells per sample; 81,160 cells in total with 56.3% annotated as B cells). Two T-cell independent stimulators targeting toll-like receptors (ODN2006 and IFN-{gamma}/R-848), were assessed next to two T-cell dependent stimulators (anti-CD40 and anti-CD3/CD28 antibodies), all incubated for eight and 30 hours. Observed overlap for differential abundance, differential gene expression and cell-cell interactions could directly be linked to T-cell (in)dependent working mechanism. Strategy-specific results uncovered time-point specific transcriptional changes, revealed the largest set of differentially expressed genes for IFN-{gamma}/R-848 and ODN2006, and showed that IFN-{gamma}/R-848 and anti-CD3/CD28 induced the majority of the cell-cell interactions. Ultimately, our reference atlas emphasizes the importance and facilitates the rational selection of optimal B-cell stimulation strategies, particularly for studies aiming to interrogate B-cell dysregulation in immune-mediated diseases.

papers.title: Modeling of human MLH1 and MLH3 variants in mice reveals novel functions of MutLγ in meiotic DNA repair and the ovarian reserve
papers.abstract: The mismatch repair proteins MLH1 and MLH3 form the MutL{gamma} complex that is essential for >90% of meiotic crossovers (CO) in mice. Although deletion of either gene causes infertility, we previously found that mouse models of certain human MLH1/3 missense variants caused elevated aneuploidy and progressive loss of female fecundity despite having a normal ovarian reserve. Here, we report that additional missense and null alleles caused significant pre-pubertal follicle loss independent of alterations to meiotic CO levels. Deletion of the DNA damage checkpoint kinase Chek2 (Chk2) partially rescued the oocyte pool of Mlh1- and Mlh3-deficient mice, indicating that defects in meiotic prophase I triggered oocyte elimination. In spermatocytes, both missense and null alleles caused abnormal {gamma}H2AX flares on autosomes during late pachynema and diplonema, extending into chromatin loops from the synaptonemal complex. These flares frequently contained unusually large foci of the ssDNA binding protein RPA as well as DNA end processing factors including CtIP, RAD50 and BLM, consistent with abnormal and extensive DNA resection. The results reveal a previously unrecognized meiotic function of MutL{gamma} in preventing DNA hyper-resection of spontaneous DNA breaks or of persistent recombination intermediates in late prophase I. Together with our previous studies, the results show that MLH1/3 variants can impair fertility through at least three mechanistically distinct routes: severe crossover loss sufficient to activate the metaphase I spindle assembly checkpoint; subthreshold crossover defects that increase aneuploidy and embryo loss; and abnormal late-prophase DNA processing that activates a CHEK2-dependent oocyte quality-control pathway and depletes the ovarian reserve, causing primary ovarian insufficiency (POI). Thus, MutL{gamma} has broader roles in maintaining meiotic genome integrity than can be explained by crossover formation alone.

papers.title: Metric-driven Pre-acquisition Diagnostics for Automated Microscopy Ultraviolet Surface Excitation (MUSE)
papers.abstract: Background Automated microscopy enables large-scale tiled imaging but remains sensitive to variations in alignment, illumination, focus, and sample coverage that may only be detected after acquisition. We present an adaptive pre-acquisition quality-control framework for microscopy ultraviolet surface excitation (MUSE) that uses sparse scout imaging and tile-level metrics to guide acquisition and selective rescanning. Methods The framework quantifies brightness, dynamic range, focus, tissue fraction, and exposure error across the field of view. For example, in a representative 10 x 10 acquisition (100 tiles, 20-megapixel imagery), the mean p99 brightness was 0.525 (CV 10.4%), the mean dynamic range was 0.331, the median focus score was 0.0333, and the median tissue fraction was 0.943. Furthermore, applying a conservative exposure-error threshold (|error| > 0.25) identified 25% of tiles as rescan candidates. Results These results show that compact tile-level metrics can be converted into actionable quality gates, enabling early detection of local acquisition errors and targeted rescanning to improve mosaic consistency while minimizing unnecessary acquisition.

papers.title: ProtCell: a foundation model for single-cell proteomics
papers.abstract: Single-cell proteomics provides a direct functional readout of cellular states, but targeted assays measure limited and non-identical protein panels, fragmenting information across experiments. Here, we present ProtCell, a foundation model developed using approximately 380 million cells from 98 datasets for pretraining and evaluation. ProtCell combines protein-identity and continuous-abundance embeddings in a transformer encoder and learns cell- and protein-level representations through masked abundance modeling. ProtCell first connects fragmented profiles through transferable annotation and batch correction while preserving biological organization. It then extends limited profiles through abundance reconstruction and inference of an unmeasured cytotoxic protein program enriched in natural killer cells and memory CD8$^+$ T cells. The learned protein dependencies further guide the selection of compact panels that retain information for profile reconstruction and biological classification. ProtCell thus provides a framework for connecting fragmented proteomic profiles, extending information beyond measured panels and guiding more informative measurements.

papers.title: How Much Can AI Virtual Cells Gain from Unified Perturbational Modeling?
papers.abstract: Predicting how individual cells respond to perturbations is a central task in artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC) modeling. However, integrating perturbation datasets is challenging because they differ in measured gene sets, perturbation types and cellular contexts. Existing AIVC predictors are typically developed for specific settings, limiting their applicability across heterogeneous datasets. Here, we investigate the extent to which AIVC predictors can benefit from unified perturbational modeling (UPM), a novel paradigm designed to integrate heterogeneous Perturb-seq datasets into a single predictive model. To this end, we introduce three unification modules into a variational autoencoder (VAE)-based AIVC predictor to address these sources of heterogeneity: gene-channel alignment, shared perturbation encoding, and joint embedding of gene expression and identity. We systematically evaluate and validate the individual contributions of these modules. Building on UPM, we assemble a dataset of 110 million cells spanning over 22,000 genes, four perturbation types and 76 cellular contexts, and use 89.7 million cells from 71 contexts to train a unified AIVC predictor with more than one billion parameters. Across genetic perturbation benchmarks, UPM achieves the highest PES and gene-wise response correlation among the evaluated models. It also improves all four evaluation metrics over State on the five held-out Tahoe-100M cell lines and over Stack on the cytokine benchmark. UPM also improves combinatorial perturbation prediction relative to specialized predictors. In the HSC application, our model achieves a 40.0% improvement in accuracy on a downstream task involving the recapitulation of effects induced by the knockdown of hepatic stellate cell (HSC)-related targets. Our implementation is openly available at https://github.com/youlab2025/UPM.

papers.title: Astatine-211 injury induces an immunostimulatory melanoma-cell state and promotes systemic antitumor immunity
papers.abstract: Targeted alpha therapy is generally evaluated by absorbed dose and direct tumor-cell killing, but whether alpha-particle-injured tumor cells can induce systemic antitumor immunity remains poorly defined. We investigated the immunogenic consequences of astatine-211 (211At) injury in a prophylactic melanoma vaccination-challenge model. B16F10 cells were exposed ex vivo to 211At, etoposide, or ultraviolet irradiation under conditions that reduced viable-cell counts at 24 hours to approximately 40% of untreated controls. Injured cells were administered subcutaneously to syngeneic C57BL/6J mice before intravenous challenge with viable B16F10 cells. Vaccination with cells exposed to 1 MBq/mL 211At suppressed pulmonary metastasis, reduced regulatory T-cell proportions, and elicited tumor-reactive interferon-{gamma} responses and antibodies. Transcriptomic profiling revealed enrichment of type I interferon, inflammatory, and chemokine-related signatures, together with suppression of cell-cycle, translation, and metabolic programs. At the cellular level, 211At injury was accompanied by {gamma}H2AX accumulation, G2/M arrest, increased reactive oxygen species and cytosolic double-stranded DNA, and senescence-like changes. These features arose without consistent increases in classical damage-associated molecular patterns or prominent induction of senescence-associated secretory phenotype factors at 1 MBq/mL. In vivo pharmacologic inhibition of stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling attenuated the antimetastatic effect of vaccination. Together, these findings demonstrate that 211At injury can generate an immunostimulatory tumor-cell state characterized by DNA damage and altered inflammatory signaling. STING contributes to the resulting immune protection, highlighting immunogenic tumor-cell conversion as a consideration in the design of targeted alpha therapies.
affiliations: The University of Osaka (corresponding author)

papers.title: BenchMHC: a reproducible framework for peptide-MHC presentation prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting which peptides an MHC molecule presents is the first step in neoantigen and epitope discovery pipelines. Most published predictors are released for inference only, and each is trained on a different dataset, so the effect of a new method cannot be separated from the effect of its training data. We present BenchMHC, an open framework that reproduces, retrains and evaluates pMHC presentation models on public data only, and that records every implementation decision made in a reproduction. Our NetMHCpan-4.1 reproduction reaches 0.794 per-allele Mean Top-K against 0.790 for the official webserver, and 0.0025 Median FRANK against 0.0022. It scores 280,000 peptide/allele pairs in 27 s, about 350 times faster than the original binary. We then examine the training data. In the public NetMHCpan-4.1 eluted-ligand sets, 86 to 99% of hits are found in the human proteome, against about 12% of their decoys, so a model can separate hits from decoys using this difference rather than features related to MHC binding. Redrawing the decoys within the source protein of each hit and matching their cysteine status, with no other change, raises per-allele Mean Top-K on the regenerated v2.0.0 evaluation set from 0.734 to 0.755, and increases Median FRANK on CD8 epitopes from 0.0025 to 0.0053. The same change improves one evaluation set and degrades the other. Code (Apache-2.0) and model checkpoints (CC BY-NC-4.0): https://github.com/instadeepai/BenchMHC-public.

papers.title: Best Practices for Pre-Processing Large-Scale ATAC-Seq Data: Why Epidemiological Studies Demand Greater Stringency
papers.abstract: Assay for transposase accessible chromatin using sequencing (ATAC-seq) and related techniques provide critical insight into the epigenetic mechanisms that regulate gene expression in health and disease. Accurate identification of biologically meaningful chromatin accessibility signals remains an underexplored analytical challenge. Advances in sequencing technologies have increased both the magnitude and complexity of ATAC-seq datasets, leading to demand for scalable, reproducible and robust computational analysis frameworks. Peak calling, which identifies regions of chromatin accessibility, is a critical step that underpins all downstream quantitative analyses. However, there is a lack of consensus regarding the optimal peak calling strategy. Here, we present a novel bioinformatics pipeline PIPPA (Pipeline for Integrative Peak calling in Population-scale ATAC-seq), for quality control and peak set curation of large-scale ATAC-seq datasets. Using two independent cell-type sorted ATAC-seq datasets, we show that peak calling performance is dataset-dependent and that no single significance threshold performs optimally across all scenarios. We provide practical recommendations for parameters to generate high-confidence chromatin accessibility profiles. Our peak calling approach is applicable for other genome wide epigenomic assays such as ChIP-seq and CUT&Tag. By standardising this process, the PIPPA pipeline enhances epidemiological studies focused in identifying epigenetic dysregulation associated with development and disease.
affiliations: University of Exeter (corresponding author)

papers.title: Lymphoma response to chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy is driven by endogenous tumor-reactive CD8⁺ T cells
papers.abstract: CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy induces durable remissions in a subset of patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma; however, most patients fail to respond or eventually relapse. By integrating whole-genome and transcriptome profiling of 54 patients with functional assays, syngeneic models, and mathematical modeling, we demonstrate that durable CAR-T efficacy requires cooperation between CAR-T cells and endogenous CD8 (eCD8) T cells recruited to join the attack on malignant cells. Tumors with biallelic loss of MHC class I or CD58 exhibited high genomic complexity, increased neoantigen burden, and resistance to CAR-T therapy. MHC-I-deficient lymphomas showed suboptimal response in immunocompetent hosts compared to wild type. Importantly, sustained responses in mice occurred only in the presence of eCD8 cells, whereas all CD8-depleted mice relapsed after initial CAR-T-mediated tumor regression. Patients and murine ELISPOT assays confirmed enhanced endogenous T-cell activation post-CAR-T. These findings reveal that CAR-T therapy functions not only as a cytotoxic modality but also as a catalyst for endogenous anti-tumor immunity.
affiliations: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (corresponding author)

papers.title: Inferring somatic copy number aberrations from spatial transcriptomics data to study early cancer development
papers.abstract: Understanding the spatial organisation of cells undergoing early transformation and their interactions with the local microenvironment is critical to studying the earliest stages of cancer development. Somatic copy number aberrations (SCNAs) are among the earliest genomic alterations observed in many cancers, but their spatial context remains difficult to study using conventional sequencing approaches. We developed a computational framework to infer SCNAs directly from Xenium spatial transcriptomics data, enabling the identification and spatial mapping of cell populations sharing common SCNA profiles. Applying this approach to ovarian, cervical and breast cancer datasets identified spatially coherent SCNA-defined populations that recapitulated known tumour-associated copy number aberrations and pathological states. In high-grade serous ovarian cancer, we identified an intermediate epithelial population within the fallopian tube exhibiting features of early transformation accompanied by immune remodelling. Together, our pipeline establishes a scalable framework for reconstructing the spatial architecture of SCNA-defined clones, providing new opportunities to identify and characterise candidate early transforming cell populations in situ.
affiliations: University College London (corresponding author)

papers.title: mRNA deep sequencing profiling and integrative miRNA-mRNA network analysis in pediatric Burkitt leukemia and lymphoma
papers.abstract: Background: Although the genomic alterations in Burkitt leukemia and lymphoma (BL) have been extensively studied, data on genome-wide dysregulation of messenger RNA (mRNA) and microRNA (miRNA) in Burkitt leukemia (BuAL) and Burkitt lymphoma (BuLY) are scarce. The aim of this study was to analyze mRNA and miRNA expression profiles in pediatric BuAL/BuLY to identify dysregulated mRNA-miRNA networks. Methods: Total RNA from fresh tumor samples of 13 pediatric BL patients (BuAL n=7, BuLY n=6) and 4 pediatric normal control lymphoid tissue (NCLT) samples was included for mRNA-deep sequencing and miRNA-microarrays studies. Differential expression (DE) analysis of mRNAs and miRNAs as well as gene set and functional enrichment analysis were performed. The multiMiR R package was used to identify the validated target genes for the dysregulated miRNAs. miRNA-mRNA target interaction analysis was performed combining DE, validated targets observed among the inverse-significant miRNA-mRNA correlations, with evidence statistics retained (p[≤]-0.5 and Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) -adjusted correlation p-value 0.5) and 11 DE miRNAs (three upregulated and eight downregulated) (FC>1.5, p-adj<0.05). The transcriptional differences observed between BL and normal lymphoid tissue inferred by functional enrichment analysis identified along a MYC-driven proliferative backbone with strong E2F4 and MYB pathway activity, activation of the MAPK, PI3K and the G2/M checkpoint signaling pathways and repression of the JAK-STAT, NFkB, TP53, TRAIL and hypoxia pathways (p-adj<0.05). Functional enrichment analysis highlighted an upregulation of proliferative and metabolic pathways accompanied by an attenuated inflammatory and immunosurveillance signaling in BL compared to NCLT. Correlated miRNA-mRNA expression analysis identified DE dysregulated miRNAs and their validated target genes. DE downregulated miRNAs (hsa-miR-150-5p, hsa-miR-342-3p and hsa-miR-450-5p, among others) inversely correlated with upregulated mRNA targets showing pathway enrichment related to transcriptional activity and nuclear organization modules. mRNA targets of DE upregulated miRNAs (hsa-miR-106a-5p, hsa-miR-17-5p and hsa-miR-7-5p) were enriched in downregulated pathways related to immune response processes. Conclusions: Overall, this pilot study provides new insights on key proliferative, metabolic and cytokine-mediated immune signaling pathways in BL and highlights miRNA-mRNA networks influencing transcriptional activity and immune surveillance, paving the way for experimental validation models.
affiliations: Rostock University Medical Center, Pediatrics Department, Pediatric Hematology, Oncology and Palliative Care, Rostock, Germany (corresponding author)

papers.title: Taxon-in-context reveals ecological individuality in the human gut microbiome
papers.abstract: Ecological theory holds that a microbe's role depends on its surrounding community. Yet abundance profiles and fixed ecological groupings leave its individual context implicit. We introduce taxon-in-context, a reproducible representation of each microbe's context within an individual's microbiome. Across 7,700 metagenomes, we show that common gut species occupy different contexts in different people. This flexibility peaked in early life and declined through adulthood, a pattern reproduced in a larger genus-level compendium. For selected species, context within each person's microbiome revealed age associations beyond species abundance and the person's context mixture. In an independent longitudinal urinary tract infection cohort, microbes switched contexts within individuals. Taxon-in-context enabled recurrence prediction where an abundance-based model performed near chance. Taxon-in-context and these findings expose a measurable, dynamic and individualized layer of microbiome organization, providing a basis for investigating why the same microbe or intervention may have different biological consequences across people.
affiliations: Minutia.AI, Singapore (corresponding author)

papers.title: IL-27 Reduces Cell-Surface LDLR in Human Macrophages and Restricts VSV-G-Pseudotyped HIV infection
papers.abstract: Low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) is a major cellular receptor for vesicular stomatitis virus glycoprotein (VSV-G), which is widely used to pseudo-type viral vectors. We previously showed that IL-27 suppresses infection by VSV-G-pseudotyped HIV encoding luciferase (VSV-G-HIVLuc) in macrophages; although IL-27 induced multiple anti-virus genes in cell, the underlying mechanism of VSVG-HIVLuc inhibition remains poorly understood. Here, we examined whether IL-27 regulates LDLR expression and contributes to suppression of VSV-G-HIVLuc infection. Monocyte-derived macrophages differentiated with M-CSF or GM-CSF, with or without IL-27, were analyzed for cell-surface LDLR by flow cytometry, LDLR transcripts by quantitative RT-PCR, and total LDLR protein by Western blotting. Viral binding, proviral DNA, and reporter expression were evaluated by cell-associated p24 antigen, late reverse-transcription products, and luciferase activity, respectively. IL-27 reduced surface LDLR to 38.3 {+/-} 2.6 % in M-CSF-derived macrophages (p<0.01) and 31.4{+/-} 3.2 % in GM-CSF-derived macrophages (p<0.01). Western Blotting demonstrated that total LDLR protein decreased to 48 {+/-} 0.8 % in IL-27-treated M-CSF-derived macrophages (27M-Mac) (p<0.01) while it was not significantly changed in IL-27-treated GM-CSF-derived macrophages (27GM-Mac), although approximately 1.6~1.9-fold increase in LDLR transcripts following IL-27 treatment in both macrophages (p<0.01). Viral binding decreased to nearly 50 % in 27GM but not significantly changed on 27M-Mac whereas late reverse-transcription products decreased to 23 {+/-} 2.1% (p<0.0001) and 44 {+/-} 1.5% (p<0.0001). Luciferase activity was further reduced to 5.8 {+/-} 0.4 % and 5.9 {+/-} 2.1 % (both p<0.0001). These findings demonstrate that IL-27 downregulates cell-surface LDLR in human macrophages, suggesting that IL-27 restricts VSV-G-pseudo-typed Lenti virus infection through both receptor-associated and additional post-entry mechanisms.
affiliations: Frederick National Laboratory for Cancer Research (FNLCR) (corresponding author)

papers.title: Autonomous sampling and eDNA metabarcoding for offshore biodiversity monitoring: a pilot study around an FPSO in the Southwestern Atlantic
authors: do Amaral, D. L. A. S.
papers.abstract: Characterizing biodiversity around offshore infrastructure is necessary to assess possible influences of industrial activities on marine communities and distinguish persistent ecological change from short-term variability. Combining environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding with autonomous sampling offers a way to expand biological, spatial and temporal coverage while reducing dependence on crewed field operations. We evaluated this approach around a floating production, storage and offloading unit (FPSO) in the Santos Basin, Brazil, to establish an initial biodiversity reference and inform subsequent monitoring. A third-generation Environmental Sample Processor integrated into the W Tupan II uncrewed surface vessel enabled autonomous water sampling at coastal sites, transit locations and the FPSO area, yielding 64 biological samples. We used mitochondrial 12S and 16S metabarcoding to assess taxonomic diversity, sampling completeness and spatial and short-term temporal variation. Around the FPSO, 47 samples from 21 points detected 34 species with 12S and 28 with 16S, representing 74.3% and 65.4% of the respective estimated species richness. Local analyses showed weak radial differentiation across 300-1,500 m around the FPSO, with no near-far taxonomic indicators remaining significant after multiple-testing corrections. Samples collected at the same point approximately 1-2 h apart were almost as dissimilar as samples from different points, whereas technical replicates of post-extraction processing closely matched their source DNA profiles. Taxon turnover accounted for approximately 73% and 80% of temporal Jaccard dissimilarity for 12S and 16S, respectively. Regional analyses recovered a coastal-offshore compositional contrast, with geography and sampling date jointly represented. This pilot supports autonomous eDNA sampling as an operational approach to offshore biodiversity monitoring. The findings favour repeated sampling across campaigns to distinguish transient detections from recurrent patterns and persistent compositional changes.
affiliations: Bio Bureau Biotecnologia, Rio de Janeiro, RJ, Brazil (corresponding author)

papers.title: Additive and dominance gene effects described by a logistic function in concentration-limited metabolic pathways at steady state out of equilibrium
papers.abstract: Abstract Additive (a) and dominance (d) gene effects are key to phenotype manifestation. We investigated the relationship between these effects and gene-encoded enzyme rates in an n-step linear metabolic pathway with mass limitation at stationary state out of equilibrium, where internal flux depended on internal enzyme concentrations (Ei, i=1 to n) and external flux on input/output enzyme/transporter concentrations (Ee). Using coupled reversible Michaelis-Menten (MM) equations for Ei rates and irreverisble MM for Ee rates we found that stationary-state metabolite concentration (Si) was a logistic function of Ei. Its inflection point (S0i, E0i) depended on the total mass of the system ({Sigma} Si) and on Ee saturation, shifting from negative to positive values as reaction kinetics transitioned from first to mixed or zero order. Moreover, {Sigma} Si and Ee saturation explained negative, partial, and complete dominance in this metabolic system, provided phenotypic value of trait T is linearly dependent on Si at certain sink. The system was unstable when approaching closure (Ee=0). In this condition, asymptotic Smax equaled equilibrium concentration, being equilibrium displacement the driving force of flux. In pathways with n>1 reaction steps there was a change of regime in early reactions when increments in En passed E0n. This change of regime led to peaks raising at some Si previous to Sn and Sn+1 that were modeled by adding a Gaussian component to the logistic equation. Therefore, if T is determined by some of these Si, overdominance and dominance reversals may be explained. We obtained a good fit when applied this equation to Ei and Si data obtained from silicon-cell models developed with specific kinetic equations and experimentally determined kinetic parameters. In addition, we applied this framework to experimental data on amylose accumulation in starch granules catalyzed by granule-bound starch synthase I, and found that the logistic function fitted data from six plant species. This framework may contribute a partial explanation of the non-linearity between genotype and phenotype from the metabolic standpoint, which may be useful in the future for plant or animal breeding technologies.
affiliations: Departamento de Ciencias Biologicas, Facultad de Ciencias Agrarias y Forestales. Universidad Nacional de La Plata - IBBM-CONICET (corresponding author)

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell Transcriptomics and Explainable AI for Disease Mechanism and Biomarker Discovery in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
papers.abstract: Invasion is an early step in the metastatic spread of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), yet cells within a single tumour or cell line differ in their capacity to invade, and it is unclear which transcriptional features distinguish cells that invade from those that do not. We re-analysed the public single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset GSE329526, in which ClonMapper-barcoded MDA-MB-231 cells were separated in a transwell assay into invasive (five samples, 6,289 cells) and non-invasive (five samples, 5,983 cells) fractions and compared with the parental population (one sample, 3,022 cells). An initial cell-level analysis combined Wilcoxon differential expression, an XGBoost classifier with a random cell split, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Enrichr over-representation analysis. Because cells from the same sample are not independent, we then repeated the analysis at the sample level, using differential expression on sample means (five versus five), XGBoost with cross-validation that held out whole samples, a quality-control-metric baseline model, SHAP on held-out samples and rank-based gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA). At the sample level, 6,651 of 11,727 tested genes differed between invasive and non-invasive samples (false discovery rate [FDR] < 0.05), including the ten top-ranked cell-level genes such as PHLDA2, ANTXR2, VIM and HMGA1 (FDR 0.0007 to 0.0022) and the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) regulators TGFBR2, JAG1, SDCBP and WWTR1. With whole samples held out, XGBoost distinguished invasive from non-invasive cells with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.92 (range across folds 0.89 to 0.95); removing ribosomal and mitochondrial genes did not change performance (AUC 0.92), whereas a model using only four quality-control metrics reached 0.63, and every held-out invasive sample received a higher mean predicted probability of invasion (0.74 to 0.79) than every non-invasive sample (0.20 to 0.28). On held-out samples, SHAP ranked inflammatory and stress-response genes highest (CCL2, LGALS12, DUSP1, CXCL3, KYNU, CXCL2), and GSEA showed higher KRAS signalling (normalised enrichment score [NES] 2.30, FDR 0.001) and E2F targets (NES 1.62, FDR 0.038) and lower interferon-alpha and interferon-gamma responses (NES -1.97 and -1.65; FDR 0.001 and 0.019) in invasive samples. The ribosomal genes that dominated the original SHAP ranking were absent from the held-out ranking. Invasive MDA-MB-231 cells therefore carry a transcriptional state that is reproducible across independent transwell samples and involves EMT-related, inflammatory and proliferative programmes. Limitations include a single cell line, sequencing of the invasive and non-invasive populations in separate libraries and the absence of external validation; the candidate genes reported here are hypotheses that require confirmation in independent experiments and patient material.
affiliations: UNIVERSITY OF DELHI (corresponding author)

papers.title: Asking the Data: Conversational Interrogation of LC-MS/MS Proteomics Data Sets with an LLM Agent
papers.abstract: Proteomics workflows are designed to answer predefined questions, leaving analytical problems that emerge after first results difficult to investigate without additional bioinformatics work. We introduce data set interrogation, a conversational framework in which a researcher uses a large language model (LLM) agent to translate emerging questions into executable tests, check the answers against controls, and keep the code, inputs, and decisions in a dated record. Applied retrospectively to four LC-MS/MS data sets, the framework exposed problems that changed the interpretation of three in-house studies: a search database lacking one of two symbionts, a swapped pair of tandem mass tag (TMT) channels, statistics inflated by non-host proteins, and false deamidation assignments caused by selection of the 13C isotope peak as monoisotopic; the same question asked of every data set revealed failed or partial cysteine alkylation in all three. A public TMT data set was reanalyzed from raw files in 24 min, a feasibility measure without a human comparison; among spectra identified by both workflows, 99.2% received the same peptide assignment as in Proteome Discoverer, and protein fold changes correlated (r = 0.93). In seeded tests, a purpose built channel assignment check detected all 216 between strain channel swaps and none of 90 within-strain swaps. The framework couples natural language interaction with executable analyses, explicit controls, and traceable decisions, enabling researchers to investigate questions not anticipated by the original pipeline. These results establish feasibility in a limited retrospective setting with one researcher; broader evaluation across users, models, and data sets is required to determine general performance.
affiliations: Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (corresponding author)

papers.title: GLOM TGITO: multiscale protein modelling and multiview landscape-guided sequence discovery
papers.abstract: Motivation: Offline protein design can exploit surrogate-predictor errors, favouring high-scoring sequences lacking measured support. We test whether multiscale representations and local experimental evidence improve prediction and candidate prioritization. Results: GLOM-TGITO links a global-local fluorescence predictor to multiview landscape-guided optimization. Across 31,434 measured ppluGFP2 sequences, GLOM achieved random/depth-holdout RMSEs of 0.170/0.247 versus 0.247/0.324 for the strongest SaProt-650M controls. Averaged across three training seeds, 96.3%/97.3% of prediction-ranked Top 100 test variants were measured bright (log10 fluorescence >=4.2). Search from 900 peak regions yielded 2,594 distinct candidate sequences. The selected Top 100 showed 2.9-8.2% lower mean representation deviation than four comparator pipelines; 38 versus 11-16 met joint novelty-reliability filters. Deviation identified measured test errors >0.1 (AUROC
