affiliations: Biosceptre (Aust) Pty Ltd (corresponding author)

Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis
Non-polar surface passivation of PbS Quantum Dots using metal thiolates enables photodiodes rivaling InGaAs performance
papers.abstract: Colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) short-wave infrared (SWIR) detectors (1-2 µm) are of great interest for a plethora of applications including autonomous driving, machine vision, night and adverse weather imaging, in view of their low-cost and compatibility to read-out electronics. However, to date, CQDs photodetectors still suffer from high dark current and thereby noise such that their performance remains inferior to epitaxially grown III-V semiconductors. This performance gap originates from the limited passivation of non-polar surfaces existent in large PbS CQDs needed to access the SWIR spectral range. Here we report on a lead-thiolate based chemistry that serves to passivate both polar and non-polar surfaces of PbS CQDs yielding inks with unprecedented optoelectronic quality evidenced by open circuit voltage deficit and dark current activation energies matching those of single crystalline semiconductors. As a result, we demonstrate infrared photodetectors with remarkable thermal resilience, very low dark current density ( ~ 34 nA cm −2 at −1 V) and a specific detectivity D* of ~8×10 12 Jones. The measured D* value is on par with that of commercially available InGaAs photodiodes (PDs).

A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin-defect emission and quantum sensing
papers.abstract: Spin defects in two-dimensional materials are promising platforms for quantum information technologies and nanoscale sensing. The negatively charged boron vacancy ( $${\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$$ V B − ) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is particularly attractive due to its sensitivity to temperature, magnetic fields, and pressure, but its application is limited by intrinsically weak photoluminescence (PL). Here we demonstrate a van der Waals heterostructure that enhances the PL intensity of $${\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$$ V B − by up to 45× at 4 Kelvin while preserving compatibility with ultrathin optoelectronic platforms. A quasi type-I band alignment at the PbI 2 –defected hBN interface facilitates efficient interlayer coupling to the defect, and strong spectral overlap supports fluorescence resonance energy transfer. Ab initio calculations indicate that this coupling enables a photon-ratcheting mechanism, in which optical absorption in PbI 2 generates a nonlinear polarization that drives $${\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$$ V B − excitation. This process is compatible with interlayer energy transfer while maintaining minimal electronic and spin hybridization and preserving optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast. The heterostructure further exhibits improved sensitivity to external magnetic fields. These results establish a route for the enhancement of defect emission via interlayer optical coupling and introduce a general materials strategy for amplifying weak quantum defect signals in nanomaterials.

papers.title: Genome-wide mapping of genetic suppression events in Streptococcus pneumoniae
Long-term electoral participation among Swedish survivors of the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami
papers.abstract: Natural disasters can spark demands for democratic accountability yet impose losses and displacement that depress participation. We study approximately 16,000 Swedish tourists exposed to the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami who returned home to intact communities. Unlike most people exposed to natural disasters, they faced no increase in the cost of voting, so the case is well suited to studying motivational responses to disaster exposure. We link a survivor registry to population-wide administrative data ( N up to 7 million) and use entropy balancing to compare survivors to matched non-exposed citizens over 25 years. Exposed individuals do not withdraw from participation. Their turnout is 1.4 percentage points higher in 2010 and 2018, a modest but persistent gap. The gap is more than twice as large among the bereaved. Mobilization is strongest among those exposed between ages 16 and 25, which is what habit formation would predict. A 2023 follow-up survey (3,956 respondents; N = 3198 to 3625 per analysis after item non-response) provides descriptive evidence that survivors still evaluate the government’s crisis response negatively and have shifted their partisan sympathies away from the then-incumbent party. The findings indicate that failed crisis management may have lasting consequences for turnout and potentially party choice, and that the electoral stakes of disaster response extend beyond the disaster zone.

papers.title: An untethered sub-gram flapping-wing flight system achieves sustained self-stabilizing and altitude-controlled flight
papers.abstract: Insect-scale flapping-wing micro aerial vehicles offer substantial potential for applications such as search and rescue. However, stringent power and payload constraints at the sub-gram scale have precluded sustained untethered flight. Inspired by the high lift generated by full-circumferential rotor motion, this study presents a cross-shaped piezoelectric direct-drive V-wing structure. The structure uses a tuning-fork vibration mode to generate full-circumferential flapping, suppressing fuselage vibration without external anchoring and substantially improving the lift performance of the piezoelectric direct-drive flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle. Based on this principle, we developed a cross-shaped four-piezoelectric-actuator V-wing micro aerial vehicle weighing 389 mg with a wingspan of 6.8 cm, capable of generating a maximum lift of 1850 mg. Waveform modulation increases the efficiency of the 173 mg drive circuit to 45%, while mechanical self-stabilization suppresses attitude disturbances. Integrated with a 350 mg battery, the 984 mg system achieves untethered, sustained, stable flight for a sub-gram flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle. The maximum lift-to-weight ratio of the untethered flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle system is 1.88. Its maximum flight altitude exceeds 10 m, and its continuous flight duration under low-power operation exceeds 240 s. The system also demonstrates altitude-controlled and disturbance-resilient untethered flight.

Now, a synthetic organelle termed the ‘recordanelle’ can record cellular RNAs in cells for several days and be read with single-cell sensitivity.

Thermodynamic origin of the phonon Hall effect in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
papers.abstract: The underlying mechanism of the thermal Hall effect generated by phonons in a variety of insulators is yet to be identified. In this work, we report on a sizable thermal Hall conductivity in nickel phosphorus trisulfide (NiPS 3 ), a van der Waals stack of honeycomb layers with a zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The longitudinal (κ aa ) and the transverse (κ ab ) thermal conductivities peak at the same temperature, and the thermal Hall angle, at this peak, respects a previously identified bound. The amplitude of κ ab is extremely sensitive to the amplitude of magnetization along the b axis but is not correlated with the phonon mean free path, which points to an intrinsic origin.

papers.title: Electronic bound states in the continuum in a two-dimensional metal
papers.abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are quantum states that remain localized despite lying within a continuum of extended, delocalized states. Whereas optical BICs have been realized in photonic systems, achieving electronic bound states embedded in a metallic background remains an ongoing challenge. In this study, we used scanning tunneling microscopy to identify two defect-induced electronic states that remain localized within the metallic continuum of Pd 5 AlI 2 , a two-dimensional van der Waals metal. Our calculations suggest that electron-hopping interference on the decorated checkerboard lattice of Pd 5 AlI 2 gives rise to a (quasi) flat band built from spatially localized eigenstates that are orthogonal to the dispersive continuum. Atomic defects within this frustrated lattice shift the associated flat-band localized states into the metallic continuum, forming robust, symmetry-protected BICs.

papers.title: Wireless electrocatalytic closed-loop system for drug-free management of diabesity
papers.abstract: Lifestyle-related type 2 diabetes and associated obesity (diabesity) affect >2.5 billion people worldwide and impose nearly $3 trillion in annual health care costs. We developed an implantable, wirelessly powered electrocatalytic closed-loop health optimization (ECHO) device containing platinum-decorated gold nanoclusters embedded in graphite felt that enabled selective, electrically tunable oxidation of blood glucose to renally cleared gluconate. In type 2 diabetic mice, wireless, low-power activation (0.75 volts, 10 milliamperes) restored glucose homeostasis within 1 hour, shifted metabolism from glucose to lipid utilization, reduced body weight and triglycerides, and increased circulating free fatty acids and ketone bodies without detectable hypoglycemia or adverse physiological, inflammatory, or behavioral effects during 6 weeks of treatment. Coupling this ECHO device to a commercial continuous glucose monitoring system enabled autonomous, smartphone-controlled, drug-free closed-loop management of experimental diabesity.

papers.title: BAK and BAX form a multiprotein complex to drive mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death
papers.abstract: The apoptotic regulators BAX and BAK, once activated, form homo-oligomers to trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP), activating the apoptosome and caspases. Activation of BAX-BAK without apoptosome activation triggers sustained efflux of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and caspase-independent cell death. However, the molecular basis of mtDNA efflux remains unclear. We purified a macromolecular complex comprising BAK, BAX, activator BH3-only molecules, voltage-dependent anion channels 1 and 2 (VDAC1 and VDAC2), and prohibitins that released mtDNA from mitoplasts. BAX-BAK activation resulted in VDAC closure, mitochondrial calcium influx, and mtDNA efflux. Loss of VDAC1, VDAC2, or prohibitins prevented BAX-BAK activation–induced mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death without affecting MOMP or mitochondrial inner membrane herniation. These findings support differential regulation of cytochrome c and mtDNA efflux by distinct BAX-BAK complexes.

papers.title: Intron retention regulates STAT2 function and associates with immunotherapy response in lung cancer
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the STAT2 gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti–programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in STAT2 as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.

papers.title: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet
papers.abstract: During interglaciations, the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS), which is the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, retreats to Arctic Canada, where it achieves a minimum configuration. The reexpansion of the LIS following this minimum marks the start of the next glaciation. Here, we show that the last remaining remnant of the most recent LIS, Barnes Ice Cap (Baffin Island, Canada), achieved its minimum interglacial dimensions after ~3.6 thousand years ago, before reexpanding ~2000 years ago, marking the onset of the next glaciation. The new LIS reached maximum dimensions in ~1960 CE, after which anthropogenic summer warming resulted in a negative mass balance, ice margin recession, and the termination of the next glaciation. The demise of the next glaciation, despite the ongoing decline in summer insolation, illustrates the influence of anomalous greenhouse gas forcing on climate.

papers.title: Ultrarapid decision-making in an avian brain
papers.abstract: Perceptual decision-making is well studied in mammals, but its operation in other vertebrates remains unclear. We show that carrion crows ( Corvus corone ) make deliberate decisions in a classic visual motion discrimination task with unprecedented speed, reporting choices in approximately 235 milliseconds on average, which is roughly twice as fast as has been observed in monkeys or humans and without sacrificing accuracy. Recordings from the pallial endbrain reveal that direction-selective neurons encode the upcoming choice as early as about 70 milliseconds after stimulus onset and about 170 milliseconds before the response, with ramping activity scaling with sensory evidence and converging at response onset. These findings highlight the extraordinary efficiency of avian decision-making circuitry, possibly shaped by evolutionary pressures for rapid visuomotor control.

papers.title: Dynamic functionality–enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
papers.abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.

papers.title: Imaging electron-hole asymmetry in the quantum melting of generalized Wigner crystals
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional moiré materials provide a versatile platform to explore phase transitions in strongly correlated systems. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we imaged the density-driven melting of generalized Wigner crystals (GWCs) and Mott insulators (MIs) in electron-doped, near-60°–twisted molybdenum diselenide bilayers featuring a triangular moiré superlattice. We observed notable electron-hole asymmetry in GWC melting: Hole-doped GWCs yielded interaction-driven disordered states, whereas electron-doped GWCs melted into delocalized liquid-like states. This asymmetry arose from the broken particle-hole symmetry of the moiré superlattice, which produced electron and hole Fermi pockets with different momentum geometries upon GWC condensation. MI states melted without such asymmetry, consistent with the absence of a symmetry-breaking density modulation. This work provides direct visualization of the emergent phases that appear as GWCs undergo quantum melting transitions.

papers.title: Visualizing symmetry-broken Chern insulators and their quantum melting
papers.abstract: In the presence of a magnetic field, electronic states of moiré quantum materials develop a Hofstadter spectrum that provides a distinctive setting for studying the interplay between band topology and strong electron-electron interaction. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we studied Hofstadter’s states in bilayer graphene aligned with hexagonal boron nitride and directly visualized the formation of interaction-driven symmetry breaking Chern insulators. Our measurements revealed the formation of phases that double, triple, or quadruple the moiré unit cell at fractional filling of the Hofstadter bands as well as states with complex intra–unit cell wave functions. We visualized two distinct quantum phenomena in different Chern states, including quantum melting driven by the appearance and proliferation of topological defects and a quantum transition co-occurring with phase competition and separation.

papers.title: Decoupled self-assembled monolayer and perovskite deposition for efficient flexible solar modules
papers.abstract: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability of flexible perovskite solar modules (PSMs) are less than those of their rigid devices because surface hydroxyls desorption on flexible substrates, which disrupts self-assembled monolayer (SAM) anchoring and perovskite crystallization. We developed a decoupled SAM-perovskite codeposition strategy that accelerates SAM anchoring by reducing the SAM-perovskite interaction and ameliorates perovskite crystallization. The certified PCE with phenethylammonium iodide as the passivation molecule was 20.2% on PSMs with device areas of 750 cm 2 . With 1,3-diaminopropane dihydroiodide as the passivator, the PCE of 22.0% for a device area of 14.55 cm 2 decreased by 8% after 1044 hours under maximum power point tracking at 85°C and 65% relative humidity. The devices pass all sequences of an international commercialization assessment standard for flexible portable PSMs.

papers.title: Natural product biosynthesis by guanidine prenyltransferases in plants and bacteria
papers.abstract: Guanidine exists almost exclusively as a resonance-stabilized cation, making its direct enzymatic functionalization challenging. We identified the cyanobacterial enzyme NosH, which catalyzes direct prenyl transfer to free guanidine. Structural and mechanistic analyses revealed guanidine activation by a two-aspartate clamp coupled to prenyl-donor binding through a distinct catalytic architecture. Guided by these features, we identified a large family of guanidine prenyltransferases across bacteria and plants. Plant enzymes produced guanidine alkaloids such as galegine in vitro and heterologous expression of a plant ortholog in Nicotiana benthamiana produced galegine in planta, providing a direct enzymatic link to plant-specialized metabolism.

papers.title: Sequential diagnosis with language models
papers.abstract: We explored the capabilities of frontier language models in sequential diagnosis, a diagnostic paradigm that captures the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Given a brief clinical presentation, clinicians selectively acquired information to reach a diagnosis, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy and workup cost. We developed an interactive benchmark and an artificial intelligence (AI) system that simulates a panel of physicians, continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests. Using this benchmark, the system achieved 83.2% accuracy on New England Journal of Medicine clinicopathological conference cases and 80.3% on MIMIC-IV-ED emergency department admissions, outperforming generalist physicians (36.1 and 46.8%, respectively). Although these findings were obtained in a controlled benchmark setting, they highlight the promise of language models for supporting more accurate, lower-cost diagnoses.

The Virtual Biotech: A multi-agent AI framework for therapeutic discovery and development
papers.abstract: Drug development requires evidence integration across biological scales and modalities, but relevant tools are fragmented. We introduce the Virtual Biotech, an organization of artificial intelligence (AI) agents modeled on a drug-development company, with agentic divisions spanning target discovery, safety assessment, modality selection, and clinical development. We demonstrate its utility at three drug-development decision points. First, more than 37,000 agents annotated outcomes from 55,984 trials and found that drugs targeting cell type–specific genes were 48% more likely to reach market with 32% fewer adverse events. Second, it integrated multimodal evidence to propose a therapeutic strategy in lung cancer. Third, it analyzed a terminated ulcerative colitis trial and inferred potential mechanisms of failure. These results demonstrate that human-guided multi-agent systems can conduct transparent, multiscale analyses to inform therapeutic-development decisions.

papers.title: Lifestyle-induced regulatory T cell fragility primes adverse events after immune checkpoint blockade
papers.abstract: Dietary and microbial alterations increase susceptibility to irAEs by promoting IFN-γ-driven Treg fragility and cytotoxic tissue-resident T cell responses. Treg-specific disruption of IFN-γ signaling restores tissue homeostasis and reduces irAEs without compromising antitumor immunity, highlighting Treg stability as a potential therapeutic strategy for limiting checkpoint blockade toxicity.

papers.title: Metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive
papers.abstract: Single-molecule imaging reveals that metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive, and it relies on the repeated recruitment of Pol α and Pol δ rather than their stable replisome association, thereby uncoupling leading- and lagging-strand synthesis.

papers.title: MCT6 is an intestinal Lac-Phe exporter required for metformin-associated weight loss
papers.abstract: The orphan transporter MCT6 is the route by which the meal- and exercise-associated metabolite Lac-Phe exits intestinal cells and enters the blood. Mice lacking gut MCT6 cannot maintain normal circulating Lac-Phe levels and exhibit resistance to metformin-associated weight loss, establishing metabolite export as a regulatory node for systemic action.

papers.title: Lung neuroendocrine cancer induces immunosuppressive macrophages via serotonin to drive resistance to the T cell engager tarlatamab
papers.abstract: Nomura et al. identify a neuroimmune mechanism of resistance to DLL3 × CD3-directed T cell engager and ICB therapy in SCLCs and LCNECs. They show that tumor-derived serotonin programs immunosuppressive macrophages through HTR7 signaling, dampening antitumor T cell responses and limiting immunotherapy efficacy, while revealing a therapeutically actionable vulnerability.

papers.abstract: Sadanandam et al. integrate multiomic, single-cell, and clinical data from ∼2,000 CRC tumors (∼4,500 multiomic profiles including 195,246 cells/nuclei) to define microsatellite stable (MSS) CRC complexity. Analyses identify replication stress, right-sidedness, glutaminolysis, and MYC-E2F-associated epigenetic programs as key features and FAK, PDK1/2, and proteasomal inhibition, combined with trametinib, as potential therapeutic strategies in MSS CRC.

papers.title: Programmable apoptosis circuits enable subtractive engineering of stem cell-derived organoids and embryoids
papers.abstract: The authors introduce a programmable synthetic biology framework for tissue construction from hiPSCs through subtractive multicellular engineering. By selectively removing undesired cells during development via synthetic apoptosis circuits, this approach enhances tissue maturation and refines morphogenesis across organoid and embryoid models.

papers.title: Distinguishing hepatic metabolic effects from overall cardiometabolic benefit after matched weight loss
papers.abstract: Petersen et al.1 conducted a tightly controlled randomized feeding trial to evaluate whether diets with markedly different macronutrient composition modify metabolic responses to approximately 10% matched weight loss. The study provides important evidence that the assigned dietary patterns produced different hepatic metabolic responses. However, the conclusion that the very-low-carbohydrate ketogenic diet produced “greater cardiometabolic benefits” should be interpreted more cautiously because this wording may be understood as evidence of broader cardiometabolic superiority rather than the superiority of selected physiological and biomarker outcomes.

papers.title: Response to Magkos and Silva: Diet macronutrient content and metabolic function in metabolically unhealthy obesity
papers.abstract: We thank Faidon Magkos and André Marques Fernandes Silva for their insightful comments regarding our study. We appreciate Dr. Magkos’ support of the design and execution of our study. As noted by Magkos, a common limitation of diet studies is ensuring compliance with the prescribed diets and studying participants when they are weight stable to avoid the confounding effect of negative energy balance and active weight loss on study outcomes. We addressed both of these issues by providing all meals to participants in conjunction with careful dietary supervision, and by studying participants after weight loss when they had been weight stable for 3–4 weeks.

papers.title: On the interpretation of diet-specific metabolic effects following weight loss
papers.abstract: I read with great interest the recent paper by Petersen et al. from Klein’s group on the effects of weight loss induced by diets of differing macronutrient composition on metabolic function in individuals with metabolically unhealthy obesity.1 I would like to commend the authors for their meticulous and well-executed feeding trial.

papers.title: Genetic dissection of rapid proteolysis identifies TXNDC15 as a key factor of ERAD and lipid homeostasis
papers.abstract: ER-associated protein degradation is central to organelle homeostasis, yet many regulatory components remain unknown. Liu et al. exploit the rapid turnover of short-lived proteins to identify TXNDC15 as a noncanonical MARCHF6-dependent ERAD factor that links proteostasis to lipid homeostasis, illustrating how rapid proteolysis can uncover hidden metabolic regulatory circuits.

papers.title: Targeted lactate depletion via gluconeogenesis by engineered hepatocyte-based micronanorobots for radiosensitization and immune activation
papers.abstract: Fan et al. develop CXCR4-engineered hepatocyte cytoplasts integrated with Au-Pt nanorobots to deplete tumor lactate through gluconeogenesis. Lactate depletion suppresses repair-associated lactylation and impairs MRN-mediated DNA repair, while Au-Pt catalysis amplifies radiation-induced damage. This metabolic remodeling simultaneously alleviates immunosuppression and promotes systemic antitumor immunity.

papers.title: Hit the pause button
Cancer theranostics
papers.abstract: Theranostics integrates diagnostic imaging with targeted therapy to enhance cancer treatment. In this Review, Sofias et al. discuss recent advances in radiotheranostic strategies, advances in nanotheranostic and microtheranostic platforms, and image-guided therapeutic and surgical interventions in oncology.

papers.title: Molecular functions, cellular responses and pathological implications of the RNA modification N6-methyladenosine
papers.abstract: This Review discusses how the RNA modification N6-methyladenosine (m6A) precisely regulates eukaryotic gene expression and orchestrates cellular stress responses, metabolic homeostasis and immunity. It also explores the pathological consequences of m6A dysregulation in brain disorders and cancer.

papers.title: Sensing a problem here: nucleotide signaling in immunity
papers.abstract: Cyclic nucleotides are shared messengers of antiviral immunity across bacteria and animals, yet the same chemical signal can produce strikingly different cellular outcomes. Recent studies show that bacteria generate the mammalian cyclic GMP–AMP synthase product, 2′-5′,3′-5′-cyclic GMP–AMP, during phage infection and use it to activate membrane-disrupting SMODS-associated and fused to various effector domains-family effectors. Structural work further reveals how ligand binding drives receptor oligomerization, filament formation, and vertical membrane shearing. In parallel, viral proteins that degrade or sequester cyclic nucleotides have exposed new evolutionary pressures on these pathways. We discuss how receptor architecture, supramolecular assembly, and antagonism determine signal meaning and how newly defined defense systems invert conventional signaling logic by sensing the loss rather than the production of an immune nucleotide.

papers.title: Nondestructive quality control across the life cycle of bioprinted products
papers.abstract: Bioprinting is a transformative technology paving the way toward complex tissue-engineered products, yet its translation is constrained by major quality control challenges. Variability in cells, bioinks, bioprinting parameters, and tissue maturation can compromise reproducibility and product consistency. Addressing such variability requires repeated measurements across the multistage, multifactorial bioprinting pipeline that conventional destructive assays cannot provide. In this opinion article, we argue that nondestructive testing (NDT) should become an enabling component of reliable bioprinting. We discuss how complementary NDT modalities could support monitoring, optimization, automation, and scalability in the short term, while validated multimodal strategies could support clinical translation in the long term.

papers.title: Integrated nanocoating and biofilm engineering enhance extracellular electron transfer
papers.abstract: Microbes exchange electrons with electrodes to generate electricity or drive chemical reactions. This study combines conductive cell coatings, cellular recovery, and light-controlled formation of electrode biofilms to improve electron transfer in both directions, providing a strategy for designing more effective interfaces between living cells and electrodes.

papers.title: Morphofunctional Characterization of Colonic Organoids from Muc2-/- Mice
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) remain a serious challenge in gastroenterology, and disruption of the mucus barrier integrity plays a key role in their pathogenesis. The Muc2 protein is the main structural component of the protective mucus layer in the colon, and mice with a knockout of the Muc2 gene (Muc2-/-) serve as a classic model for studying IBD. In the present work, three-dimensional cultured organoids derived from the colonic crypts of Muc2-/- mice and their wild-type littermates (Muc2/) were used for a comparative analysis of their morphofunctional characteristics. Using morphometric analysis and flow cytometry to identify the Lgr5 stem cell population, we demonstrated that organoids obtained from Muc2-/- animals are characterized by a smaller size, absence of crypt-like structures, increased proliferative activity, and a reduced proportion of stem cells compared to organoids derived from wild-type littermates. The obtained data indicate that Muc2 deficiency and the associated intestinal inflammation affect epithelial architecture and stem cell balance outside the inflammatory environment in vitro. Thus, 3D colonic organoids derived from Muc2 knockout mice represent a promising tool for studying IBD and testing novel therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Vascularized Organoids Emerge from a Heart-Foregut-like Intermediate Recapitulating Early Human Development
papers.abstract: During early cardiogenesis, the heart regions lie in close contact with foregut endoderm, which supplies essential nutrients and signaling cues to orchestrate primitive heart tube assembly. Here, we show that self-organized heart/foregut like-structures emerge from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs). The initial heart/foregut-like structures, termed the Seed, are encased by surrounding supportive cells termed Soil, which provide a matrix microenvironment; the Seed progressively develops into chambered human cardiac organoids (hCOs) containing cardiomyocytes (CMs), epicardial cells, cardiac fibroblasts, and endothelial cells. Optimization of the induction system further enhanced hCO maturation and vascularization. Therefore, this Soil-Seed system provides a model to dissect human early heart/foregut self-organization.
