Plasma eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 as T2 biomarkers for biological staging and prognosis in Alzheimer’s disease
papers.abstract: Plasma biomarkers that reflect distinct stages of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) could enable scalable biological staging. We evaluated phosphorylated tau (p-tau) species across multiple analytical platforms and the endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region containing residue 243 (eMTBR-tau243) using a dedicated LC-MS/MS platform in a well-characterized cohort with amyloid PET and a subset with tau PET. While T1 biomarkers increased during preclinical stages, eMTBR-tau243 and p-tau205 increased later, consistent with fibrillar tau aggregation. eMTBR-tau243 showed the strongest and stage-dependent associations with regional tau PET and cognition, outperforming T1 biomarkers in predicting cross-sectional and longitudinal cognition. A plasma-based tau staging system integrating p-tau217 and eMTBR-tau243 closely aligned with PET-based tau staging and predicted longitudinal cognitive trajectories. These findings support plasma eMTBR-tau243 as a prototypical T2 biomarker and highlight the potential of plasma-based tau staging for prognosis and therapeutic decision-making in AD.

Transforming electrified railway into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization
papers.abstract: Decarbonizing electricity requires vast energy storage capacity worldwide, but constructing dedicated storage assets creates substantial capital, material and embodied carbon burdens. Electrified railways already exchange energy with electricity systems through traction and regenerative braking, but their inherent potential as mechanical energy storage remains unexploited. Here we show that modulation of train operations can transform electrified railways into Electrified Rail-Based Energy Storage. By analyzing 326,034 inter-stop train operations, we estimate its global potential at 190 gigawatts in 2025 and 315–579 gigawatts by 2050. Capacity expansion models for China, Europe and India indicate that it can reduce investment in conventional storage by 11.9–20.0%, corresponding to an extrapolated global value of US$14.9–35.1 billion annually. Without increasing total system cost, electricity systems with this flexible resource could further reduce operational CO 2 emissions by 94.3–258.9 million tonnes per year. Electrified railways can therefore complement conventional storage technologies for electricity system decarbonization.

papers.title: dITP shifts the assembly equilibrium of Kongming to activate NAD+ hydrolysis
papers.abstract: The Kongming (Kom) system, consisting of KomA, KomB, and KomC, protects bacteria from phage infection. KomA collaborates with a phage enzyme to generate deoxyinosine 5′-triphosphate (dITP), which activates the KomBC complex to hydrolyze NAD⁺ and trigger cell death. Recent studies propose that dITP activates KomBC through a simple conformational change. Our findings instead reveal a more dynamic mechanism. Without dITP, KomBC complexes exist in equilibrium between tightly packed oligomers and loosely packed filaments, both inactive. Tight packing accumulates unfavorable electrostatic interactions without positioning catalytic residues for NAD⁺ hydrolysis, whereas loose packing relieves these interactions but leaves catalytic residues misaligned. dITP binding at KomB stabilizes tightly packed KomC cores in the filament while aligning catalytic residues. Therefore, a small-molecule signal activates signaling by shifting the assembly equilibrium of higher-order protein complexes toward a catalytically competent state.

papers.title: The 2023 North Atlantic marine heatwave could have evolved into a far more extreme event
papers.abstract: In 2023, the North Atlantic Ocean experienced a marine heatwave of unprecedented intensity and duration, raising the question of whether substantially more severe outcomes were physically plausible under comparable present-day preconditioning, and which processes could produce them. Here, we apply ensemble boosting to a coupled Earth system model to generate physically consistent alternative evolutions of a 2023-like event. The boosted ensemble produced marine heatwaves lasting up to 579 days, reaching maximum intensities of 4.5 °C above climatology and cumulative intensities of 717 °C·days, compared with 240 days, 2.9 °C and 224 °C·days in observations. Detailed analyses of the longest and most intense events highlight contrasting roles for persistent Euro-Atlantic high pressure, reduced turbulent heat loss, enhanced shortwave radiation and upper-ocean heat redistribution. Finally, we place these present-day storylines in the context of future warming, showing that events comparable to the observed 2023 event become increasingly common as global warming progresses.

Short-term effectiveness and impact of Vaxchora vaccine during the 2024 cholera outbreak in Mayotte
papers.abstract: Global cholera resurgence and vaccine shortage have driven the adoption of reactive one-dose strategies with killed oral cholera vaccines (OCVs). The live-attenuated vaccine CVD 103-HgR (Vaxchora) shows high efficacy in human challenge studies, but its real-world effectiveness in outbreaks is unknown. Here, we analyze the 2024 outbreak in Mayotte, focusing on Koungou village, which had high cholera incidence and vaccine uptake. We develop several stochastic models and calibrate them to daily cases by vaccination status. In total, 3354 individuals (71%) of Koungou’s at-risk population ( n = 4733) received CVD 103-HgR, and 77 cases were confirmed, with symptom onset between 19 April and 7 July 2024. At baseline, we estimate a basic reproduction number $${R}_{0}$$ R 0 of 1.5 (95% credible interval (CrI): 1.2, 1.9) and a CVD 103-HgR effectiveness in preventing cholera of 87% (95% CrI: 74, 99), remaining between 75% and 91% across scenarios. Counterfactual simulations estimate 536 (95% CrI: 240, 824) cases averted at baseline, with a range of point estimates from 152 to 1228 across sensitivity analyses. Rapid single-dose CVD 103-HgR deployment is associated with high effectiveness during a real‑world outbreak, with a substantial but more uncertain population impact, supporting the inclusion of live-attenuated OCVs in reactive strategies when necessary.

papers.title: The pyrin inflammasome senses OCTN2-mediated uptake of extracellular ʟ-carnitine from muscle injury or ingestion
papers.abstract: ʟ-Carnitine is a nonproteinogenic amino acid highly abundant in myocytes, and both excess ingestion of myocytes and myocyte necrosis are associated with systemic inflammation. Here, we find that the pyrin inflammasome senses extracellular ʟ-carnitine through the high-affinity carnitine transporter OCTN2 (SLC22A5) and this leads to IL-1β-mediated inflammation. Our findings position OCTN2 as a potential target to reduce inflammation from exogenous or endogenous sources of extracellular ʟ-carnitine.

The FDA-approved drug ixazomib selectively disrupts SOX2 condensates in an HSP70-dependent manner, offering an SCC-specific, biomarker-guided therapeutic strategy with high translational potential.

papers.title: Isobavachalcone targets deubiquitinase OTUB1 to induce PD-L1 degradation and enhances antitumor immunity
papers.abstract: Zhang et al. demonstrate that isobavachalcone targets the deubiquitinase OTUB1 to promote PD-L1 ubiquitination and degradation in cancer cells. This regulation enhances T cell-mediated antitumor immunity and reshapes the tumor immune microenvironment to suppress tumor growth.

papers.title: RiboCouple links RNA backbone generation to sequence design through a learned interaction topology
papers.abstract: Designing ribonucleic acid (RNA) molecules with prescribed structures and functions is central to RNA engineering. Backbone-first approaches generate three-dimensional geometry before assigning a nucleotide sequence, yet leave open how that geometry should be represented for downstream sequence design. Here we introduce RiboBridge, which infers a probabilistic residue-pair state from backbone geometry, recycles binary pair probabilities through a second pass and transfers binary and typed signals as soft attention biases for sequence decoding. On 550 generated backbones, pair-type decoding achieved joint refolding validity of 0.451 versus 0.335 for an architecture-matched topology-free decoder. On a matched 110-backbone intervention cohort, replacing aligned pair states with exact-length donors matched on pair-state statistics reduced joint validity from 0.464 to 0.214, showing backbone alignment matters. Pair-confidence ranking enriched the joint-validity rate from 0.451 overall to 0.596 among the top 248 before external refolding, with the same ranking signal transferring to independently generated RFDpoly and RNA-FrameFlow backbones. On 53 experimentally determined backbones, pair-coupled decoding improved secondary-structure agreement relative to residue-wise argmax. These results support a learned relational interface between sequence-free backbone generation and sequence design.
affiliations: School of Engineering, Westlake University, Hangzhou, China (corresponding author)

papers.title: Beyond Better Models: Barriers and a Path Forward in Generalisable TCR Antigen Specificity Prediction
papers.abstract: T cells are at the centre of adaptive immunity, protecting the organism against infection and cancer. T cell receptors (TCRs), expressed on the surface of T cells, enable the recognition of target cells through interactions with peptides presented by major histocompatibility complex (pMHC) molecules. Reliable, large-scale mapping of TCRs to their cognate pMHCs remains a holy grail of modern systems immunology, with far-reaching implications for cancer immunotherapy, vaccine development, and the understanding and treatment of autoimmune diseases. While exhaustive experimental mapping remains intractable due to the enormous combinatorial sequence space of TCRs and pMHCs, computational approaches offer a promising alternative. Consequently, we have witnessed increasingly sophisticated computational models of TCR antigen specificity, from small neural networks to deep generative models and large protein language models. However, several independent benchmarks have shown that these models, despite their size and sophistication, largely fail to generalise to TCRs or pMHCs not present in the data available during model development. Here, we investigate possible reasons for this and suggest a path forward to generalisable TCR:pMHC prediction. First, our analysis of the largest public repositories of TCR:pMHC data reveals significant biases towards a small number of antigens and MHC molecules, sparse sampling of TCR sequence space per pMHC, as well as inconsistencies and inaccuracies in data collation. Second, we show the importance of carefully setting up model evaluation to measure discrimination based on antigen specificity instead of confounding factors present in the evaluation data. Finally, we highlight the need for and propose how best to match the evaluation metric with the specific downstream application of the predictions. Our investigation suggests that we, as a community, need more representative and better curated data, and a robust set of metrics and benchmarks to guide future model development towards generalisable TCR:pMHC specificity prediction.
affiliations: The University of Oxford (corresponding author)

papers.title: Re-evaluating the benefit of training scale in cell foundation models
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models are self-supervised neural networks pretrained on millions of cellular transcriptomes to learn representations that transfer across biological domains and downstream tasks. Despite increasing investments in model and pretraining data scale, it remains unclear how to assess whether these investments improve the quality of learned biological representations. Recent evidence from standard finetuning benchmarks suggests that cell foundation models reach performance saturation after exposure to only a fraction of the available pretraining data. We hypothesised that conventional finetuning may obscure improvements in underlying representation quality and the biological information they encoded during pretraining. To address this, we tested second- and first-generation cell foundation models across corpus sizes using standard finetuning and extended it with a comprehensive fully frozen evaluation. We found that the training-data scaling relationship becomes apparent under fully frozen finetuning, particularly for second-generation models. Zero-shot analyses similarly recovered dependence on pretraining scale. Our findings reveal a fundamental limitation of conventional foundation model evaluation and establish the importance of frozen-representation benchmarking for assessing representation quality and guiding pretraining-scale decisions.
affiliations: Adelaide University (corresponding author)

papers.title: A CAR T cell-amplified suppressive B cell circuit in AML
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is constrained by a hostile bone marrow niche. Here we identify atypical memory B cells (Batyp) as a suppressive population within this microenvironment. Across single cell and flow cytometry cohorts, Batyp were expanded in AML, and their molecular and phenotypic profiles resembled those of atypical B cells associated with chronic inflammatory conditions. Batyp were polarized within the AML microenvironment, and this was amplified by CAR T cell-AML interactions. Mechanistically, polarization was dependent on Toll-like receptor, interferon and CD70-CD27 signaling. Batyp suppressed T cell and CAR T cell responses via PD-1- and TGF-beta signaling, and were enriched in non-responding patients with AML and myeloma. CD180-directed CAR T cells, targeting an antigen shared by Batyp and AML blasts, resisted suppression in vitro and cleared disease in B cell-humanized xenografts while sparing hematopoietic stem cells, with B cell engagement further enhancing their expansion. CAR T cells thus reinforce their own suppressive niche through Batyp polarization, a constraint that can be relieved by dual blast- and B cell-targeting strategies.

Nuclear adaptation to intracellular mechanical forces regulates the phagocytic capacity of Drosophila macrophages in vivo
papers.abstract: How macrophages fine-tune their appetite to fulfil their clearance role is incompletely understood. Phagocytosis exacerbates cytoplasmic crowding, but whether macrophages can sense this increase and use it to regulate their phagocytic capacity has never been investigated. Here, we test the hypothesis that phagosomes exert a strain on the nucleus, which in turn responds to the intracellular mechanical inputs influencing macrophage appetite. Combining genetic manipulation and live in vivo imaging, we show that engulfed apoptotic bodies indent and deform the nucleus of Drosophila embryonic macrophages, and that phagocytosis increases Lamin B levels. Importantly, we show that silencing Lamin B or components of the LINC complex negatively regulates apoptotic body engulfment in vivo. Thus, we demonstrate that phagosome-induced nuclear molecular and mechanical adaptations are critical for Drosophila embryonic macrophages to sustain apoptotic corpse uptake, thereby unveiling a role for nuclear plasticity in the regulation of macrophage phagocytic capacity in vivo.

papers.title: Rapid assessment of chemical complementarity of ligands for protein design
papers.abstract: Driven by deep-learning methods, computational protein design can now rapidly generate de novo structures, opening new frontiers for creating proteins that bind small molecules tightly and specifically, although achieving predictable and tunable binding remains challenging. Here we address this with a rapid physics-based computational method to generate isosteric and chemically complementary binding pockets for small-molecule targets in de novo designed proteins. We test this experimentally by constructing and characterizing binding proteins for several synthetic and natural chromophores. By evaluating only single-digit numbers of designs, the pipeline delivers stable proteins with pre-organised binding sites in apo structures confirmed by X-ray crystallography, which bind the targets with micromolar affinities or better. To illustrate the scope and applications of this approach, we incorporate selective and coupled chromophore-binding sites in a two-domain de novo protein enabling controlled energy transfer between the two sites, and we develop a small de novo binding protein that can be used in live mammalian cells to visualise sub-cellular structures.

papers.title: A randomized trial of supported versus self-fitting over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults
papers.abstract: In a multicenter pragmatic trial, structured primary care physician or remote audiologist support improved the benefits and sustained use of over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults compared with self-fitting.

papers.title: Sudden collapse of ice mélange under increasing submarine melt at tidewater glaciers
papers.abstract: This study models the collapse of ice mélange in glacial fjords in response increasing submarine melt rates. It shows that perennial mélange today is vulnerable to collapse subject to increasing melt, potentially accelerating glacier mass loss.

papers.title: Projected intensification of soil salinization in global drylands under future aridity increase
papers.abstract: Soil salinization threatens agricultural production, water management, and ecosystem health. Yet, how increasing aridity will reshape 21st-century soil salinity patterns across drylands, particularly in croplands, remains unclear. Here, we compile a relatively comprehensive global soil salinity dataset from the past two decades, projecting future dryland soil salinity dynamics using climate-driven machine learning models with multiple covariates, including dynamic dryland extent and human influences. Our results show an 8% expansion of global drylands saline soils under increasing aridity by 2100 (SSP5-8.5) relative to 2004–2023. Southwestern US, Mexico, southern Europe, central South America, eastern and southern Africa are highest-risk hotspots. We further show dryland croplands face serious salinization, especially irrigated systems, where half of these newly salinized areas project more than 4.9% (maize), 17.2% (dryland rice), 3.3% (sorghum), and 21.2% (wheat) potential production losses. Our findings inform long-term adaptation strategies to mitigate emerging salinization risks and sustain water and food security.

papers.title: Dimeric granzyme-A mediates the specific recognition and cleavage of full-length GSDMB
papers.abstract: Cytotoxic lymphocytes-derived granzyme-A (GZMA) cleaves the pore-forming protein GSDMB to trigger pyroptotic killing in target cells. Here, the authors show that the homodimer GZMA provides dual exosites and active sites, allowing specific recognition and process of GSDMB in a trans mode.

papers.title: Closed-loop photoreactor design enabled by machine learning and digital twins
papers.abstract: Designing efficient photoreactors remains challenging due to the complex interplay of reflection, scattering, and absorption. Here, we introduce a closed-loop workflow integrating ray-tracing digital twins with multi-objective Bayesian optimization to design photoreactors with high photon capture and uniform irradiation. A digital 3D reactor model is calibrated using measured emission characteristics, reflectivity data, and geometrical properties and validated against potassium ferrioxalate actinometry. The validated model explores reflector shape and vial positioning, identifying geometries that maximize incident photon flux while maintaining homogeneity across 16 vials. Experimental validation using a photocatalytic Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling shows that reaction yields track simulated photon flux. The optimized reactor is further applied to quantum-yield screening, enabling mechanistic insights across diverse conditions in a single experiment. This work establishes an experimentally validated virtual co-design framework in which machine learning and digital twins accelerate photoreactor development and support quantitative understanding of photochemical processes.

papers.title: Controlling the shell growth mechanism and interfacial oxidation of InAs/ZnSe quantum dots for shortwave infrared emission
papers.abstract: Short-wave infrared (SWIR) emitters underpin applications in communication, imaging and sensing, yet efficient, scalable devices remain limited. Colloidal InAs quantum dots (InAs CQDs) offer a compelling, cost-effective alternative to conventional epitaxial SWIR light-emitting diodes (LEDs). However, developing heavy-metal-free InAs CQDs for emission beyond 1400 nm is hindered by lattice mismatch during core/shell growth, which degrades photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY). Furthermore, integrating CQDs into LEDs often introduces severe interfacial quenching and intrinsic charge imbalances. Here we report a highly efficient heavy-metal-free SWIR LED operating at 1525 nm, enabled by tailored injection strategies and oxidation-induced interfacial engineering. Optimized high-temperature ZnCl₂ treatment and continuous precursor injection improve shell nucleation and growth, while controlled interfacial oxidation is associated with reduced shell-thickness-dependent strain signatures and improved PLQY retention during shell thickening. Together, these strategies yield measured PLQYs exceeding 55% for emission beyond 1400 nm. Moreover, we demonstrate that incorporating a semiconducting InAs CQD interlayer effectively suppresses interfacial quenching and regulates electron over-injection. Combined with a doped hole-transport layer to reduce series resistance, our optimized devices achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency of 3.5% and a record radiance of ~17 W sr −1 m −2 , alongside a T50 operational lifetime of 16 h. Our findings suggest that integrating mechanism-driven shell growth with rational device engineering offers a strategy to overcome current bottlenecks in colloidal emitters, facilitating the transition toward short-wave infrared applications.

papers.title: Resolving short-term meteorological variability amplifies projected glacier loss and sea-level rise
papers.abstract: Global glacier models typically rely on temperature-index mass balance calculations forced with aggregated meteorological data, limiting their ability to resolve short-term variability. Here, we develop a daily-resolution version of the Global Glacier Evolution Model (GloGEM), which we apply globally and compare against the monthly configuration. Our results show that the daily model more closely reproduces mass balance observations and provides a more detailed representation of glacier runoff. Accounting for short-term meteorological variability leads to systematically greater projected mass loss, with up to 25% greater loss in Svalbard. These differences arise from extreme melt days, precipitation-phase transitions, and surface-type feedbacks not fully represented at monthly resolution. Globally, the daily model yields ice volume losses of 26 ± 10% under low-emission and 47 ± 17% under high-emission scenarios over 2025-2100 (ensemble mean ± 1 StD), resulting in an additional 5-10% mass loss (20-33 mm of global mean sea-level rise) relative to the monthly implementation. Resolving high-frequency forcing, or accounting for its effects through parameterisations, is therefore essential for robust glacier projections, while its omission may systematically underestimate future glacier loss.

Discovery of direct-acting small-molecule RIG-I agonists through creation of a selective CARD activation platform
papers.abstract: Retinoic acid-inducible gene-I (RIG-I) plays a pivotal role in recognizing and combating RNA viruses in humans, and it has become a drug target of significant interest. RIG-I agonists composed of dsRNA represent antiviral and antitumor therapies, however the development of small-molecule RIG-I agonists, with their potential for improved pharmacokinetics, remains an unmet need. Here, we report small-molecule RIG-I agonists that directly activate the RIG-I receptor protein. These agonists stimulate the first step in RIG-I signaling by triggering release of the signaling domains (CARDs) from an autorepressed form of the protein. This was achieved by developing a sensitive high-throughput screening (HTS) assay that directly monitors CARD expulsion through optical methods. The resulting screen hits were refined and optimized, leading to a specific RIG-I agonist that induces a robust interferon response. This study establishes a pharmacophore and assay for development of small molecules that precisely modulate RIG-I signaling.

papers.title: Near-infrared-responsive thia-hexaphyrin-based covalent organic frameworks for cancer phototherapy
papers.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COF) have emerged as promising phototherapeutic platforms for tumor therapy, where the columnar π-arrayed metal-free photosensitizers serve as both a cooperative light-harvesting antenna and a semiconducting scaffold for efficient charge-carrier separation and transport. However, the phototherapeutic agents based on COFs are usually activated with ultraviolet and visible light, resulting in the limitation of deep-tissue phototherapy. Herein, we develop near-infrared-responsive COFs through elaborate design and synthesis of a thia-hexaphyrin building block, which feature well-aligned conjugation skeletons for the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and photothermal effect upon 808 nm laser irradiation, outperforming conventional porphyrin-based COFs. This porous framework exhibits high phototherapeutic efficacy, leading to the tumor suppression for 4T1 tumors and CT26 tumors in female mouse model by inducing immunogenic cell death through phototherapy and triggering systemic anti-tumor immune responses.

papers.title: Cadonilimab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract malignancies: the phase II bicureX clinical trial
papers.abstract: Response rates with approved chemoimmunotherapy regimens remain modest in patients with biliary tract cancer (BTC). Here the authors report the results of a phase II study testing the anti-PD1/CTLA4 bispecific antibody cadonilimab in combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic BTCs.

papers.title: Passive abortive infection mechanisms targeting phage long tail fiber proteins
papers.abstract: Bacteria employ diverse defense strategies against phage infection, yet mechanisms directly targeting viral proteins remain scarcely documented. In this study, we characterize two bacterial defense systems: TFAD1 featuring a serine protease and TFAD2 featuring a Ser/Thr kinase. We show that TFAD1 and TFAD2 act on phage long tail fiber proteins via protein degradation and phosphorylation, respectively. Intriguingly, both systems allow complete phage replication cycles but generate non-infective progeny—a mechanism distinct from classical abortive infection (Abi), which we term “passive Abi”. Our findings expand the paradigm of bacterial immunity by unveiling protease- and kinase-mediated incapacitation of phage structural proteins, offering insights into the molecular arms race between bacteria and phages.

papers.title: Superradiant charge density waves in a driven hybrid cavity-matter system
papers.abstract: Optical cavities enable strong, long-range, light-matter interactions that drive collective ordering, such as superradiant self-organization in ultracold atomic gases. Extending these ideas to solid-state electron systems could enable continuous-wave optical control of electronic order, but is impeded by the mismatch between optical wavelengths and electronic length scales. Here, we propose a platform for realizing superradiant charge density waves in doped, driven transition-metal dichalcogenides coupled to an optical cavity. A nanoscale grating generates electric fields at large in-plane optical momenta, allowing cavity photons to couple efficiently to electronic density fluctuations through exciton-polaron processes. Using a linear-stability analysis, we determine the threshold for superradiant ordering and map out the driven phase diagram. We show that matching the grating periodicity to the enhanced electronic density fluctuations—such as those near Wigner crystallization—lowers the required pump intensity. Our results establish a route toward cavity-controlled electronic order in quantum materials.

papers.title: Ten protein panel predicts ALS from plasma with high accuracy
papers.abstract: Using large-scale plasma proteomics, Kim et al. identify proteins altered in ALS and develop a 10-protein model with high classification accuracy, supporting development of a blood-based tool to facilitate earlier ALS diagnosis.

papers.title: Editor’s pick: Bioptimus
papers.abstract: Each year, Nature Biotechnology highlights companies that received sizeable early-stage funding in the previous year. Bioptimus is developing multimodal and multiscale AI pathology models for biomarker and drug treatment prediction.

papers.title: Molecular predictors of minimal residual disease in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma treated with quadruplet therapy
papers.abstract: In a multiomic analysis of samples from patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma treated with isatuximab, carfilzomib, lenalidomide and dexamethasone induction therapy followed by consolidation treatment guided by minimal residual disease (MRD) status, baseline genomic, transcriptomic and epigenetic features are associated with MRD status after induction.

papers.title: Waiting to get sick enough
papers.abstract: The liver can warn us of metabolic dysfunction long before serious consequences emerge. Why aren’t we listening?

papers.title: Multi-immersion oblique plane microscope (miOPM): a reconfigurable platform for high-resolution light-sheet fluorescence microscopy
papers.abstract: The multi-immersion oblique plane microscope is a flexible and versatile light-sheet microscope that allows imaging of samples ranging from cells in culture to whole organisms or cleared tissue samples.

papers.title: A distinct serological signature of preterm birth
papers.abstract: Preterm birth is the leading cause of death in children globally. We determined proteome-wide autoantibody profiles for 2,195 pregnant individuals, revealing a shared humoral program of normal pregnancy and a distinct, expanded autoreactive signature that precedes preterm birth.

papers.title: The bidirectional double burden of non-communicable diseases and infections
papers.abstract: The alarming rise in NCDs, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, is closely linked to infectious diseases. Despite growing evidence of a bidirectional, mutually reinforcing relationship, these links have received insufficient attention from researchers and healthcare stakeholders.

papers.title: Establishing Polycomb regulatory landscapes in human early development
papers.abstract: The authors profile H2AK119ub (H2Aub) in human gametes, two-cell embryos, eight-cell embryos, blastocysts and human embryonic stem cells. Their analysis provides a comprehensive view of H2Aub reprogramming and patterning during the earliest stages of human development.

papers.title: RNA ends connect genetic risk to brain disease
papers.abstract: Alternative polyadenylation changes mRNA ends, thereby altering mRNA stability, translation or subcellular localization without necessarily changing RNA abundance. New work mapping this post-transcriptional layer across 379 human brains shows how genetic variation in 3′-UTR choice relates to disease-associated loci and downstream molecular effects.

papers.title: Monocyte surface Y RNAs potentiate innate immunity
papers.abstract: Jiang, He, Xu, Zheng et al. report a functional role for cell-surface Y RNAs in modulating extracellular histone-induced inflammatory signalling and cytokine secretion, which may contribute to the pathogenesis of inflammatory bowel disease.

papers.title: Let’s degrade
Reduction reporter
Being N sync
Finding signal in the noise
Developing phenylalanine decaging
Sensing red light
An interpretable AI model decodes the rules of cell recruitment to specific destinations
papers.abstract: An interpretable neural network, SPACER, learns the rules of cellular recruitment directly from tissue spatial transcriptomics data. Analyses of multiple cancers reveal a role for the local antigen presentation machinery and tumour mucins in T cell recruitment to tumours, and a mouse model of severe checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis identifies CD4+ T cells as key disease effectors.

papers.title: Towards equitable population epigenomics: implications for global health
papers.abstract: Population epigenomic studies remain heavily skewed towards participants of European genetic ancestries, limiting the discovery and translation of DNA methylation associations across contexts. The Diverse Epigenetic Epidemiology Partnership outlines priorities for building a more equitable global epigenomics research agenda and improving the relevance of epigenetic insights for global health.

papers.title: Daily briefing: We’re close to reaching a 30% land-conservation target
A novel proviral mechanism for the ISG, Shiftless, during human coronavirus infection
papers.abstract: As highly pathogenic human coronaviruses continue to emerge from zoonotic sources, understanding how host intrinsic immune responses control infection is critical for preventing severe disease. The interferon (IFN) pathway induces antiviral effectors, including the interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) Shiftless (SHFL), which restricts -1 programmed ribosomal frameshifting during SARS-CoV-2 infection. Here, we investigate a novel proviral mechanism for SHFL using loss-of-function and gain-of-function approaches. Despite its established antiviral activity, SHFL enhanced infection by SARS-CoV-2 and the seasonal coronavirus HCoV-229E by increasing cellular susceptibility to infection. SHFL further promoted coronavirus infection by reducing cellular sensitivity to IFN, potentially through modulation of JAK/STAT signaling. Finally, we demonstrate that SHFL-mediated enhancement of baseline viral susceptibility is partially dependent on the domain previously implicated in its antiviral inhibition of -1 programmed ribosomal frameshifting. In contrast, SHFL-mediated regulation of IFN signaling is independent of this domain. Together, these findings establish SHFL as a dual-function ISG with distinct proviral and antiviral activities, highlighting the complex roles of innate immune effectors during coronavirus infection.
affiliations: Emory University (corresponding author)

papers.title: Molecular architecture of Cryptococcus cell walls reveals species-specific chitosan-dependent remodeling
papers.abstract: Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii are fungal pathogens that cause life-threatening infections, including cryptococcal meningitis. A distinctive feature of the cryptococcal cell wall is the extensive deacetylation of chitin to chitosan, a modification that is essential for virulence but whose structural role in cell-wall organization remains poorly understood. Here, we analyze the cell walls of wild-type strains of both species and their avirulent chitosan-deficient mutants, which serve as vaccine candidates. Loss of chitosan disrupted cell morphology and altered cell-wall ultrastructure, with more pronounced defects in C. neoformans . Solid-state NMR reveals that aggregated α-(1→3)-glucans form the principal rigid domain of the cell wall in both species and are closely associated with chitin microfibrils, whereas surrounding β-glucans and mannoproteins constitute a more dynamic matrix. Chitosan modulates hydration and flexibility, and its loss increases chitin exposure and triggers species-specific remodeling of the polysaccharide network. In C. neoformans , chitosan depletion increased α-(1→3)-glucan content and reduced β-glucan levels, whereas C. gattii selectively lost one α-(1→3)-glucan subtype while maintaining β-glucan levels. Although capsule production remained intact, chitosan deficiency altered glucuronoxylomannan linkage patterns and mannoprotein composition. These findings reveal how chitosan organizes cryptococcal cell-wall architecture and highlight distinct structural adaptation strategies among pathogenic Cryptococcus species.

papers.title: Bacteroides–Escherichia interactions contribute to colonization resistance against Clostridioides difficile
papers.abstract: Commensal gut bacteria are key contributors to the resilience against pathogen invasion. This is exemplified by the success of faecal microbiota transplantation in treating recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection. Yet, characteristics of communities that can confer colonisation resistance and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. Here we use a synthetic community of 14 commensal gut bacteria to uncover inter-species interactions and metabolic pathways underpinning the emergent resilience against C. difficile invasion. We challenged this synthetic community as well as faecal-matter-derived communities with antibiotic treatment and C. difficile in a continuous flow bioreactor. Using generalised Lotka-Volterra and genome-scale metabolic modelling, we identified interactions between Escherichia coli and Bacteroides/Phocaeicola sp. as key to the pathogen’s suppression. Metabolomics and targeted validation experiments revealed that fructan-derived fructooligosaccharides, vitamin B3 biosynthesis, and competition for Stickland metabolism precursors causally contribute to suppression across multiple C. difficile strains and donor backgrounds. Analysis of metagenomics data from patient cohorts and clinical trials attested the in vivo relevance of the identified metabolic pathways and the ratio between Bacteroides and Escherichia in successful colonisation resistance. The latter was found to be a stronger discriminator than commonly used alpha diversity metrics. Together, our study uncovers emergent microbial interactions in pathogen resistance with implications for rational design of bacteriotherapies.

papers.title: Solvent heterogeneity regulates assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization
papers.abstract: Supramolecular polymers are fundamental mimics of biological assemblies with diverse functions. However, predicting monomer solubility and controlling the colloidal stability of the resulting assemblies in solution remain major challenges. As a result, their preparation commonly relies on solvent mixtures, which can generate local heterogeneities during sample processing—an effect that remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that solvent heterogeneity biases assembly pathways in supramolecular polymerization, with the extent of this effect modulated by monomer structure. Using an amphiphilic Pd(II) complex as a model system, we uncover a thermally accelerated transition from kinetically controlled discrete nanostructures to thermodynamically stable supramolecular polymers in water/1,4-dioxane mixtures. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that this transformation is mediated by microscopic liquid–liquid phase separation within the mixed solvent, creating 1,4-dioxane-enriched microdomains with increased local monomer concentration. Thermal annealing enhances molecular mobility and promotes the growth and coalescence of these microdomains, facilitating the transition to one-dimensional fibers. Extending the investigation to structurally related monomers further identifies the metal center and hydrogen-bonding motifs as key design elements governing this behavior. By linking molecular design and solvent heterogeneity to pathway complexity, our findings highlight how mixed solvents can be used to control supramolecular polymerization.

papers.title: Lesions of anterior cingulate cortex disrupt an electrophysiological signature of goal completion in humans
papers.abstract: The reward positivity (RewP) is an event-related brain potential (ERP) component associated with feedback and goal completion. Although the component is said to be generated in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), this inference is disputed because of the inverse problem. Recent intracranial electroencephalogram (EEG) current source density analyses provided direct evidence that the RewP is generated in caudal ACC, specifically Brodmann areas 24c’ and 32’. To further test this hypothesis, we examined the effects of damage to frontal cortex damage on RewP amplitude. Scalp EEG was recorded from 68 stroke patients with frontal lesions while they performed a trial-and-error guessing task used to elicit a canonical RewP. Non-parametric voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping revealed that damage to Brodmann areas 24c’ and 32’ significantly attenuated RewP amplitude. These results align with evidence suggesting a single generator of the RewP in the caudal ACC, supporting the role of caudal ACC in motivation of extended behaviors.

papers.title: Zr-based oxyhalide superionic electrolyte with self-passivating interphase stabilisation for high-voltage and fast-charging all-solid-state lithium batteries
Low-Dose Glucocorticoids Adjunctive to Flow Diverter Therapy for Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysms Improve Cerebrovascular Outcomes
papers.abstract: Flow diverter (FD) implantation is standard for unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIAs), but cerebrovascular complications persist. This nested study within a prospective multicenter cohort evaluates whether short-term, low-dose glucocorticoid use is associated with cerebrovascular outcomes after FD implantation. Propensity-score matching with exact matching on UIA location yielded 1327 patients (360 glucocorticoid-treated; 967 controls). Intravenous glucocorticoids, initiated within 2 hours of the FD procedure and administered for ≥2 days, were associated with fewer in-hospital cerebrovascular events (6.9% vs. 13.1%; adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.53) and major cerebrovascular events (4.7% vs. 12.4%; aOR, 0.37). Over a median 2-year follow-up, glucocorticoid use was also associated with fewer new-onset major cerebrovascular events (3.6% vs. 8.7%; adjusted hazard ratio, 0.41) and less in-stent stenosis (7.9% vs. 13.2%; aOR, 0.55). Findings remained robust in unmatched patients on sensitivity analyses. We demonstrate that perioperative glucocorticoid regimens may reduce cerebrovascular events and in-stent stenosis in FD-treated patients, warranting randomized trials.

papers.title: A CRC–MYB chromatin loop controls auxin-mediated nectary growth in Arabidopsis
papers.abstract: Floral nectaries, typically located at stamen bases, secrete sugar-rich nectar containing diverse secondary metabolites. Despite their defined position and specialized function, the mechanisms governing nectary formation remain unclear. Using publicly available single-nucleus RNA-seq data and newly generated spatial transcriptomic data, we identify a putative ordering of transcriptional states associated with nectary development and a spatial regulatory network controlling nectary growth in Arabidopsis thaliana . We further show that CRABS CLAW (CRC) is central to this network, integrating transcriptional regulation with spatial auxin transport and pathways controlling phytohormone signaling, sugar transport and terpene biosynthesis. CRC interacts with MYB21, MYB24 and MYB57 to form a complex that binds the 5′ and 3′ regulatory regions of MACCHI-BOU 4 ( MAB4 ), promoting a chromatin loop that enhances MAB4 expression and supports proper nectary size. MAB4 reinforces PIN-FORMED 1-mediated auxin transport to establish auxin maxima at the nectary tip and regulates PIN6 localization to maintain auxin gradients. These findings link transcriptional regulation and auxin transport with nectary organogenesis and metabolic function.

papers.title: Unlocking electric vehicle flexibility in microgrids via lightweight on-charger coordination
De novo design of lipopeptides with antimicrobial potency enabled by a chain-as-prompt deep learning framework
Spatially resolving isomeric trisaccharides on surfaces with Orbitrap-SIMS
papers.abstract: Many biologically important molecules are structural isomers that share the same molecular mass yet differ in shape, bonding and function. This creates an ambiguity for mass spectrometry imaging (MSI), where chemically distinct species can be indistinguishable on the mass-to-charge ( m/z) scale and therefore cannot be reliably mapped in heterogeneous materials. Here we demonstrate that Orbitrap secondary ion mass spectrometry (OrbiSIMS) can provide an orthogonal contrast that enables both identification and spatial separation of isomeric molecules directly on surfaces. By exploiting structure-dependent secondary-ion dissociation and gas-phase collisional effects during ion transmission, we discriminate isomeric trisaccharides raffinose, maltotriose and melezitose and spatially resolve raffinose and maltotriose in mixtures. We benchmark these measurements against ion mobility spectrometry and observe consistent trends between OrbiSIMS transmission behaviour and ion mobility separation. These results establish OrbiSIMS as an approach for isomer-resolved MSI at surfaces and interfaces, opening opportunities to map isomeric biomolecules in complex systems where spatial distribution is central to function.

papers.title: Metabolic reprogramming of macrophage-specific transketolase orchestrates angiogenesis in diabetic wounds
Optical-handedness-driven enantioselective synthesis and programmable chirality encoding of covalent organic frameworks
papers.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) typically require chiral precursors or catalysts to achieve asymmetry. Here, the authors report the enantioselective synthesis of chemically chiral COFs using circularly polarized light as the sole chiral director.

papers.title: Molecular chaperone-like TIGR04500 family proteins guide graspetide biosynthesis
Multimodal substrate recruitment enables CTLHMKLN1 E3 ligase to target acetylated N-, C-, and internal degrons
papers.abstract: The GID/CTLH family of E3 ubiquitin ligases employs several substrate receptor subunits that recruit distinct degrons, but the substrate recognition mechanisms of the CTLH MKLN1 assembly have largely remained elusive. Here, we reconstitute CTLH MKLN1 -dependent ubiquitylation of three biochemically distinct substrates – MKLN1 itself, ZMYND19, and FAM72A-recruited UNG2, and determine cryo-EM structures of each substrate bound to MKLN1. The structures reveal how MKLN1’s discoidin and Kelch β-propeller domains engage substrates through multivalent contacts. MKLN1 recruits itself through discoidin-Kelch interactions between MKLN1 dimers, forming an assembly that competes with other substrates. ZMYND19 and FAM72A each bind to MKLN1 through loops engaging the discoidin trench domain while their C-terminal Arg residues engage the MKLN1 Kelch central channel, identifying MKLN1 as an Arg/C-degron receptor. The acetylated N-terminus of UNG2 is positioned within a Y-shaped tunnel of FAM72A, defining an adaptor-mediated Ac/N-degron recognition mechanism. Thus, our data reveal how combinatorial deployment of MKLN1 discoidin and Kelch domains enable a single receptor subunit to recognize a diverse substrate repertoire, adding to a complex picture of degron recognition across the GID/CTLH family.

papers.title: Developing and benchmarking one health genomic surveillance tools for influenza A virus in wastewater
papers.abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a persistent One Health threat, and whole-genome sequencing from wastewater offers a promising surveillance tool. However, IAV is at low abundance in wastewater, making it difficult to sequence. We benchmark four targeted enrichment methods suited for multi-subtype whole-genome IAV sequencing including custom and off-the-shelf methods. Our custom HA tiled-amplicon panel is sensitive, fast, and cost-effective, making it suitable for monitoring low-abundance seasonal variants of known subtypes, although its reliance on conserved and intact primer-binding sites limits primer design to fewer subtypes. A published universal amplicon method targets all IAV subtypes but performs poorly in wastewater due to its reliance on intact genome segments. Meanwhile, probe-capture methods are resilient to RNA degradation. In real wastewater samples, our custom probe panel recovers whole-genome signals from circulating H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, including validated H5N1 2.3.4.4b reads in samples where dPCR detection is limited. However, probe-capture is generally more costly and labor-intensive than amplicon methods. Across all four sequencing methods, two wastewater matrices, and most spike-in and endogenous virus targets, ultrafiltration-based virus concentration consistently outperforms large-volume direct extraction. Together, these benchmarking comparisons and custom panels provide needed information for implementing IAV genomic sequencing in routine wastewater surveillance.

papers.title: Perk mediates tumor cell fate and therapeutic outcome in response to CDK4/6 inhibition
Realisation of a protected cat-qutrit manifold via engineered quantum tunnelling
Epitope-resolved Epstein-Barr virus antibody mapping identifies disease-stratifying signatures in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
Nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage lithium batteries via preemptive passivation
papers.abstract: Achieving high energy density without compromising safety remains a significant challenge for advanced batteries. Nonflammable electrolytes can mitigate fire risk, but poor bulk and interfacial properties of such electrolytes limit their application. Here, a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate electrolyte was developed, achieving a self-extinguishing time of ~0 s and stable cycling in both lithium metal and lithium-ion batteries under high-voltage conditions. The electrolyte comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride, fluoroethylene carbonate, and ethyl methyl carbonate at low concentration establishes a weakly solvating environment, wherein dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride and fluoroethylene carbonate preferentially contribute to stabilize the positive and negative electrodes, while working together to enhance the rate capability, low-temperature performance, and long-term cycling at high-voltage. Accelerating rate calorimetry revealed a delayed thermal runaway onset by 87 °C, correlating with Broadness Index. These findings suggest that preemptive passivation on both electrodes, when coupled with nonflammable electrolyte design, can provide a viable route toward safe, high-energy lithium batteries.

papers.title: Real-time economic disruption and recovery from Atlantic hurricanes across the US
Adma and Ackr3a regulate cardiac lymphatic vessel formation and function during heart development and regeneration
Confining chlorine in the cation solvation sheaths towards stable and sustainable seawater electrolysis
papers.abstract: Chlorine electro-oxidation represents the primary anode side reaction during direct seawater electrolysis, causing corrosion and permanent deactivation of catalyst and thereby insufficient stability. We report that in situ segregated fluorine can actuate the desolvation of cations and Cl − ions via strong H ∙ ∙ ∙ F bonding, leading to the formation of intimate cation-Cl − contact ion pairs that make Cl − migration toward electrode surface prohibited. Meanwhile, fluorine remaining in the cobalt-based catalyst shortens the Co–Co distance, attributable to its large electronegativity, triggering an oxide path mechanism that circumvents the nonideal scaling between OH * and OOH * during oxygen-evolving reaction. Direct seawater electrolysis (with 1 M NaOH) incorporating this catalyst achieves 1 ampere per square centimeter (A cm −2 ) at 1.7 volts and maintains at 0.5 A cm −2 and 60 °C over 2,450 hours degrading at 24.9 microvolts per hour. Our catalyst even survives repeatedly switched current densities (0.25, 0.5, and 1 A cm −2 ) for more than 1,250 hours, manifesting compatibility with fluctuating renewable electricity.

papers.title: Evolutionary extensions of IF2 couple translation initiation to bacterial stress adaptation
Coordinated control of both microtubule ends regulates mitotic spindle length
papers.abstract: The mitotic spindle is a biomechanical structure whose length must be precisely controlled to ensure faithful chromosome segregation. The treadmilling of microtubules towards spindle poles, termed poleward flux, is involved in spindle length control. However, poleward flux velocity has been shown to be both inversely and directly proportional to spindle length, a contradiction that remains unexplained by current mechanisms. Here we introduce a model which demonstrates that length-dependent regulation at both microtubule ends allows plus- and minus-end dynamics to synchronize with one another, enabling pathways of poleward-flux-based spindle length control which rectify previous results. Moreover, our model predicts that spindle length and poleward flux velocity can vary independently via simultaneous perturbations at both microtubule ends, which we validate with protein depletion experiments in human cells. Finally, we provide experimental evidence for length-dependent accumulation of proteins at microtubule minus-ends. Our results thus resolve a longstanding paradox and provide mechanistic insight into the reciprocal control of spindle length and poleward flux.

papers.title: Enantioselective sp3-sp3 cross-coupling of oxygen-containing heterocycles with cyclopropanols
Sequential TPRX1 and HERVL activation delineates a progression toward the totipotent-like state
papers.abstract: Using a TPRX1-EGFP/HERVL-tdTomato dual-reporter system, Huang et al. resolve the cellular dynamics of human 8-cell-like cell induction. They show that TPRX1 activation precedes HERVL reporter activation and that TPRX1+HERVL+ cells most closely resemble in vivo human 8-cell embryos, with HERVL-associated activity contributing to the 8CLC program.

papers.title: Microbes as a programmable toolbox for cancer diagnosis, monitoring, and theranostics
papers.abstract: Microbes have evolved molecular machinery to recognize hosts, access tissues, sense local conditions, replicate, and modify their environments. These capabilities are increasingly being repurposed for cancer detection and control. Phage and yeast display generate tumour-recognition modules; engineered bacteria sense and amplify local disease signals; reporter-expressing viruses reveal tumour infection and transgene activity; and microbial signatures provide minimally invasive biomarkers. Here, we compare these mechanistically distinct platforms through an input-processing-output framework, examine their diagnostic and theranostic functions, and assess the readout, safety, manufacturing, analytical, and regulatory requirements that determine clinical actionability. We also propose tumour-reporting viruses and theranostic viruses as functional terms extending beyond the predominantly therapeutic concept of oncolytic viruses.

papers.title: Mechanism-guided Discovery of Fluoroacetate Dehalogenase (FAcD) Variants for Enzymatic PFAS Defluorination
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent anthropogenic "forever chemicals" whose strong C-F bonds (~460-533 kJ mol-1) resist defluorination, and the recast EU Drinking Water Directive sets parametric values of 0.10 ug L-1 for the sum of 20 specified PFAS and 0.50 ug L-1 for total PFAS. Here, we present DeFluorX, a mechanism-first pipeline that uses Boltz-2 to co-fold 2,150 bacterial fluoroacetate dehalogenase (FAcD) variants with 26 PFAS and fluoroacetate, generating uniformly high model confidence (rho = +0.08) but poorly tracked catalytic competence. Thus, the complexes were ranked and tiered by SN2-defluorination geometry based on the known mechanism of control of FAcDs RPA1163 with fluoroacetate: Odelta...C-alpha distance and Odelta-C-alpha-F angle; relay; carboxylate clamp; F-stabiliser; F-cradle; and penalties for scissile bond strength, backside occlusion, beta-fluorination and bond multiplicity. The tiering identified eight complexes (med angle 173.2 degrees, distance 2.91 A) with a high probability of degradation, including Alphaproteobacterial enzymes, with mono-, di- and trifluoroacetate attacking at 172-178 degrees versus 163 degrees for the control. We performed WaterMap, restrained 1 us Desmond MD, MM-GBSA and scans of the three WaterMap-aware best MD frames per complex using B3LYP/6-31G** QM/MM. All 12 frames exhibited product-end C-F cleavage with barriers ranging from 1.1 to 11.8 kcal mol-1, and the departing fluoride carried -0.43 to -0.63 e. The Laboratory validation is ongoing.
affiliations: Section of Plant Glycobiology, Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences, University of Copenhagen, Frederiksberg C-1871, Denmark. (corresponding author)

papers.title: Drug-centric knowledge graph: representing therapeutic modality, pharmacology and multiscale biology
papers.abstract: Biomedical knowledge graphs link targets to mechanisms, diseases and phenotypes, but target-centered representations omit much of what distinguishes therapeutic interventions. We introduce a drug-centric knowledge graph, whose identity model, schema and information-selection priorities are organized around the therapeutic intervention, and a graph built on this design. Each intervention has one identity, linked through relation types shared by all compounds, including target actions, indications, adverse effects, classifications, half-life and direct links to pathways, Gene Ontology concepts, cells and anatomy, and through modality-specific relation types describing small-molecule chemistry, antibody sequences and formats, protein-therapy sequences and antibody-drug conjugate components. Integrating 38 source resources, the graph contains 166,261 nodes of 27 types, 8,106,906 directed edges of 129 relation types and 18,429 compounds in eight therapeutic categories. Construction combines source-specific extraction, compound-identity resolution, language-model-assisted vocabulary and predicate mapping, confidence scoring and connectivity filtering; an expert-reviewed workflow adds investigational therapeutics without altering the base graph. The design offers a reusable template for representing interventions as structured, multimodal objects.
affiliations: Quanthealth (corresponding author)

papers.title: Beyond Stickers and Spacers: Residue-level Contact Networks Predict IDR Organization and Phosphorylation Rewiring
papers.abstract: Intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) act through ensembles of interconverting conformations, and the sticker and spacer framework describes how IDR sequences encode behaviour by sorting residues into two context-dependent classes. Coarse-grained simulations cover whole proteomes, yet force fields have been compared mainly on global dimensions rather than on residue-level contacts where stickers and spacers act. Here we turn simulations of thousands of IDRs with three force fields into contact networks and describe each residue by contact degree, how densely the residue is contacted, and how often the residue bridges distant parts of the chain. We show that residue types dominating these networks follow the parameters of each force field, whereas the positions of densely contacted and bridging residues are shared between force fields, set by sequence arrangement and learned by a model whose frozen predictions track experimental ensembles in blind tests. We then show that phosphorylation rewires the network most where the electrostatic potential of the unmodified ensemble fluctuates, in two force fields and beyond sequence charge descriptors, and that simulated contact changes track NMR shift changes. Contact degree from a simple model extends the sticker and spacer framework from two classes to a predictive, residue-level description of disordered proteins.
affiliations: University of South Florida (corresponding author)

papers.title: MYC targeted de novo binders impair tumor growth
papers.abstract: MYC is one of the most frequently dysregulated oncogenic drivers across many cancers, yet direct therapeutic targeting has remained difficult because its function is mediated by disordered regions and transient protein-protein interactions. Here we design proteins that bind epitopes within regions of MYC whose sequence is conserved between human and mouse, including intrinsically disordered motifs required for oncogenic activity. In vitro, the designs bind MYC with nanomolar affinity and in cells they engage MYC, disrupt interactions with MAX, and remodel MYC-associated protein complexes. Expression of the binders decreases cell proliferation across diverse MYC-dependent hematopoietic, liver, pancreatic, and patient-derived tumor models, and in an orthotopic pancreatic cancer model, binder-expressing tumor cells were selectively depleted. This work establishes de novo protein design as a generalizable strategy to therapeutically target intrinsically disordered transcription factors.
affiliations: University of Washington (corresponding author)

papers.title: Persistently activated virus-specific CD8 T cells indicate antigen-driven immune aberrations in long COVID
papers.abstract: Long COVID (LC) affects millions of people worldwide, yet its driving mechanisms remain incompletely defined and no treatment has been approved. Persistence of SARS-CoV-2 and reactivation of herpesviruses have been implicated in LC, but direct detection of these viral antigens in blood and tissues has been challenging. T cells are exquisitely sensitive to viral antigens, survey organs throughout the body, and can be readily sampled in peripheral blood. Using high-dimensional spectral flow cytometry and single-cell sequencing approaches with multiplexed peptide/HLA tetramers, we profiled virus-specific T cells from hundreds of people with LC and recovered controls. We identified a subset of people with LC that maintained elevated activation of CD8 T cells targeting SARS-CoV-2 spike and/or lytic antigens from Epstein-Barr virus, but not other viral specificities. Spike-specific cells in LC expressed genes linked to TCR stimulation, terminal effector differentiation, and exhaustion and demonstrated reduced functionality upon cognate peptide stimulation ex vivo. Thus, T cells from a subset of people with LC are likely chronically stimulated by persistent SARS-CoV-2 antigens. These findings establish the use of T cells as biosensors of persisting antigen in LC and other disease settings and may help develop new therapeutic strategies for LC.
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania (corresponding author)

papers.title: The lysis mechanism of the haloarchaeal virus HFTV1
papers.abstract: Kuiper et al. have identified the main lysis protein for a tailed virus infecting archaea. The identified protein, GP33, is a small membrane protein which forms pores in the cell membrane resulting in the disruption of the archaeal host cell envelope, causing cell lysis.

papers.title: Brown adipose tissue ankyrin-B cell-autonomously modulates lipid content and its deletion protects male mice against diet-induced obesity
papers.abstract: Ankyrin-B couples BAT lipid droplet lipolysis to thermogenic fuel availability. Its loss impairs thermoregulation during fasting but preserves fed-state thermogenesis and protects against diet-induced metabolic dysfunction.

papers.title: Permeability heterogeneity controls fluid migration and microseismicity evolution in The Geysers geothermal field, California
Decomposing multi-scale dynamic regulation from single-cell multiomics with scMagnify
Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes
papers.abstract: Hydration critically governs the physicochemical behavior of solutes in both the aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. As typical chaotropic Hofmeister ions, weakly hydrated anions (WHAs) can reshape hydration structures and accumulate at water–hydrophobe interfaces. Notably, WHAs paradoxically suppress the solubility of certain small-molecule monomers in water while enhancing that of chemically analogous polymers. Here, we exploit WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control to regulate polyamide-forming interfacial polymerization (IP), using the piperazine (PIP) and trimesoyl chloride (TMC) nanofiltration system as the primary model. Introducing WHAs into the aqueous phase reduces the affinity of amine monomers for water and accelerates partitioning into the reaction front in the oil phase, remarkably reinforcing IP self-limitation. Simultaneously, interfacial WHA enrichment lowers interfacial tension and, together with accelerated amine delivery, potentially intensifies transport-driven interfacial instabilities. WHAs also lower interfacial water availability, attenuating acyl chloride hydrolysis. These synergistic effects yield hollow-ridged polyamide selective layers with reduced thickness and high crosslinking density, delivering enhanced water permeance and salt rejection. Crucially, module-scale fabrication of high-performance membranes demonstrates that WHA-mediated Hofmeister hydration control is directly compatible with established desalination pipelines.

papers.title: ADAM17 is a broad HIV-1 restriction factor targeted by Nef to restore Env maturation
papers.abstract: Here, the authors show that the cell-surface protein ADAM17 blocks HIV-1 by preventing maturation of the viral envelope protein, while the viral protein Nef counteracts this effect by redirecting ADAM17 out of infected cells.

papers.title: Molecular basis of PADI6 species-specific oligomerization in maternal regulatory complexes
papers.abstract: Maternal effector PADI6 forms the MPU complex with UHRF1 and UBE2D and assembles CPLs with SCMC members in oocytes and early embryos. PADI6’s oligomerization capacity, driven by its N-terminal domain, defines species-specific MPU structure and highlights differences in CPL architecture and regulatory mechanisms

papers.title: Baseline radiographic and microbiologic predictors of treatment outcomes in a shortened all-oral regimen for MDR/RR-TB
papers.abstract: WHO-endorsed shortened, all-oral regimens have improved tolerability and outcomes for MDR/RR-TB treatment, but predictors of poor outcomes remain incompletely-characterized. We conducted a prospective cohort study (NCT05871489) of adults with bacteriologically-confirmed pulmonary MDR/RR-TB treated with a shortened, all-oral regimen in Lesotho. We evaluated baseline microbiologic and radiographic features and their associations with time-to-culture-conversion, end-of-treatment outcomes, and final post-treatment outcomes. Among 238 participants (median age 41 [IQR:31–56], 29% female, 62% with HIV), there were 27 unfavorable outcomes (20 deaths, 3 treatment failures, 4 recurrences). 142 of 148 (95.9%) with positive baseline cultures experienced conversion within four months. Fibrosis, cavitation, bilateral disease, and high smear grade were associated with delayed culture conversion and lower odds of treatment success. Bilateral disease was more strongly associated with unfavorable outcomes in those without HIV; fibrosis and high smear grade showed stronger associations among those with HIV. Cavitation with high smear grade (uOR=0.29, 95%CI:0.11–0.78; aOR=0.39, 95%CI:0.14-1.14), and severe fibrocavitary disease (multi-lobar fibrosis and at least one cavity ≥5 cm) (uOR=0.20, 95%CI:0.07–0.64; aOR=0.26, 95%CI:0.07-0.94) were negatively associated with favorable final outcomes. These findings suggest that baseline sputum and chest radiographic features—particularly in-combination—identify higher-risk patients and may inform risk-adapted strategies for shortened all-oral MDR/RR-TB regimens.

papers.title: Rationally micropatterned antifogging hydrogels counteracting extreme condensation
papers.abstract: Loss of transparency due to water vapor condensation is a widespread problem across diverse applications such as windows, eyewear, displays, vehicles, and kitchenware. Conventional antifogging strategies relying on hydrophilic or hydrophobic coatings, based on chemistry and/or nano-topography, can counteract up to mild water deposition, but lose functionality at excessive condensation environments. Here, we present a passive approach, rationally micropatterning an inherently hydrophilic hydrogel to maintain high transparency under supersaturation. Guided by optics and wetting theory, and employing a diffusion model to calculate related timescales of water film formation, we engineer a wicking structure on poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate hydrogel, facilitating long-term sustainable filmwise condensation. Employing quantitative optical clarity measurements and visualization, we show that our approach clearly outperforms state-of-the-art antifogging alternatives, retaining high optical clarity even in boiling environments. Facile fabrication and superior performance establish our microstructured hydrogel as an excellent choice for sustaining transparency under extreme condensation.

papers.title: Brassinosteroids improve nitrogen utilization by antagonizing BIN2-mediated SnRK1 activation
papers.abstract: Brassinosteroids are widely used in agriculture, but their modes of action remain incompletely understood. Here, the authors show that brassinosteroids inhibit BIN2, leading to KIN10 degradation and activation of gene expression and nitrogen assimilation enzymes.

papers.title: Size-dependent catalysis of Ru nanoparticles for selective reductive amination of PET plastic
papers.abstract: Turning waste plastic into valuable chemicals requires precise control of competing reactions. This study shows that tuning ruthenium particle size enables selective conversion of polyethylene terephthalate into p-xylylenediamine.

papers.title: APOE ε4 carriership status enhances age-related changes in Alzheimer’s disease plasma biomarkers concentrations
papers.abstract: In cognitively normal individuals, the rate of change in concentrations of plasma ptau217 and Aβ−42/40 over age differs between APOE ε4 carriers and non-carriers. For p-tau217, the effect of APOE ε4 carriership is stronger in males than females.

papers.title: Accounting for longitudinal peak quality metrics with MSstats+ enhances differential analysis in proteomic experiments with data-independent acquisition
papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics with data-independent acquisition benefits from advanced instrumentation and computational analysis. Despite continued improvements, the quality of quantification may be poor for some measurements. As the scale of proteomic experiments increases, these poor-quality measurements are challenging to characterize by hand, yet they undermine the detection of differentially abundant proteins and the downstream biological conclusions. We introduce MSstats + , a computational workflow that takes as input not only peak intensities reported by tools such as Spectronaut or DIA-NN, but also quality metrics such as peak shape and retention time, and longitudinal run order profiles of these metrics. MSstats+ translates these metrics into a single measure of quality, and downweights poor quality measurements when detecting differentially abundant proteins. The method offers a natural treatment of missing values, weighting the imputed values according to the quality metrics in the run. We demonstrate the accuracy of the resulting differential analysis in five experiments: two custom benchmarking studies with intentionally induced anomalies, a controlled mixture of proteomes, and two large-scale clinical investigations. MSstats+ is implemented in the family of open-source R/Bioconductor packages MSstats.

papers.title: Cross-species atlas of bacterial RNA 3′ ends reveals termination mechanistic signatures and evolutionary patterns
papers.abstract: Bar et al. generated a comprehensive atlas of bacterial transcript 3′ termini for 32 bacterial pathogens grown under diverse conditions, enabling comparisons across orthologues and growth conditions. These analyses reveal species-specific elements shaping transcript 3′ ends and conserved regulation by premature termination.

papers.title: Molecular triage and isoform protection safeguard ubiquitin chain editing on DNA
papers.abstract: Zhou et al. show that the RPA-stimulated deubiquitinase ZUP1 is itself controlled by ubiquitin-dependent molecular triage. p97/VCP and ATXN3 protect ZUP1, whereas UBR5 and HUWE1 promote its degradation and restrict chromatin accumulation. A naturally occurring ZUP1 isoform bypasses this fate control, providing a protected pool of ubiquitin chain-editing activity.

Orbital-driven Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov state in a layer-locked 3D Ising superconductor
Infant hippocampal and amygdala volume in an observational follow-up from a randomized clinical trial for maternal prenatal depression
papers.abstract: Prenatal maternal depression may have intergenerational effects on offspring brain development, with potential socioemotional consequences. This observational follow-up study examines brain development and subsequent negative emotionality among 109 infants born to mothers participating in a randomized clinical trial (NCT03011801). In the prior trial, brief interpersonal psychotherapy significantly reduced prenatal depression symptoms and disorder as the published primary and secondary endpoints. Exploratory infant outcomes include hippocampal and amygdala volumes at 6 weeks and negative emotionality at 6 months. Here we show that infants of mothers randomized to interpersonal psychotherapy during pregnancy have lower right hippocampal volume than infants of mothers in the enhanced usual care group ( p = .002, d = 0.62). No statistically significant group differences are observed in left hippocampal or amygdala volume. Smaller hippocampal volume predicts subsequent lower negative emotionality (r = 0.19, p = 0.045). In this study, a maternal prenatal depression intervention is associated with differences in infant brain development with implications for their subsequent emotional health.
