papers.title: Embracing macrophage complexity for research and translation
papers.abstract: Ginhoux, Mulder, Arcila-Barrera, and Amit argue that macrophage identity is best understood not as a set of discrete subsets or a binary M1/M2 axis but as combinations of modular gene programs. They propose an extensible, program-based classification of macrophage states and discuss how it reframes macrophage-directed therapy from targeting individual checkpoints toward program-level reprogramming.

papers.title: One structural class, one treatment? Firmonertinib in PACC-mutant NSCLC
Firmonertinib in advanced non-small cell lung cancer with epidermal growth factor receptor P-loop and αC-helix compressing mutations
papers.abstract: Le et al. show that the small molecule TKI firmonertinib has a unique structure to inhibit EGFR PACC mutations in non-small cell lung cancer. In the phase 1b FURTHER trial, patients had robust and durable responses to firmonertinib with tolerable side effects. These findings support advancing to a large, randomized trial.

papers.title: Early-life high-fat diet accelerates the development of vagal satiation signaling and predisposes females to overconsumption
papers.abstract: McCoy, Roman-Ortiz et al. show that early dietary experience shapes how the nervous system learns to sense and behaviorally respond to ingested nutrients. High-fat diet exposure in early life accelerates maturation of gut-brain satiation signaling in mice and produces sex-specific increases in fat consumption and weight gain risk in adulthood.

papers.title: Divergent interplay between STIM1 and STIM2 sets the efficacy of central synapses
papers.abstract: Xiao et al. show that the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) resident stromal interaction molecules (STIMs) 1 and 2 serve both overlapping and segregated roles at multiple steps of the neurotransmission process, demonstrating that STIMs are central regulators of synaptic function.

papers.title: The COX2-PGE2-PKA axis suppresses antiviral immunity by inhibiting mtDNA-dependent STING activation
papers.abstract: STING activation and type I interferon responses are essential for potent antiviral immunity, yet their aberrant activation can drive pathological interferonopathies. Vo et al. demonstrate that COX2-induced prostaglandin E2 signals through the EP4-PKA cascade to establish a negative-feedback loop that restrains mitochondrial DNA-dependent STING-mediated antiviral immunity.

papers.title: Organotypic vascularization improves maturation of human stem cell-derived islets and restores normoglycemia in diabetic mice
papers.abstract: Wang et al. generate vascularized pancreatic islet organoids (VPIOs) containing organotypic vascular networks exhibiting endothelial fenestration. Vascularization enhances β cell maturation in vitro and survival under hypoxia. Following transplantation into diabetic mice, VPIOs establish functional connections with the host vasculature and effectively restore normoglycemia.

papers.title: NKG2D overexpression potentiates CAR-T cells through costimulation by tumor NKG2D ligands
papers.abstract: Li et al. show that activated CAR-T cells upregulate NKG2D ligands (NKG2DLs), rendering them susceptible to NK cells. Overexpressing NKG2D shields endogenous ligands and harnesses tumor NKG2DLs for costimulation, thereby enhancing CAR-T cell persistence, tumor infiltration, and antitumor efficacy across multiple models.

papers.title: Targeting MMGT1 enhances immunotherapy efficacy in triple-negative breast cancer
papers.abstract: Liu et al. demonstrate that high membrane magnesium transporter 1 (MMGT1) expression promotes immune evasion via a senescence-associated secretory phenotype that induces CD8+ T cells exhaustion. Targeting MMGT1 represents a promising strategy to improve anti-PD-1 immunotherapy efficacy.

papers.title: Lean, mean, breast cancer-fighting machine
Towards a rational terminology for cell types
papers.abstract: In this Comment, the authors outline how the lack of a consistent evolutionary framework for defining and naming cell types complicates comparisons across species and obscures questions of homology. As a solution, they propose that cell-type nomenclature be grounded in evolutionary theory by identifying conserved regulatory cores and explicitly incorporating phylogenetic origins into cell-type names.

papers.title: Translating base editors: a decade of progress from the bench to the clinic
papers.abstract: Base editing, a gene editing technology capable of installing point mutations with high efficiency and precision, was first reported a decade ago. This Review examines the evolution of base editors and their road to clinical translation, highlighting key advances, ongoing challenges and the current clinical trial landscape.

papers.title: Closing biosafety gaps in the global plastics treaty
papers.abstract: Bio-upcycling is increasingly proposed to tackle plastic waste, yet the emerging global plastics treaty lacks biosafety governance for the engineered biological systems required. We propose an exposure-based framework distinguishing contained from open-environment applications, addressing biosafety gaps not covered by existing regulations, and preventing bio-upcycling from legitimizing continued plastic overproduction.

Self-extending DNA recording with stochastic and programmed writing
papers.abstract: Recording cellular histories requires new information to accumulate without erasing earlier records. Here we introduce Infinite Printer, a CRISPR recording architecture that couples self-extension to regeneration of a writable terminal context. A self-targeting prime-editing guide RNA (stpegRNA) directs repeat extension, while base editing generates diversity in situ without a separate insertion template for each character state. Earlier sequence remains upstream of the renewed terminus, linking substrate growth with record retention. Auxiliary pegRNAs specify payloads within a write-renew-write architecture. After three rounds of payload input, 4,436 distinct complete CCA-based records contained identities from all three pools. Longer AC/AT records retained shared upstream marks, and full-length sequence analysis resolved additional endpoint distinctions. Joint single-cell readout recovered 1,549 distinct records and 7,669 combinations across 12,302 transcriptome-linked cell labels from a single stpegRNA design. Spatial-transcriptomic readout recovered spacer records at 11,330 capture spots, linking record content to tissue coordinates and gene-expression profiles. Infinite Printer unites substrate renewal, sequence diversification and programmed writing with cell- and tissue-linked readout, providing a foundation for future lineage recording across large cell populations during mammalian development.

papers.title: High-throughput affinity profiling of antibodies against soluble and native membrane targets by digital flow cytometry
papers.abstract: Binding affinity measurements are essential for optimizing and validating therapeutic and research antibodies, yet no high-throughput platform supports quantitative affinity measurements for both soluble and native membrane targets. Here we present a suite of digital flow cytometry (dFC) assays that determine equilibrium binding affinities by directly counting free and bound molecules in homogeneous mixtures without immobilization. The assays enable titration-free absolute KD measurements for fluorescent binding partners, affinity measurements for unlabeled antibodies against membrane receptors on cell-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs), and multiplexed assays for rapid ranking or screening of antibody variants. We demonstrate applications by quantifying the effects of degree-of-labeling on the affinity of antibody-dye conjugates, and of drug conjugation on therapeutic antibody binding to receptors on human cancer EVs. By combining single-molecule quantitation, adaptable assay designs, and high-throughput analysis, dFC provides a versatile platform for therapeutic antibody optimization and research antibody validation.

Market Integration Pathways for Enhanced Geothermal Systems in Europe
papers.abstract: Enhanced geothermal systems can provide constant, reliable electricity and heat with minimal emissions, but high drilling costs and uncertain cost reductions leave their future unclear. We explore scenarios for the future adoption of these systems in a carbon-neutral, multi-sector European energy system. Here we show that in a net-zero system, heat (co-)generating enhanced geothermal plants at current cost can support 20–30 gigawatts (GW) of thermal capacity in Europe, primarily driven by district heating demands. If drilling costs were to decrease by approximately 60% relative to 2020 costs, the technology would become competitive in electricity markets, greatly expanding its market opportunity. However, the spatially dispersed rollout of district heating stands against the confined overlap of high geological potential with low potential for other renewables, which conditions the competitiveness of electricity-generating plants. This results in a challenge where the majority of the market potential depends on pan-European technology learning for cost reductions, emphasising that coordination is crucial in stakeholders’ efforts.

Temporary carbon storage can mitigate slow-responding climate changes
papers.abstract: Carbon removal and storage is central to many net-zero commitments, yet its durability, particularly for nature-based methods, is uncertain due to disturbance risks. Previous work shows that carbon storage-years (the time-integrated quantity of carbon storage) are proportional to time-integrated avoided warming, which in turn causes avoided changes in slow-responding climate variables. Here, we show that temporary carbon storage results in avoided changes in inertial climate variables. Avoided changes in 2100 are proportional to carbon storage-years across a range of storage amounts and emissions scenarios for permafrost carbon, ocean carbon, Atlantic meridional overturning circulation, ocean temperature, and thermosteric sea-level rise. By 2300, proportionality persists in some variables, notably sea-level rise, ocean temperature, and ocean carbon. Temporary storage therefore has climate benefits that extend beyond the duration of the storage, with some persistence of benefits even on multi-century timescales. We find that these climate benefits are greatest when temporary storage is paired with ambitious mitigation.

From fragmentation to fault zone architecture as a structural framework for fault weakening
A smart photothermal microneedle system for dual-targeted therapy of osteoarthritis via MMPs inhibition
Coordinated inhibition of SOX9 and cell-cycle progression by microRNA-200 restricts sebaceous gland fate specification
papers.abstract: The microRNA-200 family (miR-200s) is known for inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cell-cycle progression in cancer, but its function in epithelial development remains unclear. Here we show that miR-200s are highly enriched in hair matrix progenitors but absent from the upper hair follicle (HF), where sebaceous gland (SG) and HF stem cells are specified. Ectopic miR-200 induction abolishes SG specification while preserving hair morphogenesis. Genome-wide identification of miR-200 targets reveals direct repression of negative regulators of WNT signaling and cell-cycle regulators. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses uncover mutually exclusive domains of WNT activity and SOX9 expression in the upper HF that is disrupted by miR-200 induction. Genome-wide mapping of SOX9 targets further uncovers a lipogenic and fatty-acid metabolic program required for SG specification. Together, these findings show that miR-200 blocks SG fate by inhibiting SOX9 function and restricting cell proliferation, defining a spatially organized regulatory network essential for SG development.

papers.title: Only time will tell
papers.abstract: Chronotherapy promises to improve medicine by aligning treatment with the body’s internal clock. As this idea moves into clinical trials, a high-profile retraction reveals the ups and downs of circadian medicine.

papers.title: Conversational brain AI for adaptive epilepsy care
papers.abstract: A small study shows that patients can help fine-tune their own seizure detectors by chatting with an AI agent. However, the more difficult challenge ahead is to build AI that responds appropriately.

papers.title: EGFR-targeted antibody−toxin conjugate in recurrent glioma: a phase 1 trial
papers.abstract: Results of a phase 1 trial of the antibody−toxin conjugate D2C7-ATC targeting EGFR/EGFRvIII in patients with recurrent malignant glioma show encouraging safety and efficacy signals, with translational analyses of patient samples indicating intratumoral and systemic immune activation.

papers.title: Real-world, digital-first delivery of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in women
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated substantial weight reduction and cardiometabolic benefit in randomized trials; however, prospective implementation evidence from digital care models and female sex community populations remains limited. Here we report outcomes from an observational study of 8,127 women initiating GLP-1RA therapy (99.8% tirzepatide) through a structured digital program incorporating mandatory biochemical monitoring, weekly video-supported follow-up and clinician-guided dose titration in the UK. Mean weight reduction was 16.1 kg (95% confidence interval 15.9 to 16.2; P − 1 (95% confidence interval 3.1 to 3.4; P − 1 , low-density lipoprotein cholesterol of 0.61 mmol l − 1 and triglycerides of 0.47 mmol l − 1 ). Retention was 91.4% at 6 months, with no serious treatment-related adverse events. These findings support the feasibility of delivering structured, digitally enabled obesity pharmacotherapy at scale and provide prospective real-world implementation evidence for this care model. Interpretation is limited by the observational design, absence of a comparator group, self-pay population and 6-month follow-up.

papers.title: Recent developments of fluorescent proteins and biosensors driven by cross-disciplinary insights
papers.abstract: This Review summarizes recent developments in fluorescent protein technology, including the engineering of fluorescent biosensors.

papers.title: AmpliconSuite: an end-to-end workflow for analyzing focal amplifications in cancer genomes
papers.abstract: Here we present AmpliconSuite, a toolkit for focal amplification analysis from cancer whole-genome sequencing that identifies extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), breakage–fusion–bridges and other amplification modes. Its ecContext module categorizes ecDNA structures to understand formation mechanisms. Validation across 175 metaphase fluorescence in situ hybridization-probed genes in 72 models demonstrated accurate predictions. Analysis of 6,506 patient pan-cancer samples revealed ecDNA-mediated oncogene co-amplification preferences. To democratize data sharing, we created AmpliconRepository, a community-contributable platform, enabling investigation of results across >15,000 publicly hosted samples.

papers.title: NAD+ precursor treatment prevents cardiomyopathy but disrupts erythroid maturation in mitochondrial progeria
Stereochemical preorganization directs triple-helical assembly of Au 4 nanoclusters
papers.abstract: Translating local stereochemical information into higher-order helical architectures is a central challenge in materials design. Now it has been shown that stereochemically preorganized Au4 nanoclusters assemble into homochiral triple helices through directional aurophilic interactions, providing a design strategy for chiral nanocluster materials with amplified chiroptical responses.

papers.title: Unidirectional rotation in a molecular motor driven by angular-momentum transfer via helical orbitals
papers.abstract: Molecular motors typically rotate by cycling through excitation and relaxation to ground states. Now it has been shown that a molecular motor can be driven by angular-momentum transfer. Circulating positive and negative currents flowing through orbitals of opposite helicity along a carbon–carbon triple bond enable unidirectional rotation.

papers.title: Neoplastic and non-neoplastic astrocyte states converge on mesenchymal and injury-response programs during glioblastoma recurrence
papers.abstract: Lindgren et al. profile murine glioblastoma progression from healthy brain through post-radiotherapy recurrence. Non-neoplastic astrocytes and tumor cells converge on a shared reactive, injury-response program. Irradiation enriches tumor cells with a reactive astrocyte-like state that persists at relapse, signals via Gas6/AXL, and associates with poor patient survival.

papers.title: Lymphangiogenesis driven by VEGF-C reshapes tumor immune landscape and enables tumor eradication by viral immunotherapy in mouse melanoma models
papers.abstract: Fernandez-Rodriguez et al. show that VEGF-C enhances the effects of APMV viral immunotherapy, leading to eradication of tumors and lymph node metastases and long-term survival. VEGF-C promotes lymphangiogenesis, increases T cell accumulation, and cooperates with APMV to enhance NK/NKT cell and T cell effector responses, inducing durable anti-tumor immunological memory.

Elevated prenatal IL-6 levels disrupt early patterns of hippocampal electrical activity and chloride homeostasis by targeting GABAergic signaling at perinatal stage
papers.abstract: Early patterns of neuronal electrical activity are fundamental for driving critical developmental processes, including neuronal maturation and synapse formation. While genetic programs are key in orchestrating these events, the influence of environmental stressors remains poorly defined. Maternal immune activation (MIA) during pregnancy induces a systemic cytokine surge that can profoundly impact fetal brain development, increasing the risk of psychiatric and neurodevelopmental disorders. Here, we show that maternal elevation of interleukin-6 (IL-6) – a key cytokine upregulated during MIA – perturbs early hippocampal electrical activity in male offspring during the first postnatal week, a critical window for circuit formation. By triggering a STAT3-dependent modulation of early GABAergic synaptic transmission, IL-6 disrupts chloride homeostasis, causing a premature shift in the developmental GABA polarity switch. Our findings reveal a direct link between maternal immune signaling and early GABA-driven network maturation, providing insights into how inflammatory events during pregnancy may predispose male offspring to neurodevelopmental disorders.

Machine-learning surrogates enable rapid prediction of 3-D substrate gradients in industrial bioreactors
papers.abstract: High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) provide detailed substrate gradient predictions in industrial stirred-tank bioreactors but are computationally intensive, limiting their routine application. We developed surrogate models trained on $$760$$ 760 CFD simulations to rapidly predict fully 3-D substrate concentration fields from global operating conditions (e.g., stirring speed, feeding strategy, feeding point location, fluid density and viscosity, liquid height, bio-kinetic parameters, biomass concentration), and local spatial descriptors (e.g., distance to the feeding point). Among various methods, attention-based neural networks achieved the highest accuracy (test $${{{\rm{R}}}}^{2}\approx 0.91$$ R 2 ≈ 0.91 ), capturing essential mixing features and enabling millisecond-scale inference—up to a million-fold speed-up compared to CFD. These surrogates facilitate rapid exploration of operating spaces, supporting real-time optimization and digital-twin frameworks in bioprocessing. Our results demonstrate that data-driven models can effectively couple hydrodynamics and biokinetics to provide fast, accurate spatial predictions, advancing capabilities for industrial bioreactor design and control.

FKS1/2-variant independent mechanisms underlying the emergence of resistance in echinocandin-refractory Candida auris infections
papers.abstract: The emerging fungus Candida auris is a drug resistant global public health threat and WHO critical priority pathogen. Recommended first-line invasive candidiasis treatment is echinocandin monotherapy, but C. auris can develop on-treatment resistance via FKS1/2 gene mutations and additional, previously unexplained mechanisms. To better understand echinocandin failure in C. auris , we sequenced the genomes of echinocandin refractory FKS1/2 wild-type C. auris serial isolates from two critically unwell patients in London, UK. Population analysis profiling revealed echinocandin heteroresistance, and in vitro culture of clinical isolates at supra-MIC concentrations of anidulafungin (8 μg/ml) exhibited morphotypic heterogeneity. Small colony variants (SCVs) and large colony variants (LCVs) showed elevated MICs with polyploidy (to 4n and above) alongside adaptive changes in cell wall β−1,3-glucan content. LCVs contained significantly more mutations in calcineurin-related stress tolerance pathway gene CRZ1 compared to clinical parents and SCVs, associated with further increases in MIC. These findings indicate progressive step-wise accrual of adaptation to echinocandins, including genomic instability, alterations in stress tolerance pathways, and cell wall remodelling, paving the way for resistance emergence.

papers.title: Electric fields control static charge during contact-friction-separation
papers.abstract: Contact electrification occurs when two materials rub against one another. This is either a problem, such as when charge builds up during powder processing, or an exploited phenomenon to harvest energy, as is the case in triboelectric nanogenerators. However, why contact electrification occurs remains a topic of hot debate, with ions, adsorbates, electrons and combinations thereof being ascribed the charge carriers. Irrespective of the charge carrier however, there must be a driving force inducing charge to separate and move from one surface to another. Herein, we demonstrate that electric fields, either applied externally or spontaneously generated at an interface can completely alter and even invert surface charge measured after contact electrification in polymer-polymer contact. Applying an external electric field allows the direct control of both magnitude and polarity static charge on dielectric polymers. These results are coupled to simulations that show the applied electric field is on the order of the fields generated by the flexoelectric effect – providing prima facie evidence of flexoelectric driven contact electrification.

papers.title: Klebsiella-dominant gut communities are associated with impeded oral rotavirus vaccine response in infants
papers.abstract: Rotavirus gastroenteritis is the leading cause of infant diarrheal death worldwide. Oral rotavirus vaccine (RVV) prevents illness and death, but efficacy differs between high- and low-income countries and the etiologies are unclear. Here, we describe the relationship between colonization of the infant gut by commensal bacteria, inflammation, and vaccine response across a cohort of infants from Panama, Peru, and the U.S. Vaccine immunogenicity was related to community composition in the first month of life and inverse to increased relative abundance of Klebsiella . Clustering communities into gut types revealed that microbiome configurations with elevated Klebsiella or Escherichia in the first month of life were negatively associated with both seroconversion and rotavirus shedding after vaccination, suggesting potential inhibition of vaccine function or host response. Infants without RVV strain shedding displayed elevated fecal calprotectin in the first month. These results implicate microbiome-augmented infant gut inflammation as a potential impediment to RVV response.

papers.title: Active crustal straining and fault reactivation at Valles Marineris
papers.abstract: Tectonic deformation on stagnant-lid planets reflects the interaction between long-lived lithospheric structures and evolving stress fields. Whether the ancient tectonic fabrics can localise present-day seismic failure under contemporary stress fields remains poorly tested by direct geophysical observations. Here we show that the farside seismic event, S0976a, detected by InSight in the western hemisphere is a marsquake that occurred in Valles Marineris and involved strike-slip faulting in the deep crust. The stress orientation inferred from the focal mechanism is consistent with reactivation of pre-existing fault systems under a present-day stress field shaped primarily by long-term planetary cooling, regional Tharsis-related loading, and surface erosion-related local unloading. These observations provide direct seismic evidence that inherited fault systems on Mars can remain mechanically favourable for reactivation over billion-year timescales, suggesting that slip on deeply rooted faults remains a key mechanism of long-term strain release in a cooling single-lid planet.

Closed-loop upcycling of residual lithium in LiFePO4 into tunable thin lithium metal electrodes
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of electric vehicles, massive quantities of spent lithium iron phosphate batteries are generated, creating an urgent demand for efficient and sustainable recycling. Here we show a redox mediator-assisted strategy that directly converts simulated spent lithium iron phosphate powder into thin lithium metal, reducing energy requirements and enabling regeneration of the redox mediator. The process achieves a 98% final lithium extraction and produces lithium foils with a preformed interphase, tolerating volume changes and resisting air corrosion. The recycled Li (4.14 mAh cm −2 ) enables Li | |Li cells to cycle over 1,200 h at the test condition of 1 mA cm −2 / 1 mAh cm −2 and shows stable interfacial resistance with reduced electrolyte decomposition. When paired with NCM811, the cells retain 91.4% capacity over 400 cycles at 0.2 C/0.3 C. This closed-loop process couples lithium recovery with designed electrode fabrication, providing an alternative pathway for sustainable battery recycling and negative electrode design.

papers.title: Divergent asymmetric synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy
papers.abstract: Natural products are of substantial value in drug discovery screening campaigns. Their three-dimensional structures exhibit high complementarity with target proteins, via a multimodal combination of hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic contacts, electrostatic interactions, and van der Waals interactions. Skeletal diversity directly determines the three-dimensional shape diversity of compound libraries. Therefore, the rapid access to distinct molecular skeletons significantly increases the odds of drug discovery. Ganocins A–C and cochlearol B, Ganoderma meroterpenoids, feature distinct skeletons and diverse bioactivities. Despite tremendous efforts by synthetic chemists, a unified asymmetric synthetic strategy towards all four members has remained elusive. Here, we report the unified, asymmetric total synthesis of (–)-ganocins A–C and (+)-cochlearol B via a non-biomimetic strategy, featuring diastereoselective oxa-Michael addition, acid-controlled divergent cascade aldol/etherification cyclization or aldol/dehydration, and SmI 2 -mediated 4- exo -trig reductive cross-coupling. This meticulously designed synthetic strategy establishes a general solution to a problem previously deemed intractable by biomimetic approaches.

papers.title: Uhrf1 loss disrupts CTCF-associated chromatin organization during early mouse embryogenesis
Dendritic computation bridges neuroscience and foundation models
Polarization-controlled Floquet engineering in twisted photonic lattices
papers.abstract: Floquet engineering has emerged as a powerful approach for both classical and quantum systems, enabling versatile exploration of synthetic dimensions, topological phases, and quantum information processing. Further advances, however, require precise and continuous control over both the magnitude and sign of the coupling coefficient. Although static modal-engineering approaches can tune both, existing Floquet photonic platforms typically rely on geometric modulation, auxiliary structures, or phase engineering. Continuous tuning of the coupling coefficient in both magnitude and sign within a Floquet period therefore remains challenging. Here, we present a compact Floquet platform based on twisted photonic waveguide arrays, in which the twist-induced variation of the relative polarization angle between adjacent waveguides directly tunes the coupling coefficient through zero, allowing continuous access to positive and negative values with different magnitudes. To highlight the core capability of the platform, we focus on representative driven phenomena in both one- and two-dimensional lattices: Floquet flat bands and the associated period-n $$\Lambda$$ Λ oscillations in one-dimensional lattices, as well as chirality reversal of topological edge states in two-dimensional lattices.

papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by motor neuron (MN) loss caused by early axonal and synaptic changes. However, the mechanisms underlying these changes remain incompletely understood. Here, we exploit FUS-ALS to interrogate cell compartment-specific changes in RNA expression and regulation in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived MN. This approach identifies compartment-specific 3’ untranslated region (3’UTR) isoform expression in human healthy control MN axons. Further, it unveils altered 3’ UTR isoforms in ALS in different cellular compartments in genes such as SNCA , previously linked to neurodegeneration. Expression of SLITRK2 is most strongly and consistently upregulated across multiple FUS-ALS models, and its knockdown normalizes axonal defects linked to FUS-ALS. Using a fully iPSC-derived neuromuscular microfluidics protocol, we show that SLITRK2 knockdown in FUS-ALS MN rescues neuromuscular junction (NMJ) signaling without affecting NMJ innervation or MN hypo-excitability. Our study provides insight into compartment-specific 3’UTR expression in ALS, presents a robust iNMJ-on-a-chip model, and links elevated SLITRK2 to axonal and synaptic defects in FUS-ALS.

cPRIME enables endogenous mapping of genetic variant effects at RNA level
papers.abstract: Understanding the functional consequences of genetic variants, particularly those classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS), is a major challenge in genomics. While variant effects at protein level are well recognized, roles in post-transcriptional regulation are increasingly appreciated. Here, we introduce cPRIME (prime editing with cDNA readout), a scalable method for assessing variant effects at RNA level. cPRIME employs prime editing to insert genetic variants into endogenous genomic loci, followed by the quantification of changes in variant frequencies at RNA (cDNA) and genomic DNA (gDNA) level. We demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse karyotypes and genomic loci and reveal that synonymous marker edits - frequently used in prime editing screens - can themselves alter RNA processing and thereby confound the interpretation of variant effects. Taken together, cPRIME provides a platform for studying the post-transcriptional consequences of genetic variants in their genomic context and establishes a framework for the functional interpretation of RNA-altering variants in cancer and other diseases.

USP28 potentiates endothelial necroptosis via deubiquitinating NMMHC IIA in septic male mice
papers.abstract: Endothelial dysfunction contributes to multi-organ injury in sepsis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here we show that endothelial ubiquitin-specific protease 28 (USP28) is increased in patients with sepsis and in male mice in a murine polymicrobial sepsis model. Mechanistically, USP28 stabilizes non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA (NMMHC IIA) by removing K48-linked ubiquitination at K1413. Moreover, NMMHC IIA promotes interferon-α/β receptor 1 (IFNAR1) trafficking to the plasma membrane, enhancing IFNAR1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) signaling and endothelial necroptosis. In turn, STAT1 transcriptionally increases USP28 expression, forming a positive feedback loop. Endothelial USP28 deletion or pharmacological inhibition attenuates sepsis-induced multi-organ injury, whereas USP28 overexpression exacerbates it. Conversely, endothelial NMMHC IIA or IFNAR1 overexpression largely abrogates the protection conferred by USP28 deficiency in septic male mice. These findings identify a USP28–NMMHC IIA axis that promotes endothelial necroptosis and multi-organ injury in sepsis through IFNAR1/STAT1 signaling.

Single Staphylococcus aureus SauUSI restriction enzyme motors fragment methylated DNA
papers.abstract: SauUSI is a dimeric, ATP-dependent type IV restriction enzyme that protects Staphylococcus aureus by cleaving nonself DNA containing 5-methylcytosine or 5-hydroxymethylcytosine. Using biophysical, single-molecule and nanopore sequencing methods, we show that 5-methylcytosine recognition first induces ATP-driven unidirectional translocation by one helicase-like subunit, displacing its target recognition domain (TRD). In half of events, the partner TRD can then bind the liberated modified site, stabilizing a growing DNA loop. On symmetrically methylated DNA, looping is more frequent and both motors can engage in bidirectional loop translocation. Cleavage occurs stochastically throughout translocation but events that increase dwell time such as rebinding methylated sites elevate the chance of cleavage. Interactions with other SauUSI dimers or protein roadblocks influence cleavage distributions but are not required for nuclease activation. While the first cleavages principally generate 1-nt 3ʹ overhangs or blunt ends, multiple binding–translocation–cleavage cycles by individual enzymes ultimately fragment the modified nonself DNA, neutralizing its threat.

papers.title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal’s assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing’s most important challenges.

papers.abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. papers.title: Gate-tunable chiral spin mode in WSe 2 /WS 2 moiré superlattices
papers.abstract: The interplay between many-body and spin-orbit coupling (SOC) effects can lead to previously unobserved phenomena in solids. Chiral spin modes (CSMs) are collective spin excitations that arise from such interplay and connect states with opposite chirality. Here, we report a gate-tunable CSM that occurs between conduction SOC-split minibands in near-0°-twisted WSe 2 /WS 2 bilayers. This mode manifests as a sharp resonance with giant Raman efficiency in the pseudovector-symmetry channel of the Raman spectra. By varying the filling, the CSM transitions from a chiral spin exciton to an excitonic polaron. The spin-flip nature is directly confirmed by the Zeeman effect, and the filling dependence indicates a charge-transfer insulator at unity filling. Our results demonstrate that transition metal–dichalcogenide moiré superlattices are a fertile platform for exploring exotic low-lying collective excitations.

papers.title: Frequency encoding regulates cell type composition in the small intestine
papers.abstract: Intestinal homeostasis requires tight regulation of stem cell maintenance and differentiation to absorptive and secretory cell types, two major intestinal lineages. Key signaling pathways have been identified, but how they balance cell type composition remains unclear. We uncovered oscillatory expression of the Notch-target protein Hes1 (hairy and enhancer of split 1) that controls cell fate specification in a frequency-dependent manner. An endogenous fluorescent Hes1 reporter revealed distinct, cell type–specific oscillation frequencies forming a gradient along the crypt-villus axis, which was modulated by cell cycle phase as well as Wnt (wingless-related integration site)–signaling and Notch-signaling activity. We developed a microfluidic system to modulate Notch-signaling oscillations in organoids and found the oscillation frequency to regulate the balance of cell type composition. This study provides evidence that information for cell fate specification is encoded in the frequency of an oscillatory signal.

papers.title: A pair of chitosan receptors confer broad-spectrum fungal resistance
papers.abstract: Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane–localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression of OsFID1 in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.

papers.title: Structural basis for size-selective perception of chitin in plants
papers.abstract: Plants detect microbes through pattern recognition receptors that perceive conserved microbial surface motifs known as microbe-associated molecular patterns (MAMPs). Lysin motif (LysM) receptors recognize and mediate downstream responses to chitinous MAMPs. In this study, we elucidated the mechanism for the specific recognition of long-chain chitin oligomers and identified a hallmark bridge domain characteristic of the CHITIN PERCEPTION (CHIP) receptor class. Structural analysis of receptor-ligand complexes, biochemistry, and in planta functional studies of inhibitory nanobodies revealed the mechanism of size-selective, high-affinity chitin perception in Lotus japonicus and Medicago truncatula . Additionally, we identified the CHITIN ELICITOR RECEPTOR KINASE (CERK) class as low-affinity, yet essential, co-receptors and propose a mechanistic model for a ligand-induced core signaling heterocomplex. Our findings establish the structural and mechanistic basis of differential chitin perception and receptor complex assembly in chitin-elicited plant immune signaling.

papers.title: Regulation of target gene expression by chromatin-associated protein-coding transcripts in plants
papers.abstract: Protein-coding transcripts are regarded as intermediates that mediate DNA-to-protein information flow, leaving their noncoding regulatory potential largely underappreciated. Genome-wide profiling of RNA–chromatin interactions in Arabidopsis has uncovered widespread associations between protein-coding transcripts and distinct genomic loci, implying that they possess regulatory functions. Here, we found that BT2 and GSL8 transcripts modulate target gene transcription independently of their protein products through distinct mechanisms. The BT2 transcript represses transcription of its targets CEP2 and MRF4 by forming RNA–DNA triplexes, thereby restricting root growth and promoting flowering, whereas GSL8 acts through a triplex-independent pathway. Our findings unveil intrinsic regulatory activities of protein-coding transcripts, challenging the canonical definition of mRNA function and blurring the functional distinction between coding and noncoding RNAs in the context of genome evolution.

papers.title: Dendritic computation for abstract rule-based flexible decision-making
papers.abstract: Intelligent behavior involves flexible integration of sensory input and abstract rule knowledge. Dendritic computation has been shown to contribute to top-down modulation of sensory processing; however, whether and how it is involved in flexible cognitive processing remains to be elucidated. Combining a rule-based flexible decision-making task with in vivo two-photon imaging and optogenetics in mice, we found that within single layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the auditory cortex, apical dendrites preferentially encoded the inferred abstract rule and somata preferentially represented sensory stimuli, whereas choice signals were present in both compartments. Optogenetic dendritic inhibition impaired rule-dependent somatic choice coding, supporting a task-relevant integration across the dendritic and somatic compartments. These results indicate that dendritic computation in cortical neurons mediates flexible behavior.

papers.title: Empirical constraints on ice cliff calving
papers.abstract: When calving cliffs at the margins of Earth’s ice sheets exceed a critical height, runaway retreat may be initiated in a process called the marine ice cliff instability. However, sufficiently tall ice cliffs have rarely been observed. To address this gap, we measured the characteristics of 15,330 ice cliffs across Earth’s ice sheet margins using laser altimetry. We show that cliff height is highly correlated with mélange thickness, water depth, and crevassing. We found that tall cliffs calve more rapidly than parameterizations assume, but dynamic thinning and retreat into regions with low ice thickness gradients prevent runaway retreat. These observations suggest that model projections may underestimate subannual rates of cliff calving, but that the potential for instability will depend sensitively on additional quantities, not cliff height alone.

papers.title: Airflows redefine the cost of aerial transport in the wild
papers.abstract: Fuel economy matters to both animals and machines, as the cost of transport can determine where, when, and how far locomotion is possible. However, established estimates of these values for animal flight come from laboratories and treat the atmosphere as constant, even though free-flying animals routinely extract energy from atmospheric flows. Using high-resolution movement data, we estimate the cost of transport for 50 bird and bat species flying in the wild. Our results revise the classic ranking of locomotion costs, suggesting that flying can be cheaper than swimming though almost as costly as running, depending on interactions between physical environment, morphology, and behavior. Linking transport costs to atmospheric conditions provides a mechanistic basis for predicting how changing windscapes will reshape the energetics, movements, and distributions of flying animals.

papers.title: Engineering ordered two-dimensional defect phases to strengthen structural alloys
papers.abstract: Defects in crystals are usually considered to be consequences of deformation, but they can also be engineered as strengthening features. Planar defects can strengthen structural alloys but usually form only during deformation or service, limiting control over their density, stability, and chemistry. We show that predeformation followed by aging can convert such defects into a designed architecture of ordered defect phases. In a single-crystal cobalt-nickel–based superalloy and a polycrystalline cobalt-chromium-tungsten alloy, this treatment creates dense networks of coherent, atomically thin, ordered defect–confined phases. These increase room-temperature strength by more than 200 megapascals and reduce the superalloy’s minimum creep rate by more than threefold. Electron microscopy and simulations show that local chemical ordering amplifies strengthening and that the ordered defect phases remain shearable while impeding slip transmission.

papers.title: Electrically driven chiral emission from plasmonic tunnel junctions
papers.abstract: Chirality plays a crucial role in a broad range of processes, including light-matter interactions in physics, chemistry, and biology, while quantum tunneling provides a promising mechanism for light generation at the nanoscale. By integrating tunnel junctions with chiral plasmonic nanohelicoids, we achieved electrically induced nanoscale generation of chiral light at the single-particle level. The tunneling-driven resonant excitation of chiral dipolar modes of the nanohelicoids results in emission of a vortex light beam possessing both spin angular momentum with handedness selectivity of more than 0.8 and orbital angular momentum equal in magnitude and opposite in sign. Our electrically driven approach offers a means for engineering photon spin generation at the nanoscale, highlighting its potential for next-generation optical components in display applications, as well as quantum information processing and photochemistry.

papers.title: Deterministic generation and distribution of genuine multipartite entanglement in macroscopic acoustic resonators
papers.abstract: Generating complex multimode entanglement is a central goal of quantum information science. However, scalable creation of genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging as it requires excellent control and efficient state verification. We report the generation and transfer of genuine multimode entanglement across two multimode acoustic resonators. We prepare genuine multipartite entangled states involving two, four, and six modes across the resonators with respective fidelities of 0.912 ± 0.003, 0.790 ± 0.003, and 0.570 ± 0.001. We further demonstrate the transfer of two- and four-mode genuine entangled states between the resonators with fidelities of 0.785 ± 0.006 and 0.601 ± 0.006. This hardware-efficient and scalable architecture enables deterministic control and generation of complex multimode mechanical states. Our results push the boundary of quantum control in macroscopic mechanical systems, establishing a pathway toward large-scale mechanical quantum networks.

papers.title: Modular van der Waals MOSFETs through layer-by-layer chalcogen substitutions
papers.abstract: In two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), the local electrostatic field of the chalcogen p -orbitals dictates the crystal field splitting of the transition metal d -orbitals, stabilizing diverse electronic states from semiconducting and semimetallic to exotic topological phases. On-demand substitution of the lattice chalcogens is therefore an efficient route to tuning TMDC electronic phases. Here, we custom-molded van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures by layer-by-layer vapor-phase chalcogen substitution starting from p -type WSe 2 multilayers into which we locally inscribed insulating WO x , n -type WS 2 , and semimetallic WTe 2 . This spatially precise conversion seamlessly integrated distinct electronic phases, both vertically and laterally, into modular vdW semiconductor heterostructures that are otherwise inaccessible. As a demonstration, we integrated WO x /WSe 2 local gate stacks to build ultrascaled metal oxide–semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFETs), achieving an unprecedented subthreshold swing at subnanometer equivalent oxide thickness.
