Integrated multi-omics identifies distinct immune signatures with diagnostic and therapeutic implications in immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myocarditis
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-myocarditis) is a rare but frequently fatal immune-related adverse event. A comprehensive understanding of the cellular and molecular determinants driving ICI-myocarditis is essential for improving diagnostic precision and developing targeted interventions. We delineate the immune landscape of ICI-myocarditis via scRNA-seq, flow cytometry, Olink proteomics, and multiplex cytokine profiling. We demonstrate that high levels of baseline ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells are linked to the proinflammatory features of monocytes and in vitro experiments confirm the existence of circulating ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells with a high potential to induce cardiomyocyte apoptosis, supporting their pathogenic potential for cardiomyocyte cytotoxicity. Notably, intercellular crosstalk between these subsets is possibly mediated via the CCL2-CCR2 axis, and its blockade attenuated ICI-induced cardiac injury in vivo. Based on the inflammatory signature in ICI-myocarditis, we develop an 8-protein custom panel with promising performance in distinguishing ICI-myocarditis from other ICIs-treated controls. JAK-STAT pathway activation promotes inflammatory programs in both ISG15⁺CD8⁺ T cells and monocytes. Furthermore, JAK-STAT inhibition ameliorates cardiac dysfunction and inflammatory infiltration while enhancing the response to anti-PD-1 therapy in mouse models. In summary, this study implicates immune-pathogenic features of ICI-myocarditis and provides a possible basis for future therapies.

papers.title: Enhancing ω-transaminase catalysis of bulky substrates guided by binding mechanism
papers.abstract: This study combines enhanced sampling with experiments to reveal how bulky substrates enter and bind to ω-transaminases. Distal-site engineering balanced tunnel access and binding stability, yielding 106-fold activity and >99% selectivity.

papers.title: Orientation tomography of lanthanide-doped nanoprobes by polarization-resolved micro-spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Quantifying three-dimensional (3D) orientation is critical for understanding self-assembly and collective behavior in soft matter and biological systems. Moreover, orientational analysis of anisotropic particles can characterize locally applied forces in fluids. We present a methodology for 3D orientation tomography based on polarization-resolved spectroscopy of lanthanide-doped nanorods exhibiting multiple emission dipoles, enabling 3D orientation measurements from a single viewing angle. We develop a confocal imaging setup optimized for lanthanide luminescence and a theoretical framework to extract both the local director and order parameter in nanorod assemblies. The technique achieves 0.5 μm lateral and 1 μm axial spatial resolution and is demonstrated in dense nematic liquid-crystal assemblies, resolving complex 3D topological structures, and in microfluidic flows, mapping alignment under hydrodynamic shear. This approach provides a versatile platform for quantitative studies of collective orientation, self-assembly mechanics, and alignment induced by external forces, and can be extended to other lanthanide-labeled particles and molecular probes.

papers.title: A nanosystem manipulates angiocrine signaling for cardioprotection in male mice by relocalizing endothelial exosomes
papers.abstract: Acute myocardial ischemia induces the release of endothelial exosomes with cardioprotective effect. Here, the authors show that a nanosystem relocalizes circulating endothelial exosomes to ischemic myocardium, increasing local exposure and preserving cardiac function

papers.title: Bioinspired nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides for treating comorbid anxiety and depression in inflammatory bowel disease
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic condition frequently accompanied by psychological comorbidities, such as anxiety and depression. Although current treatments may alleviate some of these symptoms, the intricate pathogenesis of these comorbidities highlights an urgent need for therapeutic strategies with combined anti-inflammatory, barrier-reparative, and microbiota-modulating effects. Herein, we develop a series of nanozyme-exoskeletonized yeast-derived polysaccharides (NZEP) by integrating nanozymes with yeast-derived polysaccharides using an insect sclerotization-inspired strategy. Among them, NZEP TA-Ce , with the highest degree of nanozyme-exoskeletonization, is capable of disrupting the inflammatory vicious cycle by inhibiting MAPK and NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling pathways. Oral administration of NZEP TA-Ce in mice enables effective retention and accumulation in inflamed colonic regions, reverses the homeostasis imbalance of intestinal inflammation and promotes intestinal barrier repair. Furthermore, NZEP TA-Ce treatment reverses gut microbiota dysbiosis and optimizes the composition of microbial metabolites, thereby alleviating anxiety and depressive symptoms associated with IBD. This study provides a safe and promising therapeutic strategy for the management of IBD patients and their associated psychological comorbidities.

papers.title: Luminal geometry and coiled coil length determine submembrane localization of type II transmembrane Golgi proteins
papers.abstract: Wong et al. show that the intraluminal widths of the ER and Golgi and the length of luminal coiled coils of the transmembrane proteins determine localization, revealing a geometry-based localization mechanism.

papers.title: From ancient practice to modern innovation solving the clay mineral puzzle in brickmaking
papers.abstract: Clay minerals are the most crucial constituents in brickmaking clays, yet the specific role of different clay minerals remain poorly understood due to their natural coexistence and formidable challenges of separation. Here, we design a kaolinite-illite-quartz-feldspar system through a multiple-stage purification strategy, enabling direct evaluation of two of the most critical clay minerals for brick making - kaolinite and illite. Precise tuning the initial clay mineral assemblage yields brick strengths up to 8.5 times the ASTM C62 Grade MW requirement, without upgrading existing production methods. Mineralogical mechanisms responsible for substantial strength enhancement are revealed. Extensive analyses of 60 brick formulations uncovered a breakdown of conventional linear relationships among different brick properties due to the temperature-dependent responses of kaolinite and illite; specific formation pathways of mullite and amorphous phases; and over-firing defects above 1200 °C due to K + -induced fluxing from illite. Notably, a previously unrecognized negative correlation between mullite and brick strength is identified, suggesting a need to reconsider the widely held assumption of mullite as a strengthening phase. This work not only presents insights for optimizing high-strength brick formulations but also opens avenues for investigating the intricate contributions of distinct starting components to key brick performance.

papers.title: Spontaneous ferromagnetic Fe–La geminal atoms with spin and coordination modulation for acidic oxygen reduction
papers.abstract: Developing robust Fe–N–C catalysts that unite activity and durability remains challenging for acidic oxygen reduction. Here, the authors report spontaneous ferromagnetic Fe–La geminal atoms that create high-spin Fe sites and a spin pinning effect for fuel-cell catalysis.

papers.title: Hemispheric asymmetry in predicted range shifts of anti-tropical fish under future climate change
papers.abstract: As oceans warm unevenly between hemispheres, the future of anti-tropical fishes is unclear. Despite larger future range contractions for northern lineages, protected area efficacy remains unchanged and significantly higher for southern lineages.

papers.title: Personalized neoantigen-targeting cancer vaccines in ovarian cancer: a phase 1 trial
papers.abstract: A phase 1 trial shows that treatment of patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer with personalized neoantigen vaccines combined with PD-1 blockade was feasible and led to tumor-specific immune responses in many patients and putative mechanisms of resistance related to antigen presentation were identified via cell-free DNA analysis.

papers.title: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide in high-volume metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer: a randomized phase 2 trial
papers.abstract: In the randomized multicenter phase 2 ZZ-FIRST trial, patients with high-volume metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer treated with poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor talazoparib combined with androgen receptor inhibitor enzalutamide had an improved prostate-specific antigen response compared with enzalutamide alone, and spatial transcriptomic analyses of paired biopsies linked AR inhibition-induced suppression of HRR-related programs to proliferation arrest rather than functional HRR deficiency.

papers.title: Stroke-induced astrocyte memories promote glioma progression
papers.abstract: The impact of earlier brain insults on the glioblastoma microenvironment is poorly understood. A study now shows that prior stroke alters astrocytes to promote glioblastoma growth and invasion via downregulation of calcium signaling.

papers.title: Reframing cancer therapy through tumor plasticity
papers.abstract: de Sauvage and colleagues discuss the latest advances in therapy-driven cancer plasticity processes and how this knowledge might be applied to clinical strategies.

papers.title: Peptide signaling in the paraventricular thalamus is essential for disrupted adult reward behaviors consequent to early-life adversity
papers.abstract: Floriou-Servou et al. analyze reward-induced active gene translation in paraventricular thalamus (PVT) cells that are selectively activated during early-life adversity and find a role of Crhr1. By deleting Crhr1, they demonstrate that CRH-CRHR1 signaling in PVT contributes crucially to early-stress-induced anhedonia in males and hyper-motivation in females for rewards.

papers.title: Mitochondrial stress induces transcription of cytosolic and mitochondrial protein synthesis components via NHR-180
papers.abstract: Mallick et al. show that mitochondrial dysfunction increases NHR-180 levels and nuclear localization in C. elegans, consistent with NHR-180’s role in mitochondrial stress responses. Inhibition of NHR-180 or S6K improves mitochondrial function in C. elegans mitochondrial mutants, while S6K inhibition also enhances mitochondrial function in mammalian cells with mitochondrial mutations.

papers.title: NONO mitigates transcription-replication conflicts during replication stress by restraining BRD4-dependent transcription elongation
papers.abstract: Replication stress triggers TRCs via dormant origin firing. Wu et al. show that NONO-BRD4 condensates block paused RNAP2 release to restrain stress-induced TRCs, whereas NONO loss derepresses elongation, aggravating TRCs and genomic instability.

papers.title: FDA new drug approvals in Q3 2026
A mysterious jelly seems to be left behind by toads
Inundated AI conferences impose submissions caps
Whistleblowing in universities is ‘extraordinarily risky’: stronger protections are needed
Diversify Nobel-prize nominations before it’s too late

Selective, Catalytic Oxidation of Polyethylene Surfaces
Author Correction: Parkinson’s disease as a somato-cognitive action network disorder
Can GLP-1s heal the brain? Obesity drugs get a makeover for addiction and depression
Lead-tainted teeth reveal medieval mines’ unequal toll
Current aviation roadmaps are not within planetary boundaries
papers.abstract: Aviation decarbonization roadmaps predominantly rely on replacing fossil kerosene with alternative jet fuels, yet the systemic impact of these alternatives on planetary boundaries other than climate change has not been quantified. Here we integrate prospective life-cycle inventories with the planetary boundaries framework to evaluate the absolute impacts of aviation roadmaps as time-dependent trajectories, rather than endpoint snapshots. Across scenarios to 2050, we find that fuel-switch-centered roadmaps do not achieve sustainability, persistently transgress the climate change and biosphere integrity core boundaries, and exert large demands for energy, land, freshwater and CO 2 capture that challenge their feasibility. Slower traffic growth brings aviation closer to its share of the safe operating space in terms of lowering energy demand, but respecting additional planetary boundaries requires air traffic to decline by at least 7.2% yr −1 . Our results show that aligning aviation with Earth’s safe operating space cannot be achieved through fuel substitution alone and requires governance strategies that combine supply-side solutions with explicit demand-side measures.

papers.title: Securing critical rare-earth supply through end-of-life NdFeB magnets recycling via molten salt electrolysis with consumable Mg-cathode
Author Correction: Engineered CRISPR-OsCas12f1 and RhCas12f1 with robust activities and expanded target range for genome editing
Epitaxial-strain engineering of supported tensile noble metallene oxides for enhanced oxidation catalysis
papers.abstract: Supported two-dimensional noble metal oxides (metallene oxides) hold great promise for heterogeneous catalysis owing to their maximized surface exposure and tunable electronic structures. However, their high surface energy and low oxidation potentials make them intrinsically unstable under reaction conditions. Here, we report an epitaxial strain strategy to stabilize and modulate the electronic structure of supported PtO 2 metallene oxide. By employing rutile TiO 2 and rutile SnO 2 supports with distinct lattice parameters, we achieve epitaxial growth of PtO 2 metallene oxide layers with controlled strain states, where the larger-lattice SnO 2 substrate imposes biaxial tensile strain on PtO 2 . The tensile-strained PtO 2 /SnO 2 exhibits a reconfigured Pt–O electronic environment that simultaneously improves structural resilience and enhances the intrinsic reactivity of PtO 2 , delivering markedly improved methane oxidation performance with a T 90 of 370 °C (versus 434 °C for PtO 2 /TiO 2 and 469 °C for PtO x /Al 2 O 3 ) and

papers.title: Population-resolved single-emitter spectroscopy
A multi-stage engineering framework for feasible scheduling of large-scale energy batch transport systems
Colossal visible birefringence and ultraviolet hyperbolicity in wide bandgap semiconductor CuAlO2
Controlled crosslink cleavage and phase separation enable highly stretchable and strong 3D-printed hydrogel for soft robotics
Gamma-alumina as a highly active hydrogenation catalyst deciphered by molecular nitrogen
Disrupting the NAD+/NAM metabolic ratio driven by IL-1β inflammatory response potentiates chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy in mice
Metabolically reprogrammed blastoids from totipotent-like stem cells exhibit enhanced tissue-specific organ-like development and placental formation
Wireless, optoelectronic, multimodal skin sensor for simultaneous monitoring of mechanical stress and vascular responses
CD200+ fibroblasts prime the immunoregulatory function of granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells in inflammatory arthritis
papers.abstract: Granulocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (G-MDSCs) are immunoregulatory cells of the neutrophil lineage. Here, we show that immunoregulation by G-MDSCs is imprinted by the joint tissue microenvironment in patients with axial spondyloarthritis and in animal models of inflammatory arthritis. We demonstrate that the suppressive function of G-MDSCs is significantly enhanced in the joint tissue, but not in the circulation. Analysis of public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets was consistent with Cd200r1 high Hmgb2 + precursors differentiating into G-MDSCs following interaction with Cd200 + fibroblasts. In hTNFtg/ Il23mc mice, treatment with a CD200R1 agonist promoted an immunoregulatory signature associated with PD-L1 expression, whereas CD200 blockade reversed the phenotype. Following adoptive transfer of G-MDSC precursor cells into arthritic mice, administration of a CD200-blocking antibody impaired the differentiation of PD-L1 + G-MDSCs and exacerbated disease severity. These findings reveal a tissue-intrinsic program that facilitates resolution of inflammation through fibroblast-myeloid crosstalk that enhances G-MDSC function.

papers.title: Precise construction of antiparallel-stacked 2D imine covalent organic frameworks for atmospheric water harvesting
High average and linear scaling of Ecological Footprint in cities
Characterizing the onset and progression of cancer cachexia using routine clinical data
papers.abstract: In 52,236 patients with cancer, cachectic weight loss episodes were linked to lower survival rates, occurred at times of disease progression, and carried a consistent serological signature across routine laboratory markers. Specific tumor genotypes, including TP53 mutations, were also positively associated with cachexia risk. Statistical models were trained to predict a patient’s impending risk of cachexia.

papers.title: Autologous and broadly neutralizing antibodies drive ART-free HIV control
papers.abstract: A secondary analysis of trial data shows that both host antibodies and infused antibodies against HIV help to delay viral rebound after interruption of antiretroviral therapy (ART), which could inform approaches to durable, ART-free HIV control.

papers.title: Human–artificial intelligence collaboration for comanaging epilepsy in real time
papers.abstract: A small epilepsy monitoring study shows that a moderated, large language model-based chat interface lets patients converse with their electroencephalography monitoring in real time, using a smartphone, and patient feedback cut seizure-detector false alarms by about 80% without clinician input.

papers.title: Author Correction: Monocyte-derived galectin-1hi cells provide innate immune help in the generation of functional memory CD8+ T cells
Targeting ribosome biogenesis
papers.abstract: New work reveals a small-molecule inhibitor of the human ribosome biogenesis AAA-ATPase NVL that shows high selectivity and anti-proliferative activity. This holds promises for the development of better cancer drugs that target ribosome biogenesis.

papers.title: A selective NVL inhibitor suppresses tumor growth by targeting ribosome biogenesis
papers.abstract: Guo, Tao and Cruz et al. identified a selective inhibitor named MM17 of nuclear valosin-containing protein-like (NVL), an AAA+ ATPase responsible for assembly of large ribosome subunit (60S). A bioavailable derivative, MM927, blocks 60S biogenesis, activates p53 and suppresses tumor growth, suggesting NVL as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Rare k-mers reveal centromere haplogroups underlying human diversity and cancer translocations
papers.abstract: By defining centromere haplogroups from rare k-mer variation, Shiraishi et al. uncover extensive hidden diversity and link centromere structure to human evolution and disease-associated genomic instability.

papers.title: A high-dimensional population code in the bat motor cortex during natural dexterous flight
papers.abstract: Bats use their hand-like wings to reproduce natural flights with wingbeat-level precision. Rather than mainly tracking the wingbeat cycle, the wing motor cortex generates sparse, distinct population states with little shared variance across wingbeats, resulting in a high-dimensional code distinct from that typically observed in constrained tasks.

papers.title: Mechanisms of transcription control by distal enhancers from single-gene nanoscopy
papers.abstract: High-resolution real-time imaging of enhancer-promoter communication reveals how the two genomic loci are actively brought together through cohesin-mediated loop extrusion and how E-P interactions are temporally coordinated with transcriptional bursts. Unexpectedly, components of the RNA Pol II general machinery form nanoscale clusters at distal enhancers, and embedding the promoter into such clusters boosts GTF activities and triggers burst initiation.

papers.title: PTPRS mediates invasion of tetanus neurotoxin into the central nervous system
papers.abstract: Tetanus neurotoxin enters the central nervous system through motor neurons. This study identifies PTPRS as the long-sought retrograde transport receptor that directs toxin trafficking in motor neurons into the spinal cord, uncovering a host pathway that can be targeted for post-exposure treatment and for drug delivery into the central nervous system.

papers.title: The nerve rings twice
Astrocytes go into presenter mode
Multidimensional view of immunotherapy
papers.abstract: The introduction of immune checkpoint blockade revolutionized cancer treatments. Since then, the field of immunotherapy has expanded exponentially, both in therapeutic innovations and applicable disease contexts. Investigators across disciplines discuss how they are reimagining strategies to drive the immune system in contexts of cancer, autoimmunity, and beyond.

papers.title: Viral deISGylation holds the key to the metabolic kingdom
Regulatory B cells: Induced, inspired, and ready to soothe neuroinflammation
The narrow path to CD8+ T cell recognition of mutant p53
The matrix remembers
Transposable element splicing reveals a tumor-enriched class of gene-independent transcripts
papers.abstract: Li et al. systematically map splicing within and between transposable elements (TEs) across cancers and define TEtrans, a tumor-enriched class of gene-independent transcripts. TEtrans display distinct regulatory programs and can function as oncogenic RNAs or encode immunogenic tumor antigens, expanding the functional landscape of TE reactivation in cancer.

papers.title: Structural basis of directionality control in large serine integrases
papers.abstract: Shin et al. present cryo-EM structures of the SPβ integrase along the integration and excision pathways that provide mechanistic insights addressing the long-standing questions of how large serine integrases enforce highly directional DNA recombination and how the cognate recombination directionality factor leads to a complete reversal of directionality.

papers.title: Reverse transcribed ssDNA derepresses translation of a retron antiviral protein
papers.abstract: Retrons help bacteria defend against phage by initiating a toxic response to restrict viral propagation. Here, Zhang et al. describe the non-canonical mechanism of Retron-Vpa2, which accumulates msDNA in response to phage triggers and regulates its toxic response on a translational level through a highly structured hybrid RNA.

papers.title: A feedback mechanism of m6A via PARP1-mediated ADP ribosylation of METTL3/METTL14
papers.abstract: Bai et al. reveal a PARP1-mediated m6A feedback mechanism involving IGF2BPs and the METTL3/METTL14 writer complex. They further show that combined targeting of ADP ribosylation and m6A leads to synergistic anti-tumor effects, providing a potential therapeutic strategy for cancer treatment.

papers.title: Anterior cingulate feedback facilitates rapid global context modulation in primary visual cortex
papers.abstract: Peterka et al. show that sensory processing as early as primary visual cortex is modulated not just by recent stimuli but by learned patterns and global probabilities. They go on to demonstrate that this modulation depends on feedback inputs from a higher brain region, consistent with predictive coding hypotheses.

papers.title: Proprioceptive sensory-driven mechanisms shape Clarke’s column development
papers.abstract: Sensory feedback from muscles does more than report body position—it helps build the circuits that process it. Song et al. find that proprioceptive sensory neurons are required for the postnatal development of Clarke’s column, a key relay carrying movement information from the spinal cord to the cerebellum.

papers.title: USP9X promotes the degradation of trapped translation factors on collided ribosomes
papers.abstract: Teodorowicz et al. show that USP9X, in conjunction with the E3 ligases RNF14 and RNF25, is required to promote the VCP-dependent proteasomal degradation of eRF1 and eEF1A1 trapped in the ribosomal A-site and identify 4EHP as a mediator of translational shutdown following translation factor clearance.

papers.title: Human organ chip models recapitulate FRC-driven high endothelial venule differentiation, immune recruitment, and cancer-induced disruption
papers.abstract: Oh et al. develop human high endothelial venules (HEVs) on a chip, specialized immune-recruiting blood vessels found in lymph nodes. The study shows that FRCs drive HEV specialization and functional T-cell adhesion, while cancer cells disrupt these processes, providing a platform for studying HEV function and dysfunction in disease.

papers.title: Structural basis of an endoplasmic reticulum EMC:Spf1 insertase–dislocase complex
papers.abstract: Most eukaryotic membrane proteins are inserted into the membrane at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). This essential process relies on molecular quality control machineries to prevent mistargeting and incorrect structure formation. Here, we show that the ER membrane protein complex (EMC) forms an evolutionarily conserved supercomplex with the P5A-ATPase Spf1/ATP13A1. Biochemical, structural and cellular analyses demonstrate that the EMC and Spf1 associate in a stoichiometric manner and retain their individual catalytic activities, the transmembrane domain (TMD) insertase function of the EMC and the TMD dislocase activity of Spf1. Our cryo-electron microscopy structures show that the EMC insertase cavity and the Spf1 dislocase cleft are positioned in close proximity within the membrane and reveal that the ATPase cycle of Spf1 remodels the interface between the two machineries and alters cytoplasmic accessibility of both substrate-binding cavities. Together, our study provides structural insights into how membrane protein insertion and extraction machineries can be spatially coordinated at the ER membrane, suggesting that functionally distinct proteostasis factors can assemble into hubs to support membrane protein biogenesis and quality control.

papers.title: Ligand-dependent G protein dynamics underlying opioid efficacy
papers.abstract: Deutsch et al. show how μ-opioid receptor agonists exert long-range allosteric control over bound G proteins, providing an additional mechanism for encoding opioid signaling outcomes.

papers.title: μ-Opioid ligands tune G-protein opening kinetics
papers.abstract: There is a thin line between opioids acting to relieve pain and causing life-threatening adverse effects, yet the mechanistic basis separating these outcomes is not fully understood. A study suggests that the difference is encoded in the motions of the G-protein α-helical domain that gates GDP release.

papers.title: Single-cell CRISPR screen maps epigenetic regulators of lineage specification and malignancies in human HSPCs
papers.abstract: Yuan et al. establish a scalable single-cell CRISPR platform in primary human HSPCs, linking 322 regulator perturbations to cell states and gene programs. The atlas identifies regulators associated with long-term repopulation and lineage-biased outputs and nominates PRDM10 as a candidate AML dependency.

papers.title: Rapid CAR-T manufacturing with low-intensity priming enhances CAR-T cell fitness and limits inflammatory programming in a phase 1 study
papers.abstract: Yang and colleagues show that low-intensity priming during rapid chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T manufacturing preserves T cell fitness while restraining inflammatory programming. PrimeCAR cells maintain stemness-associated and proliferative responses with reduced myeloid-activating inflammation, and early-phase studies in B cell malignancies demonstrate encouraging clinical activity with few severe cytokine release syndrome (CRS) or immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) events.

papers.title: Cancer-cell-derived fumarate suppresses the anti-tumor capacity of CD8+ T cells in the tumor microenvironment
TNF compromises intestinal bile-acid tolerance dictating colitis progression and limited infliximab response
Structural basis and rational engineering of a thermophilic Cas13a for robust RNA detection
papers.abstract: Oladeji et al. determined the cryo-EM structure of the TccCas13a ternary complex and leveraged structural insights to engineer a thermophilic Cas13a variant with 100-fold enhanced sensitivity. The engineered nuclease retains programmability and thermostability, enabling highly sensitive RNA detection in different biological matrices.

papers.title: Atomic, structural and molecular insights into GPCR ligand binding and signalling
papers.abstract: This Review explores the atomic, structural and molecular basis of G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)-mediated signalling, highlighting recent insights into conformational changes associated with ligand recognition and interaction with downstream adaptors, and underscoring their importance for the development of therapeutics.

papers.title: Is this idea from AI or humans? A detector claims it can tell
In the AI era, coding means thinking like a systems architect

When microbes degrade plastic, where does it go?
Why not every global problem can be tackled by an IPCC-like organization
Decentralized AI needs more evidence on energy use
What’s the secret sauce for happy scientists at work? These eight countries offer some clues
Admire another researcher’s work? Tell them about it
Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets
papers.abstract: In this study, the authors develop a computational framework, Scellmate, that curates and analyzes large-scale microbial single-cell datasets from complex environments, and show that this helps to reveal microbial diversity and infer microbe–plasmid and microbe–phage associations in sewage.

papers.title: Soil proteogenomics uncover microbial strategies for soil depth-specific carbon cycling under whole-soil warming conditions
papers.abstract: Soils are Earth’s largest carbon reservoir, yet microbial mechanisms controlling decomposition, and their warming response, remain poorly resolved, especially in subsoils. Using genome-resolved proteogenomics within a replicated whole-soil warming experiment (0–90 cm, +4 °C, 7.5 years) we map microbial traits, their depth stratification, and warming responses. Depth is the dominant driver of microbial community and trait structure. Depth-wise, metabolism converge on low-molecular-weight and C1 compounds, challenging glucose-centric models, with surface soils enriched in methanol oxidation and deep soils in alcohol fermentation, CO oxidation and N₂ fixation. Abundant sialidases in deep soils implicate glycoproteins as a key carbon source. Warming effects are smaller and decrease over time but are depth-specific: surface soils show enhanced amino sugar and sugar alcohol transport, phosphorus mobilization, and stress tolerance, whereas mid- and deep soils exhibit stimulated C1 metabolism, CO oxidation, and altered nitrogen turnover. These depth-specific microbial trait shifts may critically influence soil carbon–climate feedbacks.

papers.title: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
papers.abstract: Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.

papers.title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
papers.abstract: Formal end-of-life care expansion in the US, Europe, and South Korea has not fully compensated for declining informal care, resulting in care gaps. Demographic transitions interact with development contexts to create distinct care landscapes.

papers.title: NiCLIP: neuroimaging contrastive language-image pretraining model for predicting text from brain activation images
papers.abstract: Researchers developed NiCLIP, an AI model that decodes cognitive tasks, concepts, and domains from brain activation patterns. Trained on over 23,000 papers, NiCLIP excels at group-level decoding, outperforming traditional decoders.

papers.title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
papers.abstract: Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode–skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

papers.title: Author Correction: Improved pharmacodynamics of epidermal growth factor via microneedles-based self-powered transcutaneous electrical stimulation
Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice
papers.abstract: Impaired adipogenesis contributes to obesity-associated metabolic disorders, in which mitochondrial dysfunction plays an important role. Emerging evidence suggests that mitochondria-localized circular RNAs (circRNAs) influence mitochondrial function; however, whether they regulate adipogenesis and systemic metabolism is unclear. By profiling circRNAs in mitochondria isolated from the white adipose tissue (WAT) of obese male mice, we observe an upregulation of Birc6 -circRNA Repressing Adipogenesis and Krebs-cycle Energy (BRAKE) in mitochondria. In vivo, adipocyte-specific circRNA BRAKE knockdown in male mice reduces body weight, restricts fat expansion, and improves insulin sensitivity. In vitro studies show that circRNA BRAKE inhibits adipogenesis. Mechanistically, circRNA BRAKE binds ATP5A and disrupts ATP synthase assembly, thereby reducing ATP production and mTORC1 signaling and suppressing adipogenesis. In omental WAT (oWAT) of patients with obesity, mitochondrial circRNA BRAKE levels are elevated and inversely correlated with mitochondrial bioenergetic function. Collectively, our data identify a mitochondria-localized circRNA that regulates energy metabolism and adipogenesis, suggesting that circRNA BRAKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases.

papers.title: Proteomic aging clocks go to trial
papers.abstract: Six proteomic aging clocks are deployed in a clinical trial for the first time, revealing more about the clocks than about the drug.

papers.title: In vivo engineering of CAR natural killer cells for immunotherapy using ligand-directed lipid nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor natural killer cells to treat autoimmune disease and cancer are generated in vivo.

papers.title: The companion website
papers.abstract: How biologists can make the most of supplementary materials for impact.

papers.title: Near-infrared photochromic miniprotein enables photoacoustic molecular imaging of acute inflammation and intracellular antigens
papers.abstract: Using near-infrared photoswitchable photochromic genetically encoded probes, differential photoacoustic tomography (PAT) enables deep-tissue imaging with high resolution and sensitivity; however, current bacteriophytochrome-based probes are bulky multidomain proteins exceeding 55 kDa, which constrains their use for designing PAT molecular reporters. Here we engineer rsmiRFPnano, a compact cyanobacteriochrome-derived photoswitchable PAT probe. With a molecular weight below 19 kDa, rsmiRFPnano efficiently incorporates biliverdin, exhibits high extinction coefficients in both photochromic states and demonstrates robust performance in live cells. We established rsmiRFPnano-based reporters for NF-κB and AP-1 pathways, which display low basal activity and strong activation-dependent responses. These reporters effectively visualized acute inflammation using noninvasive PAT in vivo, further validated through cellular-level spatial omics mapping. We then created photoswitchable nanobody probes, rsNIR-Fbs, stabilized upon antigen binding and rapidly degraded otherwise, enabling selective photoacoustic immuno-imaging of intracellular antigens in vivo. Together, these results establish rsmiRFPnano as an ultracompact and versatile platform for molecular PAT.

papers.title: A unique and equity-driven approach to immunology education in low- and middle-income countries
papers.abstract: We present a model for education that has proven transformative for faculty and students, fostering mentorship, inclusion and cross-border collaboration. By embedding training in local contexts, our framework builds confidence, skills and leadership among early-career scientists. These elements foster scientific autonomy and enable sustainable global engagement.

papers.title: Clonal heterogeneity in human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and its impact on tumor progression
papers.abstract: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma tumors to investigate tumor heterogeneity and clonal evolution, providing a valuable resource for this aggressive cancer.

papers.title: Repurposing adult AI radiograph models for neonatal care through continual learning: an international multicentre study
papers.abstract: Despite growing clinical adoption of artificial intelligence in radiology, fewer than one in five commercially available models are cleared for paediatric use. Existing systems are trained predominantly on adult data and generalize poorly to neonates, yet efficient strategies for repurposing them without data sharing or large-scale local data curation are lacking. Here we present an international retrospective study of neonatal chest radiographs from 30 neonatal intensive care units across 20 countries and territories, evaluating continual learning as a privacy-preserving approach to adapt a deep learning model for adult endotracheal tube assessment to neonatal care. Each hospital contributed 50 radiographs for sequential model retraining without centralized data pooling. Continual learning achieved lower anatomical landmark localization error (0.67 cm versus 1.29 cm for hospital-specific fine-tuning and 4.30 cm for adult-only models) at 29 of 30 sites, with improved detection of deep intubations at 27 of 30 sites. These findings demonstrate that privacy-preserving collaborative learning can address critical gaps in paediatric AI deployment.

papers.title: Interpretable AI model reveals spatial codes of cell recruitment in tissues
papers.abstract: A fully interpretable multi-instance learning framework, SPACER, helps elucidate which molecular signals recruit specific cells to their precise locations by decoding gene-level recruitment rules from spatially resolved transcriptomics data.

papers.title: Untranslated region rewiring defines a novel class of oncogene fusions
papers.abstract: Cerqua et al. identify a previously unrecognized class of oncogene fusions in which native oncogene 5′ untranslated regions (5′ UTRs) are replaced by donor-derived 5′ UTRs. This rewiring of translational control increases expression from intact protein-coding sequences and extends across multiple oncogenes.

papers.title: Macrophage-induced ferritin expression protects pancreatic cancer cells from ferroptosis
papers.abstract: Cheung et al. show that pancreatic cancer cells recruit macrophages that secrete IL-6, which promotes increased expression of the iron-binding protein ferritin in the cancer cells. As a result, the cancer cells become more resistant to ferroptosis, thereby allowing them to survive under conditions of oxidative stress.

papers.title: A systemic circadian nicotinic acid riboside (NaR) signal engages the unfolded protein response and adipogenesis via the prefoldin complex
papers.abstract: Vlassakev et al. show that circadian regulation of circulating nicotinic acid riboside (NaR), driven by the liver clock, engages the unfolded protein response (UPR) and adipogenesis. Rhythmic, but not chronic, NaR exposure regulates CEBPA expression and promotes lipid accumulation, identifying NaR as a systemic circadian signal regulating lipid metabolism.

papers.title: Quantifying the impact of genetic mutations on enhancer dynamics
papers.abstract: Genetic perturbations alter both enhancer activity and gene expression. Das et al. measure enhancer responses to genetic perturbations to identify regulatory programs and sequence grammar that remain hidden from gene expression changes alone.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of promoter silencing by transcriptional readthrough
papers.abstract: Shipman et al. propose a model of transcriptional interference to define how transcriptional readthrough leads to stable gene silencing. By dissecting the contributions of antisense transcription, H3K36me3, and DNA methylation, they describe a hierarchical silencing cascade in which transcription initiates local chromatin remodeling and DNA methylation stabilizes the repressed state.

papers.title: Cingulate thrombospondin 4 protects against neuropathic pain and comorbid anxiodepression via interaction with EAAT2
papers.abstract: Liu et al. find that nerve injury-mediated THBS4 downregulation in the ACC impairs THBS4-EAAT2 interaction in astrocytes, leading to extracellular glutamate accumulation and aberrant synaptic plasticity, ultimately exacerbates pain hypersensitivity and aversive emotions, indicating THBS4-mediated neuron-astrocyte crosstalk as a mechanism underlying the neuropathic pain and comorbid anxiodepression.

papers.title: Spatial distribution of blood-brain barrier membrane proteins is controlled by sorting motifs and physiological signals in vivo
papers.abstract: Amick et al. establish a method for measuring polarized protein sorting in brain endothelial cells in vivo. This approach is used to measure the spatial distribution of blood-brain barrier membrane proteins, identify protein-intrinsic motifs that regulate localization, and observe a spatial shift in CD31 distribution between rest and active periods.

The multi-kinase inhibitor merestinib emerged as highly synergistic with CDK12 inactivation, exacerbating DNA damage. Orally bioavailable CDK12/13 inhibitor, OKI-1546, impeded neuroblastoma tumor growth in vivo, with merestinib enhancing this anti-tumor effect.

Sleep forms flexible context representations in toddlers
papers.abstract: Sleep consolidates episodic memory through a hippocampus-dependent process in adults. Whether and how sleep supports memory consolidation during early life, when hippocampal function is immature, remains unclear. Here, we examined effects of sleep on the consolidation of spatial context, a core component of episodic memory, in toddlers aged 2–3 years. Toddlers were familiarized with two spatial contexts, followed by a ~ 90-min nap or equivalent wake period. Afterwards, using a hide-and-seek game we tested their ability to relocate toys within these contexts. Only after post-familiarization sleep, toddlers showed significant context memory and formed stronger associations between toys and specific contexts compared to wakefulness. Contextual memory was positively correlated with spindle density and slow oscillation–spindle phase-amplitude coupling during non-rapid eye movement sleep. Here, we show that, despite hippocampal immaturity, memory effects in the sleeping toddler’s brain are accompanied by thalamo-cortical oscillatory dynamics that are also implicated in adult memory consolidation.

papers.title: Sea-level contribution from Thwaites Glacier doubles in an observation-constrained ice-sheet model
papers.abstract: Thwaites Glacier is a major contributor to Antarctic mass loss and a key source of uncertainty in future sea-level rise. Ocean-driven melting at its grounding line drives rapid retreat, yet most models treat the transition between grounded and floating ice as a sharp boundary, neglecting kilometer-scale seawater intrusions that develop as the grounding line migrates and forms a grounding zone. Here, we show that actively-melting grounding zones are required to reproduce nearly three decades of observed retreat, thinning, and acceleration of Thwaites Glacier in a calibrated ice-sheet model, with successful reconstruction occurring only when grounding zones are represented as 2-5 km wide regions. Extending this model forward, we show that grounding-zone processes govern glacier’s detachment from stabilizing seafloor ridges, enabling unpinning as early as 2038 and producing up to 30 ± 6 mm of global mean sea-level rise by 2100 - approximately double previous projections even without additional climate warming.

papers.title: Whole blood transcriptomics atlas across human diseases
papers.abstract: We present a WBT Atlas, comprising 4444 WBT samples across 98 distinct health conditions, enabling systematic exploration of disease-associated transcriptomic signatures. Health condition–specific profiles are characterized across immune, metabolic, and cell-type specific features at the gene, gene module, and pathway levels. By integrating matched plasma proteomics data from 1280 participants across 28 health conditions, we further assess blood RNA–protein relationships and demonstrate their complementary biological roles. By integrating RNA and protein signatures, we develop multi-class classification models that accurately distinguish among a wide range of health conditions, with integrated models consistently outperforming those based on single-omics data alone. The identified RNA and protein signatures are validated across ten independent WBT cohorts and the UK Biobank. Together, the WBT Atlas provides a genome-wide resource that enables translational discovery in precision medicine.

Genomic bases of short-term evolution in wild barn owls revealed by long-term monitoring and population-scale sequencing
papers.abstract: Understanding how wild populations undergo rapid phenotypic evolution requires linking phenotypic change to its underlying genomic architecture over contemporary timescales. Here, we leverage a 30-year study of Swiss barn owls ( Tyto alba ) to examine long-term changes in two melanin-based traits (plumage coloration and spottiness) that have previously been linked to multiple fitness-related traits. We document a consistent temporal shift toward darker and more heavily spotted individuals and show, using whole-genome sequencing of 3,102 individuals, that these traits are controlled by a small number of loci of major effect with partially overlapping architectures. Temporal allele frequency analyses reveal subtle but consistent changes at these loci. By comparing empirical trajectories to simulations, we show that genetic drift alone is insufficient to explain the observed patterns at one major locus, indicating a role for selection. Our results demonstrate how selection acting on a small number of loci can contribute to rapid phenotypic evolution of continuous traits in the wild and highlight the value of long-term genomic and phenotypic monitoring for disentangling evolutionary processes.

papers.title: Structures and molecular mechanisms of RAD54B in modulating homologous recombination
papers.abstract: Genome stability is essential for cellular viability yet constantly threatened by DNA-damaging agents. Among these, DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are particularly harmful and in S/G2 phases are faithfully repaired through homologous recombination (HR). The RAD51 recombinase forms nucleoprotein filaments on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) that performs critical functions in HR. The efficiency of HR depends on precise regulation of RAD51 filament dynamics by accessory factors, including RAD54B, a double-strand DNA-dependent ATPase. Here, using cryogenic electron microscopy, mutagenesis, and biochemical assays, we show that RAD54B stabilizes RAD51–DNA filaments, inhibits RAD51 ATPase activity, and promotes D-loop formation and strand exchange. RAD54B contains two main RAD51-interacting sites and a β-domain that bridges RAD51 protomers, is positioned to contact donor dsDNA, and regulates RAD54B’s ATPase activity. Cellular assays reveal that the RAD51-interacting sites are required for repairing DSBs by HR in human cells. Our findings uncover a modular architecture and mechanistic framework for RAD54B’s critical role in genome maintenance.

papers.title: Hysteresis of extreme precipitation in East Asia under various CO2 removal pathways

Continuous-time noise mitigation in analogue quantum simulation
papers.abstract: Analogue quantum simulators offer a promising route to explore quantum many-body dynamics beyond classical reach in the near term. However, their vulnerability to noise limits the accuracy of simulations. Here, we establish a continuous-time framework for mitigating noise in analogue quantum simulation. Our protocol fully preserves the continuous-time nature by avoiding any active control or measurement of the system during the dynamics, while achieving exact noise cancellation. This requires a small number of ancillary qubits, whose interaction with the system, combined with classical post-processing of joint measurement data, is tailored to cancel the effect of noise. Furthermore, the protocol is Hamiltonian-independent and robust to realistic ancilla noise. This work points to a promising direction for achieving high-fidelity analogue quantum simulation in the presence of noise.

papers.title: Precision functional mapping of imagined and experienced pain
papers.abstract: Imagination is a principal human capacity, enabling simulation of sensations and situations for planning, learning, and empathy. We examined neural representations of experienced and imagined pain across eight body sites using deep-phenotyping, precision functional MRI with over seven hours of scanning per participant (N = 9). Here we show, using conventional mapping, pattern classification, and representational similarity analyses, that both imagined and experienced pain activated nociceptive regions (e.g., dorsoposterior insula) and non-nociceptive regions (e.g., premotor areas and inferior inter-effector motor cortex). However, imagined pain did not reliably reactivate body site-selective nociceptive patterns in any region. Instead, imagined and experienced pain shared multivariate representations across widespread cortical and subcortical regions, particularly transmodal cortical areas including dorsomedial and lateral prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and thalamus. These findings suggest that imagination generates distributed pain-like activity, but with separable neural codes for imagined and experienced pain. This distinction may explain the difficulty of vividly imagining pain and clarify its potential roles in empathy, planning, and pain chronification.

papers.title: DHHC12 serves as a critical nutrient-responsive switch that couples amino acid sensing to insulin secretion
IL-4 exploits TNF signaling to shape its gene expression signature in monocytes and macrophages
Deep profiling of lysine methylation by covalent enrichment-enhanced proteomics
Interpretable AI-guided discovery of degradable ionizable lipids with enhanced hepatic mRNA delivery in vivo
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) enable RNA medicines, yet ionizable-lipid discovery remains largely empirical, particularly when in vitro activity must be translated into functional hepatic delivery in vivo. Here we establish an interpretable discovery framework that combines modular degradable lipid chemistry, high-throughput phenotyping, machine learning, virtual library expansion, and independent in vivo validation to define a learnable ionizable-lipid design space. Starting from a 520-member library, we train an XGBoost model on firefly luciferase (Fluc) expression in HeLa cells and use physicochemical descriptors and molecular fingerprints to prospectively prioritize candidates with higher predicted in vitro transfection activity across a 10,920-member virtual space. In vivo phenotyping subsequently identifies PA97MD101 as a lead ionizable lipid. In mice, PA97MD101 enhances hepatic mRNA expression and Cre-dependent recombination and supports Cas9/sgTtr-mediated TTR suppression. Its performance is associated with pH-dependent membrane activity and reduced lysosomal colocalization. These findings support further evaluation of PA97MD101 for functional hepatic RNA delivery.

papers.title: Syndecan-3 couples tumor mechanics to immunosuppressive macrophage identity
The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation
papers.abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

papers.title: Block-fitness modeling of the global air mobility network
papers.abstract: Accurate representations of origin-destination (OD) passenger flows on the World Air Transportation Network (WAN) are fundamental inputs to models of global mobility, epidemic risk, and infrastructure planning. However, OD data are largely commercial and proprietary, therefore often inaccessible to the research community. Here we introduce a generative model that treats air mobility as a stochastic process within a sparse maximum-entropy framework, informed by aggregate traffic volumes of individual locations and geographic regions. The model accurately reconstructs both network structure and mobility flows, yielding epidemic spreading trajectories that closely match those obtained using real mobility data. Furthermore, the method can be effectively implemented using open data on flight routes and airport traffic, reducing dependence on proprietary datasets. Our approach provides a scalable, interpretable, and computationally efficient framework for scenario analysis and policy design in global mobility systems.

papers.title: Multiplexed single-molecule analysis of barcoded protein variants
papers.abstract: Single-molecule techniques provide exceptional resolution of biomolecular dynamics but are limited by low throughput. Here, we present a DNA barcoding strategy that enables parallel kinetic profiling of multiple protein variants in a single experiment. Each protein is covalently linked to a unique DNA barcode, decoded through transient hybridisation of fluorescent probes distinguished by colour and binding duration. Applied to a library of 16 ClpS variants, this approach revealed ~5-fold variation in dissociation kinetics and uncovered previously unrecognised bimodal binding behaviour arising from distinct structural subpopulations. By enabling scalable, multiplexed functional characterisation at the single-molecule level, this platform provides a general framework for protein engineering, directed evolution and the development of next-generation single-molecule technologies.

papers.title: The VPS33B-VPS16B protein complex facilitates Golgi ribbon formation and Golgi-endosome trafficking
Tracing missing copper: ultrapotassic rocks record isotopic evidence of crustal Cu depletion
Short Wavelength Infrared Diimmonium Nano-Agents for Photoacoustic Imaging
papers.abstract: Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) as an innovative biomedical imaging modality shows high contrast and superior spatial resolution, yet remains limited by underdeveloped second near-infrared (NIR-II, 1000-1700 nm) contrast agents, particularly neglecting the NIR-IIb (1500-1700 nm) window. In this work, we designed a new class of diimmonium (DB)-based dicationic nano-agents (DB·2X, X = TFSI - , B(C 2 O 4 ) 2 - , or BF 4 - ) for 1700 nm excitation PAI. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that dicationic DB 2+ exhibits a dramatically reduced excitation energy (1.24 eV) and enhanced oscillator strength (f = 1.11) by molecular engineering, attributed to a symmetry-allowed local excitation mechanism for electronic restructuring. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction further demonstrates the intermolecular spacings >5.0 Å in DB·2X aggregates, facilitating optimized non-radiative transitions for amplified PAI signals. In vivo study using different disease models shows that DB·2TFSI nano-agents under 1700 nm excitation can achieve higher signal-to-background ratio and minimized interference from endogenous chromophores compared to conventional 1064 nm excitation. Biocompatibility assessments confirm low cytotoxicity, underscoring potential for further development of DB·2TFSI nano-agents. This work delivers a robust molecular design paradigm for non-radiative decay optimization, and for the first time establishes 1700 nm-excitable PAI nano-agents, paving the way for tissue high-quality biomedical imaging.

papers.title: Ki-67, the chromosome periphery and de-compartmentalisation each contribute to nucleophosmin mislocalisation in acute myeloid leukaemia
papers.abstract: The mitotic chromosome periphery (MCP) is an important chromosome compartment but links to disease remains elusive. Here we define the mitosis-specific, Ki-67 interactome, identifying additional MCP components and revealing that MCP genes are commonly mutated in cancer, including nucleophosmin (NPM1). Acute myeloid leukaemia (AML)-specific NPM1 mutations (NPM1c + ), result in protein mislocalisation (nucleolus to cytoplasm). We demonstrate that NPM1c+ fails to adequately bind to the MCP, instead forming aggregates during mitosis. We also report that, de-compartmentalisation at mitotic onset allows formation of NPM1wt/c+ multimers. These mislocalisation mechanisms contribute to a significant hinderance of NPM1 re-entry into daughter cell nucleoli. Enhancing MCP loading capacity via Ki-67 overexpression resulted in increased MCP-bound NPM1c+ during mitosis and greater yield of nucleolar NPM1c + . Ki-67 expression demonstrated a significant interaction with NPM1 mutation status on AML patient overall survival, whereby higher Ki-67 was associated with increased hazard in NPM1wt but reduced hazard in NPM1c+ patients. This work reveals mechanistic insight into AML and evidence that the MCP has untapped therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Anomalous spin–lattice coupling in a 2D antiferromagnetic semiconductor revealed by surface acoustic Rayleigh waves
papers.abstract: Magnetic order in van der Waals magnets can strongly influence their lattice dynamics, yet how it affects local and macroscopic manifestations of spin-phonon coupling remains unclear. Optical phonons probe bond-scale exchange modulation and short-range spin correlations, whereas long-wavelength acoustic modes couple to uniform strain fields and are sensitive to renormalization of the macroscopic elastic tensor associated with long-range magnetic order. Experimentally accessing these acoustic excitations in low-dimensional crystals is challenging due to their low energies and the small lateral dimensions of exfoliated samples. Here, we employ Brillouin–Mandelstam scattering spectroscopy to investigate surface acoustic phonons in exfoliated NiPS 3 thin films across the antiferromagnetic transition. Our results show a single Rayleigh surface mode whose phase velocity decreases significantly across the Néel temperature. This anomaly reflects a strong magnetoelastic renormalization of the elastic constants triggered by the onset of antiferromagnetic order. First-principles calculations, combined with continuum finite-element modeling reproduce the Rayleigh-wave dispersion and its magnetic-order–induced shift. The results reveal how microscopic exchange interactions govern the macroscopic elastic response of two-dimensional antiferromagnetic semiconductors, enabling magnetically tunable phononic, magnonic, and strain-mediated spintronic devices.

papers.title: Ultrahigh-speed chromatically band-limited illumination profilometry
papers.abstract: Single-shot fringe projection profilometry (SS-FPP) has been extensively applied to the study of rapid three-dimensional (3D) dynamics in physics, engineering, and biology. Despite these advancements, the imaging capability of time-resolved SS-FPP is still limited by the flexibility and speed of both pattern projection and image acquisition, as well as by the duration of the observation time window. Here, we overcome these constraints by developing chromatically band-limited illumination profilometry (C-BLIP). On the illumination side, C-BLIP projects programmable grayscale fringes at ultrahigh speed by synergizing a digital micromirror device with a user-selectable encoding region of interest and a custom-designed projection lens for chromatically band-limited illumination with incoherent light sources. On the detection side, C-BLIP acquires spatially multiplexed color fringe images, followed by 3D image reconstruction. Using C-BLIP, we demonstrated color 3D imaging of a turbofan blade-projectile collision at 25 thousand frames per second (kfps), as well as intensity 3D imaging of maple samara’s fall aerodynamics at 75 kfps and ultrasound encryption/recovery at 150 kfps. These results highlight C-BLIP’s promise for continuous-streaming, ultrahigh-speed 3D metrology in industrial inspection, bionics, and data security.

papers.title: C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of isoleucyl-tRNA synthetases is a prokaryote-specific strategy for tuning aminoacylation rate
papers.abstract: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases are the guardians of translational fidelity. Their complex function is mirrored by an elaborate structure, which includes multiple nested domains. While the evolutionary pressures that promoted the emergence of some domains, such as the editing domain, are clear, the pressures acting on other domains, particularly those at the C-terminus, are not. Here, we combine kinetic analysis, X-ray crystallography, and bioinformatics to unveil the history and evolutionary forces that have shaped isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase (IleRS) domain structure. We find that the traditional classification of IleRSs based on the C-terminal tRNA-recognition domains is incomplete, as it fails to capture features of the synthetic domain. Guided by a crystal structure of the Priestia megaterium IleRS2:tRNA Ile complex, we removed key interactions between IleRS2 and its cognate tRNA and characterised their impact on enzyme activity. We found that D-loop interactions with the IleRS2 C-terminal domains are non-essential in prokaryotes, and their loss can even increase catalytic turnover. Further, we show that the zinc-binding domain of IleRS1 recognises the anticodon less stringently than the canonical C-terminal domain of IleRS2. Our data suggest that C-terminal evolutionary remodelling of IleRSs is an ongoing process with a historical precedent and is consistent with selection for faster aminoacylation rate.

Discrete subdomains establish epigenetic diversity in subtelomeric heterochromatin in fission yeast
papers.abstract: Subtelomeres are imperfect repeats adjacent to telomeres that are transcriptionally repressed by heterochromatin. Although essential for genome integrity, their repetitive nature has thwarted dissection of local heterochromatin assembly and maintenance mechanisms. By engineering fission yeast strains carrying fluorescent reporters at a single subtelomere, we uncovered distinct subdomains. These subdomains have different silencing requirements: telomere-proximal regions rely on canonical shelterin- or RNAi-dependent nucleation pathways, whereas telomere-distal regions involve nucleosome remodelers, histone chaperones, and boundary-associated factors. Subdomains also exhibit discrete epigenetic states emerging both at homologous loci on different chromosome arms and along the same subtelomeric sequence. We document these epigenetic states using multi-generational live imaging and targeted perturbations. These analyses show that subtelomeric subdomains display position-specific, clonally variable silencing across a spectrum from robust to fragile epigenetic states. Interestingly, structural variants, common in subtelomeric sequences across eukaryotes, dictate local epigenetic stability. These findings reveal that subtelomeres, long recognized for their sequence variability, form a dynamic mosaic of coexisting epigenetic domains. This implies a wide range of gene-repressive regulatory logic at the chromosome ends, from environmental responsiveness to silencing stability.

EpCAM-associated ERM-actin remodeling couples altered membrane mechanics with nuclear deformation and confined migration, providing a mechanical framework for understanding EpCAM-associated gastric cancer progression.

papers.title: Subpopulation networks: a scaling principle for engineering living systems
papers.abstract: Cell populations underpin applications ranging from bioproduction and biotherapeutics to microbiome engineering and biocomputing. However, treating them as bulk quantities rather than as structured systems limits our understanding of population-level stability, productivity, and robustness. Cellular populations self-organize into coexisting subpopulations (SPs) representing phenotypically distinct states that emerge from the interplay of biological noise and selective pressures. We propose that networks of interacting SPs constitute a fundamental organizational layer for engineering stable cell population dynamics. Surveying published single-cell studies across bacterial, yeast, and mammalian systems, we show that populations consistently self-organize into a limited number of SPs. This dimensional reduction can be captured experimentally by clustering single-cell data and gives rise to scaling laws that link population structure to collective performance.

papers.title: Inhomogeneity of negative enthalpy enables excellent mechanical properties in nanosized single crystals of multi-principal element alloys
papers.abstract: Many nanosized metals with limited dislocation nucleation and multiplication usually exhibit poor plasticity. Previous studies have demonstrated that multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) can achieve a combination of strength and plasticity. However, whether these mechanical properties extend to their nanosized counterparts and how nanosized MPEAs accommodate plastic deformation remains unknown. Using a homemade in-situ device, we captured the atomic-scale tensile process and measured the stress-strain curve of Fe 48 Mn 32 Co 10 Cr 10 nanosized single crystals (NSCs). We find that NSCs achieve a strength of ~3 GPa and a uniform elongation of ~20%. We show that this combination arises from the inhomogeneous distribution of enthalpy, which produces a broad spectrum of energy barriers for the nucleation of full dislocations, partial dislocations, and nanotwins. Consequently, dislocations and nanotwins are randomly generated throughout MPEA NSCs, effectively suppressing local stress concentration and leading to both high strength and large uniform elongation.

papers.title: PUS7 pseudouridylation of 7SK orchestrates human somatic cell reprogramming into iPS cells
papers.abstract: Reprogramming human somatic cells into induced pluripotent stem cells (iPS cells) provides huge potential for regenerative medicine but its molecular regulation remains incompletely understood. In this study, we identify PUS7 as an RNA modification checkpoint that promotes acquisition of pluripotency. PUS7 loss markedly impairs reprogramming, whereas its overexpression accelerates reprogramming efficiency and kinetics. Mechanistically, PUS7 pseudouridylates U250 of the chromatin-associated noncoding RNA 7SK, enhancing its interaction with the BRG/BRM-associated factor (BAF) complex. Loss of this modification disrupts 7SK–BAF association, reduces BAF chromatin occupancy and decreases global chromatin accessibility. We further establish PSKM (PUS7, SOX2, KLF4, MYC) reprogramming, which generates iPS cells with faithful imprinting, robust lineage potential and improved developmental fidelity. PSKM-iPS cells differentiate efficiently toward neural and hematopoietic lineages and undergo gastrulation-like morphogenesis. These findings link 7SK pseudouridylation to chromatin remodeling and establish PSKM as a framework for generating high-quality human iPS cells for modeling and regenerative medicine.

papers.title: Skin-resident CXCR6+ memory CD4+ T cells and dendritic cells form dermal perivascular hubs that drive relapse in allergic dermatitis
papers.abstract: Tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells are heterogeneous, but how pathogenic subsets drive relapse in allergic dermatitis remains unclear. Asahina et al. identify a pathogenic CXCR6+ CD4+ TRM subset sustained through CXCL16-dependent clustering with CD301b+ cDC2s, revealing the TRM-DC niche as a potential therapeutic target for allergic dermatitis.
